title: Release 0.0.22 with integrated chart, guide, data and scene fixes
body:
## Change

Consolidate the chart/guide/data fixes and independent axis/editor/scene work for ggaction 0.0.22. The merged implementation retains named-axis ownership, compatible facet and legend policies, row-preserving data operations, explicit mark clips, polygon point shapes, missing-line gaps, linear domain/tick policies and native Canvas transition scenes. Conflicting merge implementations are resolved with both sets of regression controls retained.

The exact Hono dependency PR #252 is integrated; compatible Vite/ip-address patches remove the current audit findings. Public declarations, current contracts, generated authoring references, examples and release documentation are synchronized. Unsupported appearance nice-count and non-Cartesian dash-fallback type leakage is corrected without broadening the runtime.

## Validation

- 5,499 normal tests pass; source coverage remains enforced.
- The 830-chart Cartesian and 540-chart statistical schedules, direct encodings, 132-leaf palette ledger and all hierarchical facade requirements pass with actual pinned data and unchanged five-call/three-dataset floors.
- 125 documentation source tests, 150 built pages and the complete 320/390/768px browser keyboard/search/accessibility harness pass.
- The exact 621-entry installed package consumer passes; the measured artifact is 894,922 packed / 4,254,609 unpacked bytes locally.
- Native clipping/scene controls use exact decoded primitive/public pixels. The existing Polar trend raster tolerances are retained; its Linux bounds follow the approved outward-guide clearance change.
- The separate 1,336-family / 9,766-program dataset preflight retains all source/code/data. 1,334 frozen SVGs are byte-identical; two endpoint-rounding changes have exact decoded RGBA identity at DPR1/2/4, with explicit archive/source-bound qualifications. Public synchronization still requires the tagged canonical artifact replay.

## Closeout

[Issue/branch audit](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e934906032f624edd55697409651e3db496053a4/agent_docs/impl/release-1336/CLOSEOUT.md) records 35 implemented issues to close after verified public publication. #238, #244, #253 and #258 remain open because their public capabilities are unfinished. Historical remote heads are archived before removal when they are not main ancestors; local worktrees are preserved. Translation is stopped at the explicitly requested 1,336-family cutoff.

title: Support explicit simple polygon point shapes across marks, scales and guides
body:
## Required capability

Source family 1735 renders normally: 406 unchanged car records, an original year filter and valid-position eligibility yield 29 points. Its three category shapes are simple custom polygons: a square, a plus, and a non-equilateral triangle. Existing named shapes do not preserve all three original geometries. This source is unadmitted/untranslated, with zero School calls.

Extend existing PointShape with `{ polygon: [{x,y}, ...] }`, reused by constant create/edit, explicit shape scale ranges and unknown values, legends, highlights and persistence. No new action or graphics primitive is needed. Keep all 14 named shapes and automatic range order.

Bounded contract:

- 3–1,024 finite vertices, coordinate magnitudes ≤1,000,000; canonicalize an optional repeated closing vertex.
- Simple concave polygons and either winding; reject zero-length/backtracking edges, self-crossing/overlapping/touching nonadjacent edges, zero/nonfinite area and unknown keys.
- Preserve origin (0,0) as mark anchor; scale by `sqrt(requestedArea/rawArea)` and reuse clockwise angle handling, without recentering.
- Existing radius/size APIs retain meaning. Renderers receive existing concrete closed paths.
- No arbitrary SVG strings, curves or holes in this extension.

Acceptance: independent geometry/area/extent oracles; immutable input and atomic rejection; constructor/editor/range/unknown parity; legends/highlights/Canvas/scale/data replay; editable persistence; SVG/PNG/PDF, strict types, synchronized docs and package checks. Qualify exact source/native evidence before School authoring or counting the chart.

Standing user approval applies. Original vectors are checked numerically without image/VLM inspection. Keep the installed translation runtime pinned until candidate validation. Publish at the next 1,350-family milestone.

title: Support opt-in facet headers anchored to concrete mark content
body:
## Problem
Panel headers currently follow one plot/Canvas edge even when mark geometry extends beyond a particular plot. A circle at the top edge can therefore approach the header more closely than an identical circle inside another panel. One common offset cannot represent different per-panel mark extents.

## Minimal public reproduction
```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 100, height: 100 }, margin: 70 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { group: "A", x: 5, y: 5 },
    { group: "B", x: 10, y: 10 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: { field: "x", scale: { domain: [0, 10] } },
    y: { field: "y", scale: { domain: [0, 10] } },
    guides: false
  })
  .editPointMark({ stroke: false })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 3 })
  .facet({ field: "group", columns: 2, spacing: "plot" })
  .editCompositionLayout({ topLane: "shared" });
```
Expected opt-in behavior: the second header moves outward by 3px; the first remains fixed. Existing default output remains unchanged.

## Approved implementation scope
Extend existing header creation/editing with `anchor: "plot" | "content"`. Content requires plot spacing and uses the union of the plot rectangle and concrete semantic mark geometry, respecting strokes, translations, collections and clips. Opacity retains geometric layout stability. Along-edge alignment stays on the plot span. Axes, grids, legends, titles and extension-only graphics do not affect the anchor. Row/column overrides, rotated headers, layout/source/theme/metrics replay and editable persistence retain this intent. Field titles retain their plot anchor. Insufficient space rejects atomically.

The human has explicitly approved current and future in-scope questions for this translation/library task. Implementation remains on the local batch branch; public release is deferred to the next 200-chart checkpoint. This is distinct from the independent full-bounds wrapped-layout request in #258.

title: Support per-axis tick-step numeric label precision
body:
## Problem

A single high-level faceted chart can resolve independent numeric scales with different tick steps. Existing fixed numeric format strings apply the same decimal precision to every child; `auto` removes trailing zeroes. A per-value label map cannot distinguish zero on an integer panel from zero on a fractional panel.

Original0581 has independent Y scales with ten ticks each: −0.15…0.30 by0.05 needs two decimals (including0.00), while0…900 by100 needs integer labels (including0). Existing public fold/computed/facet actions reproduce all223 unchanged CSV rows,426 defined line vertices, two450×300 plots at relativeY0/352 and497×753 outer dimensions. Exactly replayed source SVG SHA256: `f56774156c13aeb905720c36e03d9632605c6761f9b67187d169ad80a993e0a2`.

The original also retains ten malformed year strings and does not paint their line points. Existing public parseTime produces null aliases and line missing:'break' preserves this behavior without rewriting raw rows. An empty original change string numerically becomes zero; a public conditional numeric alias preserves the original empty string.

## Proposed capability

Add explicit axis-only `format:'ticks'`, retaining existing omitted/auto output. Resolve a numeric fixed precision separately from each axis's actual settled tick values, using its smallest positive step with stable floating-point normalization. Keep trailing zeroes at that precision and use the mathematical minus symbol. Numeric data, domains and tick positions do not change. Time/discrete axes reject this numeric format; existing explicit display-label maps keep precedence. Named axes, facade creation, focused edits, scale/data/Canvas replay, facets and persistence must retain and recompute the intent. Reject unsupported precision or ambiguous empty context rather than silently falling back.

This is a library requirement, not an acceptance waiver. No School calls or admission have occurred. Local unpaid evidence is in `tmp/total1500-0581-actual-original-source-capture-v2/` and `tmp/total1500-0581-private-native-capability-v5/`. Add focused pure/public/rematerialization/type/package checks and synchronized documentation before adoption; keep public publication at the next regular200-family checkpoint.

title: Support opt-in gaps for missing coordinates in direct Cartesian line marks
body:
## Problem

Direct Cartesian line marks reject missing numeric coordinates and cannot preserve an intentional gap between otherwise valid observations. A translation must not replace a missing observation with zero, impute a value, filter it away and bridge the line, or alter the original input rows.

Reproduced on unreleased local candidate `c7cbee6f9d703b7f81b75894e1c2c90938353d5a`. This is not a claim about a newly published npm release. Existing area marks already expose an opt-in `missing: "error" | "break"`; direct line marks do not.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 350 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { date: "2025-09-01", value: 4.4 },
    { date: "2025-10-01", value: null },
    { date: "2025-11-01", value: 4.6 }
  ] })
  .createLineMark({})
  .encodeX({ field: "date", fieldType: "temporal" })
  .encodeY({ field: "value" });
```

The final action throws `Field "value" must contain a finite number at row 1.` The existing strict default should remain; an explicit gap policy is needed.

## Real original-source witness

Vega-Lite family `vl_0549`, original specification SHA-256 `e3d484ec677b8fe43c067507ce5d96094e6936f30a3355bc37b92497fdddb847`:

- Two independently owned API tables: UK `raw.years` with 55 raw rows and US `raw.observations` with 945 raw rows. Preserve all 1,000 rows, keys, string values, metadata and order.
- The original US row at zero-based index 933 has `date: "2025-10-01", value: "."`.
- Vega-Lite retains this row and produces `defined: false`, breaking the blue US line. There are 944 valid US line observations, not a new observation at zero.
- A public computed conditional can keep the raw `"."` and derive a separate numeric column containing `null` at this row. The subsequent direct `encodeY` still rejects it: `Field "sourceValue" must contain a finite number at row 933.`
- This failure is independently reproduced using a focused `createLineMark` + positional encoders, avoiding the separate repeated-facade explicit-ID requirement. The gap limitation is therefore not an artifact of an ambiguous facade ID.
- The original shared frame is 481×362 with a 450×300 plot; original X domain is 1948-01-01 through 2026-09-01. No chart-size change, interpolation change or data substitution is an acceptable repair.

This family remains unadmitted and uncounted, with **zero translation-model requests**. No original or accepted historical chart module was modified.

## Proposed public direction

Extend the existing line options with opt-in `missing: "error" | "break"` on `createLineMark`, `editLineMark`, and the existing `createLinePlot.line` options. Preserve `"error"` as the default. This follows the existing area vocabulary and adds no rendering primitive or new action.

In explicit break mode:

1. Preserve original rows and source indices. Numeric strings still need an explicit computed numeric alias; do not add implicit coercion.
2. Treat absent/null position values as gap boundaries, with precise validation matching the existing missing-data conventions. Keep invalid nonmissing types as errors.
3. Split each logically ordered series into contiguous valid runs. Start a new subpath after a gap; never connect across it or fabricate vertices.
4. Apply the configured interpolation independently to each run. Define leading, trailing, consecutive and singleton-run behavior without invented observations.
5. Define domain inference explicitly: an otherwise valid X observation must not silently disappear from its axis domain solely because Y is missing. Empty usable dimensions must still fail clearly.
6. Keep aggregate, categorical, path-order, group/appearance and polar behavior explicit; avoid silently broadening unrelated modes during a direct Cartesian implementation.

## Acceptance evidence

- Strict-default rejection remains unchanged; an explicit break succeeds for supported direct Cartesian lines.
- Two separated multi-point runs produce two `M` subpaths and no bridge segment; leading/trailing/consecutive gaps and singleton runs do not invent data.
- Numeric and temporal positions, grouping and supported curve interpolation preserve original order and gap ownership.
- The real `vl_0549` row remains `"."` in the raw input and `null` only in its derived column. Both original API tables remain independent.
- SVG, PNG, PDF, semantic/graphic outputs, selections and saved program roundtrips retain the same gaps and source lineage.
- Public declarations, API cards and documentation describe the option and its supported scope. Existing no-gap charts and existing strict errors retain their output and behavior.

Implementation and package validation should enter the next regular 200-family release checkpoint, with all affected translations reverified against that candidate. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or publication.

title: Support independently packed wrapped facet bounds and shared footer axes
body:
## Problem

A wrapped facet can have a bounds-driven flow that does not align every plot in a logical row. The current facet materializer uses one shared Y origin per row. A single `gap` cannot reproduce a source whose second-row plot origins differ between columns while all inner plots retain the same dimensions.

This blocks source family **0944**. It is not admitted, translated or counted as complete. No model calls or chart-image inspection have been used for this diagnosis.

## Reproduced original geometry

The original static view has 72 unchanged CSV rows, four Country groups, 140 × 140 inner plots and a 406 × 445 outer canvas. The compiled layout is `padding:20, bounds:"full", align:"none", columns:2`.

Origins relative to the first plot:

| Panel | X | Y |
|---|---:|---:|
| England | 0 | 0 |
| Northern Ireland | 208 | 0 |
| Scotland | 0 | 192 |
| Wales | 208 | 187 |

Panel titles sit at the same title baseline, but the second-row plots are displaced by 5px because the layout packs full group bounds. The two shared X footer axes are independently positioned beneath the complete wrapped view. Date labels rotate by 60 degrees. An exact implementation must retain these owners and must not add one X axis per panel.

Original specification SHA-256: `b4ab0dcf7ee89027f5c80d5b76faf1681f97f75d814a9d19452593e9137c7a0d`.

## Current library behavior

Against local candidate `c7cbee6f9d703b7f81b75894e1c2c90938353d5a`, actual high-level `createLinePlot → facet → editFacetScales({y:"independent"}) → editCompositionLayout({columns:2,gap,spacing:"plot"})` probes with gaps 52, 68 and 80 all produce equal Y origins for Scotland and Wales. This is an invariant of the current row-track layout. Setting a different scalar gap cannot satisfy both reference origins.

The diagnostic uses actual materialized child placement and plot bounds, not renderer pixels or coordinates inferred from text widths. A smaller gap of20 correctly rejects insufficient header space; that validation must stay intact.

## Required capability and acceptance criteria

- An explicit source-neutral facet flow/alignment contract for independently packed full child bounds, retaining the existing aligned-grid default.
- Preserve the high-level facet, raw partitions, group order, independent scale ownership, plot dimensions, parent title, panel titles and shared footer axes.
- Keep ordinal group order distinct from a naive Y-then-X sort: here Wales' plot is 5px above Scotland even though Scotland is the third logical cell.
- No generic absolute graphic primitives or per-mark manual placements in ordinary authoring.
- Immutable edits, persistence/replay, SVG/PNG/PDF and existing grid behavior require focused regressions. Layout gaps must continue to reject real header collisions.
- Do not mark0944 complete until actual model-authored variants pass source/native numeric structure, data, guide and text checks and same-family output checks.

This issue is an implementation requirement, not a fidelity waiver. Related source-only pipeline work must separately qualify encoding-level facet intent, cell-owned header text, exact60-degree browser transforms and the source's trailing empty subtitle line. Existing completed source adapters remain frozen.

title: Fix legacy editable lookup schema migration validation order
body:
## Reproduction

An editable schema-version-1 snapshot may omit dataset schemas. The documented reader infers/derives missing schemas before final schema validation. A lookup snapshot with two valid raw tables and exact derived rows currently fails with `Lookup dataset "reference" requires schema.` before migration can run.

The cause is the initial `restoreState` validation calling lookup schema derivation unconditionally. Its schema context requires the reference schema that migration is about to infer. Full critical coverage also exposes the unreachable lookup-input schema resolver in `migrateStateSchemas`.

## Fix contract

Keep the existing two-pass import boundary. During the version-1 prepass only, defer lookup schema equality when one of its required schemas is absent. Continue to validate envelope/trace/stack/IDs/references/cycles, raw lookup key uniqueness, typed matching and exact derived row values. Then infer/derive schemas through both input datasets and perform the complete unchanged strict validation. Present malformed or incompatible schemas must remain rejected. Modern editable formats and normal serialization stay strict.

No new public API, persisted format, source-data changes or rendering changes are required. Regressions cover mixed string/number keys, leading-zero copied strings, missing matches, raw row order, both input schemas, editable roundtrip, and tampered values/unknown or cyclic references/duplicate keys/wrong schemas. Keep the 100% critical function-coverage floor.

This is a development-candidate fix; public release remains at the next coordinated 200-family checkpoint.

title: Support nearest-step automatic linear axis ticks
body:
## Problem

Automatic linear axis ticks currently select the next larger step from the existing factor set. For domain `[0, 140]` and `count: 5`, this yields `[0, 30, 60, 90, 120]`. A nearest-step density policy instead needs `[0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140]`.

This matters for independently scaled facets. A six-panel example has domains `[0,140]`, `[0,110]`, `[0,180]`, `[0,110]`, `[0,140]`, `[0,120]`; its target tick steps are `20,20,50,20,20,20`. There is no uniform existing count from 1 through the 10,000-item limit that reproduces all six panels. Explicit tick arrays work for one unit chart but cannot express this automatic policy in a single canonical facet source. Facet children intentionally cannot be replaced independently.

## Proposed opt-in contract

Extend Cartesian axis tick selection with `rounding: "nearest" | "ceiling"` through complete axes, grouped ticks-and-labels, and focused tick/label actions. Omission preserves existing behavior and output. `"nearest"` chooses 1/2/5/10 decade steps at geometric midpoints; `"ceiling"` restores the current policy. `count` remains an approximate density, not an exact number of ticks.

```js
program.createYAxis({
  title: false,
  ticksAndLabels: { count: 5, rounding: "nearest" }
});
```

The policy applies only to automatic count-mode linear Cartesian axes. Explicit `values`, temporal/transformed/discrete axes and Polar/Parallel axes must not silently accept it. Inferred grids must reuse their axis owner's policy. Tick/label edits, named axes, facet replay, scale/data/Canvas updates, Basic/Full, persistence and package types need matching coverage.

## Verification and release

Prepare an explicit primitive/public target before implementing the option. Preserve existing defaults and numerical tolerances; verify literal tick values, geometry, malformed input atomicity, immutable replay, decoded PNG, browser/package consumers and documentation. The in-scope design is covered by the user's standing approval. This issue is independent of count-based domain rounding in #255. Development candidates remain unreleased until the next coordinated 200-family checkpoint.

title: Support count-based automatic linear scale domains
body:
## Need

Independent linear scales currently offer only boolean `nice`. The existing upward-rounding policy is useful and should remain unchanged, but it cannot express an automatic range based on a chosen tick density.

For example, this is valid today:

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 200, height: 120 } })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 1, y: 108 }] })
  .createLinePlot({
    x: "x",
    y: { field: "y", scale: { zero: true, nice: true } },
    guides: false
  });
```

Its automatic Y domain is `[0,120]`. A count-based policy with density 10 should support `[0,110]`. When several facets need different automatic domains, one shared explicit domain cannot express the intended design. Changing only the tick labels would leave the data geometry wrong.

## Concrete proposed API

Extend the existing option with `nice: { count: 10 }`, without a new action:

```js
.createLinePlot({
  x: "x",
  y: { field: "y", scale: { zero: true, nice: { count: 10 } } },
  guides: false
})
.facet({ field: "group", scales: { y: "independent" } })
```

The count controls domain rounding density; it does not force the number of guide ticks. Keep omitted/false/true output unchanged. Require a positive safe-integer count and an exact one-key object. Restrict the object to supported linear position scales; reject it for other scale roles/types. Explicit domains retain precedence. Reuse the same immutable stored scale decision through focused/generic edits, data revisions, shared consumers, facets and persistence.

For representative input maxima `133,108,171,107,139,116` and zero-based domains, preserve legacy boolean maxima `150,120,200,120,150,120`, and support count-10 maxima `140,110,180,110,140,120`.

## Review and verification

The implementation review package is `agent_docs/impl/linear-nice-count/PROPOSAL.md`. Its executable concrete target and an existing explicit-domain control have identical graphics, SVG and same-run decoded PNG pixels; the new public option is not implemented yet.

Required evidence includes independent numeric expectations and finite-range containment, atomic validation, unchanged boolean behavior, explicit/constant domains, type changes, scale edits, shared/rematerialized consumers, independent facets, persistence, package/type consumers, and synchronized contracts/docs/generated references/examples. Keep public publication at the next authorized batch checkpoint.

title: Support field titles across facet headers
body:
A facet composition cannot currently retain a global chart title and independently declare the field title outside the complete facet span. `editFacetHeaders({role:"column", title:{text:"Region"}})` rejects with `Unknown editFacetHeaders option "title".` Category headers and a field title have different ownership and cardinality.

The approved concrete design extends existing role-specific header options with an optional field-title object and `false` removal, rather than adding an action, fake data/axis, or renderer primitive. One title per role aligns to the union of occupied plots. Existing title-free output remains unchanged. Rotation, immutable editing, layout reservation, collisions, source/theme/metrics replay and editable persistence require shared validation.

[Design, approval evidence and executable primitive target](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8dd5cc94/agent_docs/impl/facet-field-titles/PROPOSAL.md). The reproducible primitive is 215×195 with its left title centered at (10,92.5). Implement and verify in the local batch candidate; keep this issue open until the next authorized 200-chart public release.

title: Support row-preserving null calendar buckets in createTimeUnitData
body:
## Problem

`createTimeUnitData` rejects a nullable field even when preserving the input row with a null derived calendar bucket is the intended design. This complicates faithful, row-preserving translations of charts containing missing dates.

Observed with the unreleased candidate `f507da9795004bc7142a998f0ef0880ac9c00040` while translating original Vega-Lite source `vl_1558` (source SHA-256 `cd4928195c37e9b9f71d52e4bbd2a103f4fe8f1f1d6465f6a4d42e96fd15f76a`). The two unmodified source tables contain 40,534 terms and 11,864 people. After keyed lookup and calendar-year extraction, 1,238 missing birthdays become null derived years; the remaining 39,296 numeric years are valid. All original raw strings and rows must remain intact.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

chart()
  .createData({ values: [{ birthYear: 1745 }, { birthYear: null }] })
  .createTimeUnitData({
    id: 'buckets',
    field: 'birthYear',
    unit: 'year',
    temporalUnit: 'timestamp'
  });
```

The second row throws `Field "birthYear" must contain a temporal string or finite timestamp ...`. Omitting `temporalUnit` also rejects the null row. This is separate from #72's finite timestamp range issue and #167's computed calendar-year extraction support.

## Suggested extension

Consider an explicit missing-value policy for `createTimeUnitData` and `editTimeUnitData`, such as `missing: 'error' | 'null'`, retaining the current strict behavior by default.

With the opt-in null policy:

- Preserve every original row, field, raw cell, and row order.
- Map null or an absent optional input field to a null output bucket; preserve the input field as supplied.
- Retain errors for malformed non-null values, unsupported units/zones, out-of-range dates, and invalid finite/nonfinite inputs. Do not catch all validation failures as missing values.
- Give the derived field the correct nullable number/string schema for calendar buckets/weekday and retain input lineage.
- Keep creation, editing, persistence, dependency invalidation, Full/Basic entry points, and downstream null/unknown handling consistent.

Tests should cover creation and edits, mixed valid/null/optional rows, nullable schema/lineage and row order, an all-null input, rejected malformed values, and unchanged default behavior for existing consumers.

## Current translation status

This does **not** block `vl_1558`: existing `createComputedData` operations reproduce the exact frozen source calculation and singleton year-bucket result while retaining null rows. A real original-browser replay and an independent native probe verify all 40,534 point positions/paints. The proposed high-level calendar support would simplify this workflow and make it reusable without source-specific lowering. No public API change or release was made for this issue; the dataset uses the current verified local candidate and releases remain on the approved 200-family cadence.

body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.7 to 4.13.13.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.13

Mount Middleware

app.mount() is now available as the Mount Middleware, hono/mount. It is just a handler, so you register it with app.all():

import { Router as IttyRouter } from 'itty-router'
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const ittyRouter = IttyRouter()

ittyRouter.get('/hello', () => new Response('Hello from itty-router'))


const app = new Hono()

app.all('/itty-router/*', mount(ittyRouter.handle))

app.mount() still works in v4 but is deprecated and will be removed in v5. Migrating is a one-line change:

- app.mount('/itty-router', ittyRouter.handle)
+ app.all('/itty-router/*', mount(ittyRouter.handle))

title: Support grain-preserving lookup between named datasets
body:
## Problem

A chart needs to copy `age` and `height` from one named table into another by matching `person` to `name`, then plot mean age by group. The current API has no dataset lookup action. Prejoining the inputs or hardcoding a conditional age map would lose the original two-table dependency.

On candidate `b924cba9842ddcd625e22835bc8ad76624530454`, `typeof chart().createLookupData` is `undefined`.

## Minimal requested flow

```js
chart()
  .createData({ id: "people", values: people })
  .createData({ id: "groups", values: groups })
  .createLookupData({
    id: "ages",
    field: "person",
    lookup: { data: "people", key: "name", fields: ["age", "height"] }
  });
```

The source case has nine rows in each original table. Its nine output rows must keep the left table's order and values, with group means `32`, `86/3`, and `56`. It is held before translation admission, with zero model calls.

## Approved implementation scope

- Add grain-preserving `createLookupData` and the corresponding derived editor using existing data and materialization layers.
- Resolve the lookup table explicitly; infer only the existing primary current-data context.
- Preserve typed keys and values. Missing matches produce nulls; duplicate non-null right keys reject. Support explicit aliases through the existing `fields/as` convention; reject output collisions.
- Store both input references and schema lineage. Revisions of either input must recompute downstream charts in stable dependency order, including diamonds; detect cycles and preserve atomic failure.
- Include live-reference cleanup, editable persistence, Full/Basic boundaries, facet/grid/repeat replay, declarations, current contracts, generated docs and a runnable example.
- Verify independent joined rows, numeric means, concrete output and renderer pixels. Retain all existing limits and default output.

Concrete design and executable current-capability reproduction: [lookup proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7c1903a9/agent_docs/impl/lookup-data/PROPOSAL.md), [reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7c1903a9/agent_docs/impl/lookup-data/reproduce.mjs).

The user has explicitly approved future design questions in this ongoing task. Implementation and local candidate verification continue without another approval request. Keep this issue open until the coordinated 200-additional-chart public release is actually verified; the next checkpoint is 1,413 completed source families. Current completed count is 1,297.

title: Support explicit rotation for facet header text
body:
## Problem

Facet headers cannot display rotated text. Placing a header on the left or right keeps it horizontal, and `editFacetHeaders({ role: "column", rotation: { value: -90, unit: "degrees" } })` currently throws `Unknown editFacetHeaders option "rotation".`

A source chart in the translation corpus has five 300×40 panels with 215 line vertices per panel. Its panel names sit vertically on the left. The original SVG, text styles, CTMs, glyph bounds, and panel placement were captured automatically, and fresh original SVG/PNG output reproduces byte for byte. Translation has not been sent to the model while this required capability is missing.

## Current reproduction

After creating a complete faceted program:

```js
program.editFacetHeaders({
  role: "column",
  side: "left",
  rotation: { value: -90, unit: "degrees" }
});
```

The same program without `rotation` renders. Adding it is rejected as an unknown option. `side` alone does not rotate the text.

## Proposed change

Extend existing facet header options with `rotation?: RotationInput`, using the existing radians/structured-degrees vocabulary. Support the same setting at header creation and editing, including common and row/column styles. Keep the intent in the existing header config and use the existing concrete text rotation property.

Reserve space and validate collisions using the rotated text bounds. Offset measures outward clearance from the selected plot edge to the rotated text block; alignment places that block along the edge. Preserve existing output when rotation is omitted, support zero to clear a previous rotation, and reject invalid values atomically. No new action, source-data changes, renderer API, relaxed tolerance, or global overflow exemption.

Concrete design and verification plan: [facet header rotation proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e535cda7771392121129dbb61ea3f946210035f7/agent_docs/impl/facet-header-rotation/PROPOSAL.md).

## Validation and release

Use independent numeric bounds, a representative public/primitive exact render pair, initial/edit and persistence equivalence, dependency rematerialization, existing-output regressions, installed-package checks, and documentation checks. Then replay the current translated corpus sequentially before adopting a local candidate.

The ongoing task has direct standing user approval for in-scope design questions. Public package/docs/dataset releases remain on the requested 200-completed-chart cadence; keep this issue open until a verified public release includes the change. No manual image inspection is claimed.

title: Allow zero and negative Cubehelix lightness gamma
body:
## Problem

The existing continuous Cubehelix color controls reject `gamma: 0` and finite negative gamma. Two valid static inputs need 0 and -0.1; replacing them with the default changes every color.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

chart().createScale({
  id: "tone", type: "sequential", domain: [0, 1],
  range: ["yellow", "red"], interpolate: "cubehelix-long", gamma: 0
});
```

Currently this throws `Scale gamma must be a positive finite number.` The same rejection occurs for -0.1.

## Concrete approved design

- Extend only the existing gamma value domain to all finite numbers, on Cubehelix modes only. No new actions, options, state owners or persisted fields.
- Keep default 1, existing positive results, `auto` resets, mode compatibility, clamping order and 8-bit input/output normalization.
- Gamma zero fixes segment lightness at its right endpoint, including `0 ** 0 = 1`, while hue and saturation keep the original segment position.
- At zero segment position with negative gamma, retain constant endpoint lightness and neutral saturation where applicable; bound the remaining extended RGB channels to bytes (NaN/negative infinity to 0, positive infinity to 255). This boundary is not a general invalid-data fallback. Nonzero-position nonfinite powers/RGB arithmetic still reject atomically.
- Marks, strokes, gradients, sampled legends, persistence, revision and facets share the existing mapper.

Source-neutral proposal, literal numeric targets and reproducible primitive target:
https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/6173f406c8f221a68392d19cfb0f0b33b0085943/agent_docs/impl/nonpositive-color-gamma

The human's standing approval explicitly covers future in-scope API, numeric and visual questions. The design records that approval. No additional approval request is pending.

## Evidence before implementation

- 24 independent 9-position vectors / 216 literal colors, including unchanged gamma-one controls, both hue routes, chromatic/neutral/constant public RGB ranges.
- 392 + 392 original point colors match the proposed numeric behavior exactly; original tables each retain 406 rows.
- Two primitive 480×270 targets each contain 31,050 nonwhite pixels. Literal swatch centers pass exact decoded RGB checks. Current public rejection is retained.
- No image/VLM inspection and no increased numeric/pixel tolerance.
- No paid translation request for either input yet.

## Completion

- [ ] Implement common grammar validation/mapping and synchronize declarations, Current contract, documentation and generated references.
- [ ] Cover zero/negative creation, editors, reset, immutability/atomicity, clamp/reverse/multiple stops, invalid numbers, neutral/constant endpoints, overflow, Full/Basic and persistence.
- [ ] Verify all consumer colors and exact primitive/public graphic/order/trace/decoded pixels.
- [ ] Verify source, package consumers, docs and exact current 1,292-family / 9,414-program native compatibility before local runtime adoption.
- [ ] Publish/synchronize at the next regular 200-family checkpoint, 1,413 successful families. Keep this issue open until actual public publication is verified.

title: Support direct numeric per-item offsets for independent Text marks
body:
## Problem

Independent text marks support constant `dx` / `dy` in `editTextMark`, but cannot map a numeric field to per-item pixel offsets. A staggered calendar text grid needs different horizontal offsets for different rows while preserving its data grain and painter order.

`encodeXOffset` / `encodeYOffset` currently define categorical subgroup placement for bar/point/rule marks. They reject Text and have a different meaning from an unscaled pixel nudge. Splitting one text layer into several layers changes item order and adds unnecessary authoring work.

## Proposed public behavior

Add `encodeDx({target?, field?, value?})` and `encodeDy` for independent Text. Exactly one numeric field or finite numeric constant is required; signed values are logical pixel offsets. There is no scale or `fieldType` option. The three-key API follows existing direct numeric encodings.

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({width: 500, height: 300, margin: 80})
  .createData({values: rows})
  .createTextPlot({x: "hour", y: "day", text: {value: "⬢"}})
  .encodeDx({field: "shift"});
```

Include both channels in existing atomic `encodeChannels`, `removeEncoding`, data/Canvas/scale replay, persistence, declarations, inspection and documentation. An encoded component overrides its corresponding constant text offset; removing it restores the stored constant. Omitting one channel preserves the other. A field-driven offset establishes row grain even when text and both positions are constant.

Source-owned labels and other mark types remain rejected. Preserve input rows, final item order, unrelated encodings and existing omitted behavior. Validate finite numeric fields/constants atomically and retain existing Text missing-row policy. Renderers continue to consume resolved concrete text graphics only.

## Validation

Independent primitive/public graphic and decoded PNG equality; signed X/Y offsets; separate and atomic assignment; field/constant cleanup; removal fallback; row grain including typed empty data; malformed/missing values; target ambiguity; incomplete authoring; source-owned labels; facet/data/Canvas/scale replay; Full/Basic installed-package SVG/PNG/PDF and types; current-program compatibility; synchronized machine-readable and public docs.

The direct user standing approval covers this concrete design and visual review. Keep the issue open until the scheduled public batch release and registry verification; an earlier tested local candidate is not a public release.

title: Support explicit label-title overlap for Cartesian axis titles
Support quantitative color encodings on tick marks
body:
## Missing authoring path

`createTickMark` / `createRugPlot` support a numeric `stroke` mapping, but `encodeColor({field, fieldType:'quantitative'})` rejects Tick. An original barcode chart needs per-observation colors and a solid continuous color ramp. The existing stroke gradient intentionally shows a mapped outline with the mark's fixed fill, so using that representation produces blue interiors instead of a filled color ramp.

The private 0193 source has 2,618 untouched raw CSV records, 187 observations for 2017 and 184 finite visible ticks. Existing Rug→categorical-position→stroke authoring preserves every tick coordinate, length, thickness and opacity. Its 60 stroke-ramp strips all retain fixed `#4c78a8` fill. Exact gradient tick support (#245) is implemented separately; it does not change this consumer distinction.

## Approved design

Extend the existing quantitative/temporal `color` channel to Tick, using the shared scale mapper and color gradient/interval/symbol legend owner. Apply mapped colors to the concrete tick stroke without changing geometry. Keep every prior stroke-only output unchanged. No new mark/action/option, renderer primitive or Basic Tick API.

Reject simultaneous Tick color/stroke encodings and conflicting constant edits; require existing `removeEncoding` before switching channels. Reuse target inference, missing policy, clipping, selection/highlight, rematerialization, persistence and facet rules.

[Concrete proposal and standing human approval](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8509fc95/agent_docs/impl/tick-quantitative-color/PROPOSAL.md).

0193 remains unadmitted with zero School calls. Verify the combined immutable runtime/docs candidate against all current 1,288 families / 9,382 programs before local activation. Keep open until verified publication at the next regular 200-additional-family release (1,413 completed families).

title: Support explicit tick values for continuous gradient legends
body:
## Problem

Continuous color and stroke gradient legends reject `values`, although the existing public `LegendOptions` has exact sample values for other legend representations. An original barcode chart (0193) uses a `[35, 85]` scale with gradient ticks `[40, 60, 80]`. The current evenly spaced automatic samples cannot preserve those values and positions without rendering primitives.

Reproduction with an existing continuous stroke consumer:

```js
program.createLegend({ title: 'lifeExp' })
  .editLegend({ values: [40, 60, 80] });
// strokeGradient legend does not accept values.
```

## Approved concrete design

Extend the existing `values` option to color and stroke gradients; share existing sampling validation and reset semantics. Keep all omitted-option output unchanged. Map each explicit tick through the actual scale rather than spacing its array indices. Reject invalid domain edits atomically. Keep exact samples across color gradient/symbol representation changes and reject family transitions that would discard them.

For `[35,85]`, exact fractions must be `[0.1,0.5,0.9]`; a 125px vertical strip yields offsets `[112.5,62.5,12.5]`. Existing marks, domain and gradient colors remain unchanged. No new action or renderer feature.

[Concrete proposal and standing approval record](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/b0c9d484/agent_docs/impl/gradient-exact-values/PROPOSAL.md).

0193 has zero School model requests and remains unadmitted while this is implemented and verified. Local runtime activation requires an immutable package, matching docs and native compatibility for the current 1,288 families / 9,382 programs. Public publication remains on the 200-additional-successful-family cadence (next 1,413); keep this issue open until public release verification.

title: Enhancement: explicit Steffen monotone recipe for faithful Vega-Lite curve translation
body:
## Request

Offer an explicit Steffen monotone interpolation recipe for translating Vega/Vega-Lite charts, while preserving the existing weighted harmonic/PCHIP `curve: 'monotone'` behavior and every existing program's output.

Both implementations are valid monotone interpolators. The distinction matters for faithful translation: the same anchors and the same `monotone` label can produce different intermediate cubic contours.

## Reproduction and measured evidence

Compare Vega-Lite `mark: {type: 'line', interpolate: 'monotone'}` with ggaction `createLinePlot({x: 'x', y: 'y', line: {curve: 'monotone'}})` over nonuniform data such as:

```json
[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":2,"y":1.5},{"x":4,"y":5}]
```

The source Steffen and native harmonic tangent recipes agree at anchors but generally differ in their cubic control points. This is an enhancement request, not a claim that the current documented interpolator is invalid.

A current private qualification for original corpus chart `vl_1615` provides a concrete area/error-band case: 406 unchanged raw cars records, 398 finite MPG observations, 12 year groups, seed 1 with 1,000 bootstrap samples, and a 200 × 200 plot. All 24 lower/upper boundary anchors, fill `#4c78a8`, opacity `0.3`, and dimensions agree. The native area contains 22 cubic segments. Independently solving derivative roots of every paired cubic coordinate-difference polynomial gives a conservative full-contour distance upper bound of **2.483010776730733 px**, including the original SVG's three-decimal coordinate rounding and explicit floating-evaluation safety. This is an analytic upper bound, not a pixel-difference measurement or a claim about the exact maximum distance.

Qualification runtime: unreleased local candidate `c9d8d6eaf78c2cce5abfc3a2cd96d6db2a8a4e80` (package manifest still 0.0.21; not a new registry release). Original seeded source SVG SHA-256: `00b15b8cde5ccf5a527b32e8715fd17dc0d129250c93da1ee4285a11c1f0f9d6`.

## Suggested design and acceptance criteria

- Add an explicit, separately named recipe rather than silently changing `monotone`. Final public naming should be recorded in a concrete API design before implementation.
- Apply the selected recipe consistently to line, area, error-band, and explicitly requested boundary curves through the existing semantic actions; no renderer primitives should be necessary in translated code.
- Preserve the choice through Full/Basic facades, editing, persistence, and SVG/Canvas/PDF output.
- Verify every control point against independent Steffen reference calculations, including nonuniform X spacing, reversed area boundaries, repeated/degenerate X cases, and monotonicity. Verify existing `monotone` outputs remain unchanged.
- Keep the normal action/option budgets and numeric tolerances unchanged.

The current translation can proceed using a disclosed, source-bound native interpolation convention under the user's standing approximation approval. Exact Steffen selection would remove that intermediate-contour difference in future translations. Publication should follow the existing coordinated 200-success-family release cadence; this issue does not request an immediate release.

title: Support bounded paths up to 30000 commands
body:
## Problem

A source chart with 26,265 raw observations produces 25,909 minute-bucket means. Existing numeric conversion, `createTimeUnitData` and `createSummaryData` preserve the complete input and produce the correct groups, but `createLinePlot` rejects their single linear path:

```
Curve path command count must not exceed 20000.
```

The original chart uses an 800×200 plot and a 0.2px line. Reducing rows or changing the line would change the chart. This source remains unadmitted to the translation run; no model request has been spent on it.

Minimal reproduction using ordinary public actions:

```js
const values = Array.from({length: 25909}, (_, x) => ({x, y: x % 101}));
chart().createCanvas({plot: {width: 800, height: 200}, margin: 40})
  .createData({values})
  .createLinePlot({x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false});
```

## Approved implementation

Raise the existing shared per-path command ceiling to **30,000 inclusive**. Keep M/L/C/Z validation, interpolation/area expansion accounting and rejection before allocation; reject 30,001 commands. Do not change other generated-item, point, summary-group or work budgets. No new action, option, persisted field, renderer or automatic sampling.

Existing paths at or below 20,000 retain their output. Larger saved paths require the new capacity in their reader. Verify boundary counts, expanded curves/areas, native public creation/edit/revision/resizing/persistence, SVG/Canvas/PDF consumers, immutability and unchanged independent limits; synchronize current contracts and public/generated documentation.

Concrete design and standing human approval evidence: [proposal at 8016da3a](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8016da3a/agent_docs/impl/path-command-capacity-30000/PROPOSAL.md).

This follows the bounded-capacity work in #192. Keep this issue open until the next authorized 200-family publication checkpoint (1,413 successful source charts), including registry-install verification; local candidate tests alone do not close it.

title: Fix Basic field encoding scale reassignment without exposing Full editors
Support explicit unknown fallbacks for categorical stroke-dash scales
body:
## Problem

A line dataset can contain valid categories outside an explicitly ordered stroke-dash domain. An author needs an explicit dash fallback for those paths while keeping every original row, raw category identity, domain entry, and legend item unchanged.

The ordinal scale machinery already normalizes stroke-dash unknown values, but public field encoding rejects them, the shared consumer policy restricts unknown to other consumers, the focused dash editor does not accept the option, and `DashScaleOptions` omits it.

A minimal proposed flow is:

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';

chart()
  .createCanvas({plot: {width: 200, height: 120},
    margin: {left: 20, right: 100, top: 20, bottom: 30}, plotBorder: false})
  .createData({values: [
    {group: 'known', x: 0, y: 2}, {group: 'known', x: 1, y: 2},
    {group: 'other', x: 0, y: 1}, {group: 'other', x: 1, y: 1}
  ]})
  .createLinePlot({x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false})
  .encodeStrokeDash({field: 'group', scale: {
    domain: ['known'], range: [[4, 2]], unknown: []
  }});
```

Currently the final call throws `StrokeDash scale unknown is not supported for grouped line or rule paths.` A late generic scale edit is also rejected by the shared consumer policy. A generic derived-data definition is not a value-producing workaround. Splitting a semantic style fallback into extra filtered datasets and mark layers also makes the ordinary program unnecessarily large.

## Proposed contract

- Extend existing categorical `encodeStrokeDash`/facade/bulk scale options with `unknown: DashStyle | DashPattern`; no new action and no new persisted key.
- Omission preserves existing strict out-of-domain errors. Explicit `[]` means a solid path; named styles use existing dash normalization.
- Support Cartesian line and rule consumers, with original nominal/ordinal roles and raw series identities preserved. Missing/malformed categories and within-series conflicting raw appearance values remain errors.
- Keep the explicit domain/range and legend items unchanged. Never append unknown categories to the domain or legend.
- Add the same option to `editStrokeDashScale`, generic scale edit/reuse, data revisions, selection, persistence and export. Omitted edit values retain the fallback; explicit `unknown: undefined` removes it under complete compatibility preflight.
- Rejected edits remain atomic, including removal of a fallback while out-of-domain rows still exist, shared incompatible consumers, invalid patterns, and unsupported coordinates.
- Preserve all other unknown-channel behavior and all existing programs without the new option.

## Verification and delivery

Use source-neutral line/rule examples, nominal/ordinal and facade/bulk parity, independent path/dash/legend assertions, incomplete-position order, data revision/replay, selection, immutable caller/prior state, public type consumers, saved programs and SVG/PNG/PDF export. Synchronize current contracts, declarations, generated action/LLM references and public docs.

This is authorized by the user's standing approval for all in-scope design questions. Collect verified changes on the existing candidate branch; publish only at the next 200-family checkpoint (1,413 completed families). Keep the issue open until integration/publication. The dependent chart remains unadmitted with zero model requests while the capability is implemented and qualified.

title: Add lossless aligned expansion of parallel array fields
body:
## Problem

There is no ordinary public data action for expanding parallel array columns into aligned rows. Existing wide-field folding rejects array cells, scalar nested-field access rejects arrays, and direct derived-data validation rejects `type: "flatten"`.

This blocks lossless use of records such as:

```js
[
  { amounts: [1, 2], labels: ["A", "B"], group: "alpha" },
  { amounts: [3, 4, 5], labels: ["C", "D"], group: "beta" }
]
```

Expected five rows retain each original record and add scalar aliases: `(1,"A"), (2,"B"), (3,"C"), (4,"D"), (5,null)`. The last observation must remain present. Expansion is by matching array index, not a Cartesian product. Source row order, array order, all original raw values and unrelated columns must survive.

## Proposed ordinary API

`createFlattenData({id, source?, fields, as?})`, plus the existing derived-data revision policy exposed through `editFlattenData` and `editDerivedData`. The common explicit-alias use needs only three top-level options.

Normalize one semantic `flatten` transform; preserve raw ancestors; use the existing wrapped derived materializer, typed schema lineage and atomic dependent replay. Null/missing arrays behave as empty arrays; shorter arrays pad with null. Reject non-array values, duplicate/invalid fields or aliases, unrelated-column overwrite and output beyond 10,000 rows before any state change. Selected-field replacement is allowed only in the derived result; original source arrays remain immutable.

## Acceptance

- Full and Basic entry points, typed declarations, action catalog/current contracts and public docs agree.
- Independent exact five-row expectation; mixed lengths, empty/null/missing arrays, alias collisions and row limits have tests.
- Raw/earlier programs and caller arrays stay immutable; schema lineage, trace and persistence round-trip hold.
- Derived edits reject or recompute downstream consumers atomically under existing policy.
- Installed-package and ordinary browser rendering checks pass.

Concrete design: `agent_docs/impl/parallel-array-expansion/PROPOSAL.md`. Implementation is authorized under the ongoing user-approved library-fix scope. Keep open until verified integration at the next regular release checkpoint; no per-fix public release.

title: Inherit fixed line stroke in categorical stroke-dash legends
body:
## Problem

A line with a fixed orange stroke and a categorical stroke-dash encoding renders orange marks but blue legend samples. The sample should inherit the target line's fixed stroke when no color or stroke scale owns its paint.

Reproduced at source commit `47270e126e881c378c3e66aa32dbaccecdc913b1`.

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 300, margin: 60 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { x: 0, y: 1, g: 'A' }, { x: 1, y: 1, g: 'A' },
    { x: 0, y: 2, g: 'B' }, { x: 1, y: 2, g: 'B' }
  ] })
  .createLinePlot({ x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false })
  .encodeGroup({ field: 'g' })
  .encodeStrokeDash({ field: 'g' })
  .editLineMark({ stroke: 'orange', opacity: 0.6 })
  .createLegend({ symbol: {
    layers: [{ type: 'line', length: 10, lineWidth: 1, opacity: 1 }]
  } });
```

Expected sample strokes: `['orange', 'orange']`; actual: `['#4c78a8', '#4c78a8']`. Mark opacity remains 0.6 and the explicitly requested sample opacity remains 1.

Existing workaround costs one extra action:

```js
.editLegendBlock({
  target: 'linePlot', channel: 'strokeDash', symbol: { stroke: 'orange' }
})
```

## Proposed correction

For a categorical stroke-dash legend attached to a line, inherit the uniquely resolved target's fixed stroke when no mapped color/stroke owns the sample paint. Preserve explicit block overrides, mapped scales, sample opacity, dash arrays, dimensions, other mark families, and immutable rematerialization. No new API or persisted option is required.

Add regressions for creation, later line edits, explicit block overrides, mapped color/stroke precedence, defaults and earlier program immutability. Synchronize canonical contracts and generated documentation. Keep this issue open until the next authorized batch release and consumer verification.

title: Allow opt-in plot-last placement for high-level regression lines
body:
## Problem

`createRegression` deliberately attaches its fitted line immediately after the source point mark. In a layered Cartesian plot, a line authored between the points and the later regression call therefore remains above the fitted line. Chart authors cannot express a last-painted fit through the high-level regression facade.

Reproduced against source commit 47270e126e881c378c3e66aa32dbaccecdc913b1:

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({width:400, height:300})
  .createData({values:[{x:0,y:1},{x:1,y:2},{x:2,y:1}]})
  .createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .createLinePlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .createRegression({interval:false,predict:{values:[0,2]}});
```

Semantic mark order: `scatterPlot`, `linePlot`, `scatterPlotRegressionLines`.
Actual graphic painter order: `scatterPlot`, `scatterPlotRegressionLines`, `linePlot`.

## Existing working route

The public `createRegressionData` / `editRegressionData`, an independent line mark, and `bindMarkData` can retain a last-painted fitted line. This route has been verified with all source vertices and original data, so this is a nonblocking high-level authoring enhancement, not a missing rendering primitive or a reason to fabricate rows.

Creating a line directly on a regression dataset is not equivalent: placement infers its source mark, and fails when several marks share the source dataset unless a namespaced source uniquely resolves it. Binding an already positioned independent mark preserves its existing place.

## Suggested direction

Consider an explicit opt-in placement policy on the high-level regression owner, while preserving today's source-attached behavior by default. A plot-last policy should put the fit after existing marks while respecting grid/frame/axis overlay ownership. Creation, editing, data revision, source-following rebinding, selections/highlights, restore and export must retain the chosen policy. No renderer primitive should be necessary in ordinary chart code.

This would reduce several setup/binding actions and allow a high-level-first program to be progressively decomposed into the existing regression-data / line-mark route with identical output. A concrete API design and regression checks should precede implementation; no package publication is requested by this issue.

title: Synchronize formatter types with grouped numbers and UTC weekdays
body:
## Problem

The existing shared formatter accepts grouped numbers (`","`, `",.2f"`) and UTC weekday names (`"%a"`), but the exported TypeScript format types do not cover them.

- `src/grammar/valueFormat.js` accepts `GROUPED_NUMERIC_FORMAT` and UTC directive `a`.
- `test/unit/grammar/value-format.test.js` already verifies these outputs.
- `NumericFormatString` only declares ungrouped `f`, `%`, and `e` forms.
- `TimeAxisDirective` omits `a`, so a bare `"%a"` also fails type checking.

This makes valid minimal public programs appear unsupported. For example, axis labels can use `format: ","` to produce `1,000` without supplying a long manual label map.

## Proposed fix

Synchronize declarations, current contracts and generated/public references with the existing runtime grammar:

- Add `","` and `,.<0..12>f` to the existing numeric format type.
- Add `a` to the existing UTC directive type.
- Add positive/negative TypeScript consumer checks, including Full/Basic authoring.
- Preserve all runtime source, defaults, output, precision bounds and unsupported grouped percent/scientific formats.

This requires no runtime feature, persisted field or renderer change. Runtime compatibility can retain the completed current-cohort replay only after proving every executable package file is byte-identical; any runtime difference requires a fresh replay. Publishing remains at the regular batch checkpoint.

title: Support explicit categorical unknown colors for row-owned Cartesian lines
body:
A categorical color scale with an explicit `unknown` paint is currently restricted to row-owned points. A row-owned Cartesian line whose color field is absent cannot retain its unpainted path plus its real explicit-domain legend.

Confirmed on the locally installed, hash-verified development candidate at `ffd3295e9e073ae1f28142b8f52fee6f2d4ab02a` (package manifest version 0.0.21; unreleased candidate).

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({width: 240, height: 120, margin: {left: 20, right: 100, top: 10, bottom: 20}})
  .createData({values: [{id: 0}, {id: 1}]})
  .createLinePlot({x: 'id', y: 'id', guides: false})
  .encodeColor({field: 'kind', fieldType: 'nominal', scale: {
    domain: ['Regression', 'Reference'],
    range: ['firebrick', 'black'],
    unknown: 'transparent'
  }})
  .createLegend({channels: ['color'], title: 'Line'});
```

Current failure: the nominal reader rejects the absent field. Using a separately derived string display key also fails with `Categorical color scale unknown currently requires a row-owned point mark.` Neither route should require fabricated observations or replacement legend data.

Proposed scope: extend the existing ordinal color `unknown` option to row-owned Cartesian lines with explicit nonempty categorical domains. Missing/null and valid out-of-domain color values map to the explicit paint; raw rows/keys/types remain unchanged. Keep missing versus null series identities separate, preserve the explicit legend domain even if no path paints, and retain strict validation without the opt-in. Explicit grouping, aggregated/binned/parallel/polar paths and other mark/channel fallbacks retain their existing constraints. Invalid object/array/nonfinite categorical values still reject for the new line branch.

Verify direct/facade/bulk authoring, immutable atomic rejection, scale editing/shared consumers, data revisions, selection/highlights, editable restore, Basic/Full declarations and installed public packages, and native/primitive SVG/PNG/PDF equality. No new action or persisted state field is proposed.

This is the remaining essential capability for a retained 500-row source with 494 eligible points and an intentionally unpainted categorical line; its separate clipping issue #220 is already implemented. Public publication remains in the scheduled 200-family release.

title: Place inferred side legends outside occupied same-edge axes
Allow rounded-bar legend sample recipes to change through symbol editors
body:
## Problem

On ggaction 0.0.21 (e93500081b6dde6be7614e3e9352e947bec5908d), the existing public `editLegendSymbols` API cannot change a default categorical sample on a rounded bar mark into an explicitly supported swatch recipe. It throws `rematerializeLegendSymbolSwatches requires existing swatch symbols.` The same recipe succeeds when supplied to `createLegend`.

## Minimal reproduction

```javascript
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
const seed = () => chart()
  .createCanvas({plot:{width:200,height:200},margin:{left:40,right:120,top:40,bottom:40}})
  .createData({values:[{category:'A',value:1},{category:'B',value:2}]})
  .createBarPlot({x:'category',y:'value',guides:false})
  .editBarMark({cornerRadius:1})
  .encodeColor({field:'category'});
const symbol = {width:10,height:10,strokeWidth:0};
seed().createLegend({symbol}); // succeeds
seed().createLegend({}).editLegendSymbols({symbol}); // throws
```

The equivalent layered recipe `{layers:[{type:'swatch',width:10,height:10,strokeWidth:0}]}` also throws on edit.

The rounded mark configuration is essential: the same edit succeeds without `cornerRadius:1`. This narrows the failure to replacement of the rounded/path-backed fallback symbol collection; a generic default-circle example without rounded bars does not reproduce it.

## Expected behavior

An existing categorical legend can change among its already-supported line/point/swatch recipes through its domain editor. Materialization should replace the owned concrete recipe collections, retain resource identity/data/labels/title/placement and leave no stale graphics. No new public option is needed.

## Suggested validation

Cover rounded-bar/path-backed fallback to explicit swatch, unchanged unrounded-bar controls, point-to-swatch, swatch-to-point, mixed line/point/swatch transitions and restoration to `auto`. Check repeated edits, concrete ownership/paint order, absence of stale sample collections, immutable prior programs, SVG/PDF/backend behavior and unchanged sample-label clearance. Invalid/incompatible owners must retain existing errors. Default output must remain unchanged.

Confirmed by direct public-program execution, without image inspection or model calls. A translation can currently use the complete swatch recipe at legend birth; retain that working route. Prepare a tested fix for the next regular 200-family batch release rather than publishing an isolated patch.

title: Support ordinal categorical fields in stroke-dash encodings
Render valid empty concrete text without rejecting mapped labels
body:
## Problem

The concrete graphic schema and the documented display-label contracts accept `text: ""` so a mapped label can keep its item identity while painting no glyph. Canvas and SVG subsequently reject the same valid value as a non-empty-string requirement. Node PNG and PDF inherit the Canvas failure.

## Reproduction

```js
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 180, height: 180, margin: 50 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { panel: "A", x: 0, y: 0 },
    { panel: "B", x: 1, y: 1 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false })
  .facet({ field: "panel", headers: { labelMap: [{ value: "A", label: "" }] } });
renderToSVG(program);
```

The final call throws `Graphic "facet-headers:0" requires a non-empty text property.` Both mapped items still exist in the correct concrete scene before rendering.

## Expected behavior and candidate

Render empty concrete text without a glyph, retain item identity/data/layout, and continue rejecting missing/non-string text and empty appearance strings. High-level author-supplied titles and annotations retain their own non-empty requirements.

Candidate commit `eea2d2f1` restores the existing concrete value validator as the single text-value contract in Canvas and SVG. No public API/schema or visual tolerance changes. The regression covers default and shared facet layouts, immutable persistence, Node Canvas/SVG/PNG/PDF, and all three browser engines at both densities. Existing 92 public examples retain exact default semantic/guide/graphic/SVG output.

Found during #222 qualification. This is an unreleased candidate; final full-suite/package verification and the regular 200-family release checkpoint remain separate. Keep this issue open until release integration.

title: Shared facet legend inference treats continuous color and stroke as ordinal
Preserve bootstrap interval precision and prepare 0.0.21
body:
Bootstrap interval materialization rounded a positive percentile interval around 1 to zero width. Preserve full finite Number values for the explicit bootstrap method and retain the output policy for other interval methods. Synchronize the contract and public/generated documentation and prepare 0.0.21.

Validation: 4,628 normal tests; 35 focused numerical/action tests; installed-package consumers; browser Canvas/SVG and primitive PNG parity; 150 documentation pages with responsive, search, keyboard and accessibility checks. All 8,780 programs from 1,212 chart families produce exactly their existing SVGs in the candidate. The shortened release note also passes the existing archive limit on Node 24.21.0; executable inputs are unchanged.

Closes #229.

title: Bootstrap intervals lose precision and can collapse a positive interval to zero width
Support quantitative Area color and seeded mean intervals (0.0.20)
body:

Group identity, layout, geometry, outlines and opacity remain independent; varying within-series values, temporal color, aggregation and point-only unknown fallback reject atomically.

Summary and interval data actions can calculate explicitly seeded, nonweighted percentile-bootstrap mean confidence intervals. Related endpoints share sample means, source order and raw observations are preserved, and resampling is bounded before computation. Existing normal/Student-t and regression behavior remains unchanged. Prepare version 0.0.20 with synchronized contracts, declarations, examples, generated documentation and release provenance.

Fixes #218
Fixes #219
