title: HCL interpolation rotates toward an arbitrary hue at neutral-gray endpoints
Range endpoint datum objects accepted by public types fail for rect marks
Support content-aware legend row padding and independent title-to-body spacing
body:
## Problem

The released public legend API offers `itemGap` as a uniform vertical center-to-center pitch (at least the largest sample height). It cannot express a fixed gap between the occupied bounds of adjacent variable-size rows. There is also no independently adjustable gap between a legend title and its body.

A source with explicit `rowPadding: 15` and `titlePadding: 20` therefore cannot retain these authored choices using ordinary complete legends and public edits. This is separate from an omitted default-spacing preference.

## Reproduction on ggaction 0.0.19

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({width:520,height:600,margin:{left:40,top:10,right:180,bottom:290}})
  .createData({values:[0,50,100,150,200].map((v,i)=>({x:i,y:i,v}))})
  .createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .encodeSize({field:'v',fieldType:'quantitative',scale:{
    type:'linear',domain:[0,230],range:[Math.PI,361*Math.PI/4]
  }})
  .createGuides({axes:false,grid:false,legend:{
    channels:['size'],values:[0,50,100,150,200],itemGap:15
  }});
```

Actual consecutive sample-center distances are all approximately **17.732309px**. Raising `itemGap` changes all distances together. `editLegend({rowPadding:15})`, `itemPadding`, and `titlePadding` reject unknown keys atomically. `labels.offset` is horizontal label clearance, `border.padding` surrounds the entire block, and block `gap` controls another boundary.

In the motivating source, actual source size-sample center distances are **28.5, 33.5, 36.5, 39px**. The source has 406 original car rows, 392 visible points, and categorical color, size and opacity legends with an explicit dashed frame. All 392 point positions, colors, areas, opacities and raw rows were verified using existing `encodeChannels`; the frame dash is already supported. This hold concerns the explicit internal spacing, not those capabilities.

## Expected direction / review required

Support content-aware row padding and independent title/body spacing using the ordinary legend ownership/edit lifecycle, while preserving omitted existing output and uniform-pitch compatibility. The concrete public names, precedence, persistence, all-family support and bounds behavior need a proposal and approval before implementation. No new API is assumed approved by this issue.

Regression evidence should include different sample sizes, text heights and strokes, categorical/size/opacity and sampled-color blocks, creation/edit/replay parity, title hiding, edge and in-plot positions, whole-block border bounds and collision/overflow rejection. Renderers should continue consuming materialized graphics only.

The affected source is held before admission; there have been **zero school-model calls** for this candidate. No data or fonts were changed to force the layout.

title: Align continuous-color palette descriptor types with accepted runtime count and range forms
body:
## Reproduction

This public JavaScript program executes successfully against the published ggaction 0.0.19 package:

```ts
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
chart().createCanvas({width:200,height:160,margin:30})
 .createData({values:[{x:0,y:0,v:0},{x:1,y:1,v:1}]})
 .createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
 .encodeStroke({field:'v',fieldType:'quantitative',scale:{
   type:'sequential',domain:[0,1],palette:{name:'turbo',count:64}
 }});
```

The identical program fails `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target es2022` with TS2353: `count` is absent from `{name: PaletteName; extent?: readonly [number, number]}`.

## Expected consistency

The public TypeScript continuous-color encoding type should describe the palette descriptor already accepted by runtime normalization. `NonPointContinuousColorScaleOptions` narrows the descriptor and loses `count`, although the existing `Palette` machinery accepts it. The equivalent existing runtime form `scale.range: {palette: {name:'turbo',count:64}}` also executes but is absent from the array-only continuous-color `range` declaration.

This report requests typing parity with existing behavior, not a new runtime option or a change to palette interpolation/defaults. Review shared declarations and the stroke/color/encodeChannels consumers together; retain closed types and add positive/negative package-consumer type tests.

## Evidence

Both runtime descriptor forms were independently executed and produced deeply identical graphics on the same source-backed continuous color chart. The count matters: the native default sample count and an explicit 64-stop palette produce different colors. Treating a valid runtime descriptor as unsupported would cause unnecessary chart repairs.

Package/runtime: 0.0.19, commit `f6b50bf55a9de1857f106c7aa519326ce7a86d76`. The minimal two-row JavaScript reproduction was executed; the TypeScript diagnostic was captured. No chart pixels inspected, no API or renderer changes implemented.

title: Support opt-in axes and plot-border underlays for composited marks
body:
## Problem

Ordinary Cartesian marks are always materialized before axis and plot-border graphics. A source chart that composites a `difference` mark over those guides cannot currently preserve its backdrop through ordinary mark/axis/Canvas actions. This is a paint-order limitation, not a request to change existing defaults.

## Executed public reproduction (0.0.19)

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 240, height: 180,
    margin: { left: 40, right: 20, top: 20, bottom: 40 } })
  .editCanvas({ plotBorder: { color: '#ddd', lineWidth: 1 } })
  .createData({ values: [{ category: 'a', value: 6 }, { category: 'b', value: 9 }] })
  .createBarPlot({ x: 'category', y: { field: 'value',
    scale: { domain: [0, 10], nice: false } }, guides: false })
  .encodeBarWidth({ band: 1 })
  .editBarMark({ fill: 'yellow', stroke: 'yellow', strokeWidth: 4 })
  .editBarMark({ cornerRadius: 10, blend: 'difference' })
  .createXAxis({ line: { color: '#888', lineWidth: 2 },
    ticksAndLabels: false, title: false })
  .createGrid({ horizontal: { values: [0, 5, 10], color: '#ddd', lineWidth: 1 },
    vertical: false });
console.log(p.graphicSpec.objects['plot-main'].children);
// ['horizontalGridLines', 'barPlot', 'plotBorder', 'xAxisLine']
```

Moving the two mark edits after guide creation was also executed: the materialized bar layer still precedes the axes/border. `editXAxis({ zIndex: -1 })` and adding `zIndex` to `plotBorder` both reject unknown options; the original immutable program remains unchanged after both rejections.

At an opaque yellow / `#888` intersection, yellow composited with difference over the axis yields RGB `[119,119,136]`; drawing the opaque axis last yields `[136,136,136]`. Both are valid compositions, but they cannot represent the same source design. The source regression has all 53 stroked guides before its 12 difference bars; native output puts axes and border after them. Raw rows, monthly aggregates, all 12 bounds, gradient endpoints/stops and paint styles were independently checked before isolating this problem.

## Investigation

`src/materialization/graphicHierarchy.js` inserts an ordinary mark before the first plot-border/axis graphic and preserves that placement across later edits. Grid direction options expose `zIndex`; axes and the plot border have no equivalent ordinary placement option. Highlight bring-to-front changes item order within a mark layer. Extension graphics are not an ordinary semantic chart-authoring substitute.

## Desired capability / acceptance constraints

Provide an explicit, source-neutral way to place axes and/or a plot border before marks while preserving omitted/default paint order. The exact API and ownership design need review before implementation. Keep semantic ownership, immutable edit replay, canonical/named axes, facet/concat behavior and all export renderers consistent. Renderers should continue consuming materialized graphics, rather than reading semantic chart options.

Tests should cover normal and difference marks, default-output identity, guide-before/after placement, create/edit ordering, rejected-option atomicity, and exported SVG/Canvas/PDF paint order. This issue does not authorize a public API or architecture change.

Reproduction proof: ggaction 0.0.19 / commit `f6b50bf55a9de1857f106c7aa519326ce7a86d76`, reproduction script SHA-256 `0a29e3dfd33d823f91ab657a09ad85808665975e519f9108c3da3962ea34f89e`. No chart pixels inspected; no translation accepted through this gap.

title: Support a compact shared top lane for facet title, headers and endpoint labels
body:
## Problem

A compact, one-row facet cannot currently share its existing top margin between a parent title, column headers, and the upper Y-axis endpoint label. `spacing: 'plot'` adds the full header lane and parent-title lane to the complete child top margin. Reducing that child margin to compensate fails eager unit-axis Canvas validation even when the translated label would fit safely in the final assembled parent.

This is a request for a supported composition layout, not a request to weaken standalone-axis bounds checks or to modify a renderer.

## Reproduction (published ggaction 0.0.19)

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

const rows = [
  { panel: 'Sun', group: 'a', value: 13 },
  { panel: 'Sun', group: 'b', value: 14 },
  { panel: 'Mon', group: 'a', value: 13 },
  { panel: 'Mon', group: 'b', value: 14 }
];

const unit = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 136, height: 262,
    margin: { left: 40, right: 56, top: 43, bottom: 19 } })
  .createData({ values: rows })
  .createBarPlot({ x: 'group',
    y: { field: 'value', scale: { domain: [0, 50], nice: false } },
    guides: false })
  .encodeColor({ field: 'group', layout: 'overlay' })
  .createAxes({
    x: { title: false, ticksAndLabels: {
      labels: { fontSize: 10, color: 'black', offset: 5.5 } } },
    y: { ticksAndLabels: { values: [0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
      labels: { fontSize: 10, color: 'black' } }, title: false }
  });

const parent = unit
  .facet({ field: 'panel', values: ['Sun', 'Mon'] })
  .editFacetGuides({ axes: 'outer', legend: 'shared' })
  .editCompositionLayout({ spacing: 'plot', gap: 22 })
  .editFacetHeaders({ fontSize: 10, fontWeight: 400, offset: 11 })
  .createTitle({ text: 'Grouped Bar Chart', align: 'left',
    titleStyle: { fontSize: 13, fontWeight: 700, color: 'black' } });
```

The current layout adds a 21px header reservation plus a 21px parent-title reservation to the unit's existing top margin. The user needs a target whose inner plots start at global Y=43, whose header text occupies Y=20..32, and whose parent title occupies Y=3..18. The upper endpoint label occupies Y=36.5..48.5. These global bounds are mutually consistent.

## Independently measured full example

In a seven-panel case, each panel's inner plot is 40x200 with a 22px plot gap. The target Canvas is 508x262; all seven plot origins are `(40 + 62*i, 43)`.

- Current API with a 43px unit top margin produces 508x304 and plot Y=85.
- Raw 14 input rows, UTC-weekday derivation, all seven partitions, and all 14 local bar geometries are independently verified. Maximum local floating point difference is 1.43e-14. This is a layout constraint, not a data-partition failure.
- Calibrating the original 13px title and 10px headers requires a 19px title reservation and 20.609375px header reservation. Preserving plot Y=43 therefore requires a 3.390625px unit top margin under the current additive layout.
- That unit is rejected by `createYAxisLabels`: `The y-axis labels do not fit the Canvas margin.` The final assembled upper label would nevertheless occupy Y=36.5..48.5 inside the parent.
- Plot spacing must be configured after outer-axis ownership is selected; the opposite order correctly fails an unrelated collision check and is not the issue reported here.

## Expected direction / constraints for design

Provide an explicit, source-neutral way to reserve a compact parent top lane using final assembled guide bounds, or another documented public lifecycle producing the same valid geometry. Preserve immutable programs, fully materialized child/parent snapshots, renderer independence, guide ownership, and strict standalone-unit checks. Do not silently shrink fonts, drop endpoint labels, move titles into mark layers, crop content, or change the inner plots/data to hide the failure. Omitted layout behavior should remain compatible unless a separately approved design says otherwise.

The exact API/core design remains unresolved and needs its own review before implementation. No library changes or chart acceptance are claimed here.

title: Allow explicit facet partitioning by a key produced by fold data
Support opt-in Cartesian plot clipping for individual mark layers
body:
## Problem
Published 0.0.19 cannot express a Cartesian mark collection clipped to its plot rectangle while preserving the original rows and unclamped scale positions. The current public Point mark/edit/encoding options expose no plot clipping policy.

A 500-row CSV source filters to 494 observations; its first layer is 494 filled circles explicitly clipped to a 500×500 plot. Ten centers lie outside the plot. Other line layers and the outside legend must remain unclipped. This is not equivalent to clamping points, dropping raw observations, or clipping the entire outer Canvas.

## Actual public control
With the original rows, fresh typed numeric columns, the exact source filter and domains [0,3500], current createScatterPlot + source radius sqrt(30)/2 and opacity 0.7 successfully materializes all 494 circles. Ten centers remain outside the plot. Its SVG has no clip path/reference. The source SVG has one actual rectangular clipPath referenced only by its symbol layer. Thus chart-like rendering alone misses a visible semantic difference.

Runtime: npm 0.0.19 / f6b50bf55a9de1857f106c7aa519326ce7a86d76. Source inner plot 500×500; source outer Canvas 643×544 with margins left53/top7/right90/bottom37. No point values were changed, filtered by viewport, or clamped to conceal the difference.

## Required behavior and decisions to review
A concrete source-neutral public/persistence design needs approval before implementation. It should cover:
- Opt-in plot clipping on the owning semantic mark, retaining all raw/derived observations and actual scale coordinates. Existing behavior remains the default.
- Immutable, fully materialized concrete clip bounds; renderers read graphicSpec only.
- Per-layer ownership: clipping the Point does not clip the three independent Lines, axes or external legend.
- Shared behavior across SVG, Canvas and PDF, including partial boundary glyphs, strokes, opacity, exports, rematerialization, inset/facet coordinates, serialization and replay.
- Coordinate/scale/Canvas edits update the clip bounds; disabling clipping restores the unchanged off-plot geometry.
- Regression controls proving that clipping does not become data filtering, scale clamping, or outer-Canvas clipping.

## Translation status
Only the affected family is held, before any school-model translation request. This is an actual public capability gap; it is not a failure to render the source. A separate source detail also needs deliberate handling: one reference line binds a nonexistent nominal color field, so the source paints no stroke yet retains an explicit two-entry legend. Current native nominal encoding rejects both the missing field and a null alias. That second behavior must not be silently replaced with invented source data or a fake legend mark.

No new public clipping API or stored schema is approved or implemented by this issue.

title: Support deterministic percentile bootstrap mean confidence intervals
body:
## Problem
The current mean-confidence interval data actions expose only normal and Student-t methods. A percentile bootstrap interval cannot be expressed without replacing the estimator or precomputing and hardcoding derived bounds outside the native dataflow.

## Reproduction on published 0.0.19
A dataset has 1,600 numeric observations, grouped into 320 groups of five. Each group needs its mean plus the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of 1,000 resampled means (sampling with replacement).

Actual public calls reject all of the following:
- `createSummaryData` with `op: { op: 'ciLower', method: { type: 'bootstrap', samples: 1000, seed: 1 } }`: `Unsupported Aggregate confidence interval method "[object Object]".`
- `createIntervalData` with `extent: 'ci', method: 'bootstrap'`: `Unsupported Interval CI method "bootstrap".`
- `createSummaryData` with `op: 'ci0'`: `Unsupported aggregate "ci0".`

The rejected calls preserve the earlier immutable program and its raw rows. The first observed reference group has mean -86.71606827432944 and bounds [-141.3200636059544, -52.60957536920556]. 293 of 320 reference intervals are asymmetric, so swapping in the existing symmetric estimators is not an equivalent solution.

## Required behavior
- Native typed summary/interval dataflow computes percentile bootstrap confidence bounds around the mean.
- Lower and upper bounds share the same resampling run; preserve all raw rows, field names and types.
- Explicit reproducibility: specify RNG, seed, group/field traversal, quantile interpolation, missing/empty/singleton policies, limits and atomic validation.
- Preserve existing normal/Student-t behavior, immutable materialization, and renderer boundaries.
- Tests should cover skewed groups, deterministic replay, paired bounds, grouping, edge cases, limits and consumers such as area intervals.

## Status
Capability gap confirmed against the exact published runtime commit f6b50bf55a9de1857f106c7aa519326ce7a86d76. This is a feature request, not an approved API design. A concrete source-neutral proposal and independent target must be prepared and explicitly approved before implementation. In particular, the current reference bootstrap uses an unseeded random source; a reproducible reference policy remains an open design decision.

The affected translation family is held. No model translation call was spent on it and no unsupported estimator substitution was made. Other independent translations continue sequentially.

title: Support quantitative color for area series
body:
## Problem

The published 0.0.19 `encodeColor` action rejects quantitative color on an area mark even when each explicit series has exactly one finite color value. The same shared HCL/D50 scale already works on point marks. Replacing the numeric scale with categorical colors would change the meaning and disconnect the continuous legend.

The translation of source **0448** is held before any model generation call: 13,896 immutable raw rows, 3,537 aggregated positions, nine stacked area series, an eight-stop continuous color ramp, area opacity 0.7 and a matching gradient legend. This is a capability hold, not an invalid source or a successful translation.

## Reproduction and proposed contract

Review revision: [`783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4`](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4).

- [Concrete proposal, scope, compatibility and consumer verification](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4/agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable synthetic public fixture](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4/agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/fixture.mjs)
- [Actual rejection and immutable-state evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4/agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/rejection-evidence.json)
- [Independent nine-path graphical target](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4/agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/target.svg)
- [DOM geometry/paint checks and actual PNG render evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/783d7e7bc022dcd12af3475e93a19f11052106a4/agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/target-render-evidence.json)

```sh
node agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/reproduce.mjs
node agent_docs/impl/continuous-area-color/render-target.mjs
```

Current exact error: `continuous color mark requires an eligible layer.` The earlier immutable program remains unchanged.

The proposal extends the **existing** `encodeColor` consumer to quantitative area fill with one constant finite value per series. It reuses current scale kinds, interpolation and materialization ownership; it introduces no action, option or persisted key. Temporal area color, aggregation, point-only unknown handling, per-vertex gradients and line-color changes are outside this scope. Explicit grouping and layout remain separate owners. Existing categorical area and other mark output must remain unchanged.

## Status and acceptance

**Ready for public-contract and graphical-target approval; implementation has not begun.** The independent target is rendered, but no new public area/primitive equality or new public trace success is claimed.

After approval: implement atomic validation and explicit per-series materialization, test scale/data/coordinate edits, fallback/selection/persistence, continuous legends, Full/Basic and renderer/package consumers, update types/current contracts/public docs/generated references, run focused plus cumulative checks, then verify the real held translation with the released synchronized runtime. Do not loosen numeric/color tolerances or substitute externally computed colors.

title: Release 0.0.19: complete approved chart authoring capabilities

title: Canvas rectangle starting corner uses open end caps instead of a closed join
body:
## Problem

The Canvas rect drawer returned to its first point with `lineTo()` but did not close the path. Its starting corner therefore used two end caps rather than the requested closed join, unlike SVG rectangles and native `strokeRect()`.

## Reproduction and correction

Paint a rect at (20,20), size40×40, yellow8px outline and red fill. Its first corner differs from native `strokeRect()`. Replace the final return segment with `closePath()`; preserve bounds, geometry, paints, stored graphics and zero-width behavior.

Evidence: `test/contracts/rect-outline.test.js` compares every pixel for miter/bevel/round joins crossed with butt/round/square caps. All nine cases and the existing renderer tests pass. The bar compositing tests additionally compare complete independent primitive output in Chromium Canvas, OffscreenCanvas and SVG across32 background/opacity/width combinations.

This existing-contract correction will be integrated with the new capability release; no API or snapshot schema change is needed.

title: Canvas zero-width strokes reuse a preceding positive line width
body:
## Problem

Canvas ignores `lineWidth = 0`. The rect, circle, path and line drawers still called `stroke()`, producing an unintended outline or line using a preceding positive width. Stored graphics correctly retained `strokeWidth: 0`; the error was in painting.

## Reproduction

Render a concrete line with width 8, then a red rect/circle/path outline or line with `strokeWidth: 0`. The second object paints red pixels where no stroke should exist. This also affects the zero-width outlines of gradient legend strips.

## Existing-contract correction

Skip only zero-width stroke painting after normal validation. Preserve fills, geometry, stored state, positive strokes and atomic preflight. Native Canvas, Chromium Canvas and Chromium SVG raster samples must agree exactly at independently selected interior/outline points.

Implementation: `d8d9e7e0`; release backport: `d39bd0d6`. Tests: `test/contracts/zero-stroke.test.js`, `test/browser/zero-stroke.browser.js`. This correction is included in PR #211.

title: Canvas none paint reuses a preceding opaque fill or stroke
body:
## Problem

The concrete paint keyword `none` is accepted and correctly produces no paint in SVG, but assigning it to Canvas `fillStyle` or `strokeStyle` is invalid. Canvas silently retains its preceding color, producing an unintended fill or outline. This affects circles, rect/path fills, strokes, text and Canvas backgrounds.

## Reproduction

```js
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 240, height: 180, margin: 40 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 1 }, { x: 2, y: 2 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false })
  .editPointMark({ fill: '#00ffff', stroke: 'none', strokeWidth: 8 })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 10 });
```

The pixel at `(28, 140)` should stay white. It is opaque black with source revision `690767d5`, despite `stroke: 'none'` in the concrete output. The correction produces `[255,255,255,255]` instead of `[0,0,0,255]`, with an unchanged `graphicSpec`.

## Correction and verification

Resolve the exact existing `none` sentinel through the shared Canvas paint owner as a valid transparent paint, preserving ordinary colors, geometry and opacity. Verify retained paint state, fill/stroke intersections, empty text/background, atomic preflight, native output and actual Chromium SVG/Canvas samples. No new public API or persisted schema is needed.

title: Support bounded summary outputs up to 30000 groups
body:
## Problem

`createSummaryData` rejects more than 10,000 distinct output groups even when import, typing, and grouping inputs are valid. Three complete 26,265-observation sources settle to 19,194, 10,968, and 25,909 mean groups. Each fails with `Summary output cannot exceed 10000 groups.` No rows were sampled, rewritten, or split to bypass the bound.

## Concrete proposal awaiting explicit approval

Raise only the summary output-group ceiling to **30,000 inclusive**; reject 30,001 atomically. Keep existing typed keys, grouping order, arithmetic, missing/empty policies, members, immutability, and all unrelated input, generated-item, work, and path bounds. Add no configurable bypass or public option.

Review package: [exact proposal and source evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/b670fa1d31d26a8150d53725b8ff5f9e074e33ee/agent_docs/impl/bounded-summary-output/PROPOSAL.md).

The executable public reproduction independently verifies current 10,000 success and 10,001/30,000/30,001 rejection, with unchanged caller input and immutable parent in every case. The package includes frozen source/browser/probe hashes and required boundary, replay, persistence, revision, aggregate, consumer, and compatibility tests for implementation after approval.

## Separate limits

Related #207 concerns generated scatter items and does not approve this summary change. The third source would still exceed the independent 20,000-command path ceiling with 25,909 vertices; this proposal leaves that hold intact. The first two remain within the path ceiling. Supporting larger summaries does not waive exact per-source mean-membership or rendered-output verification.

Status: reproduced and designed; **not implemented and not approved**. Only affected candidates are held. Original data, failures, and accounting remain preserved; independent translation work continues.

title: Support explicit opacity on legend symbol recipe layers
body:
## Problem

Categorical legend samples cannot explicitly use translucent paint. A point mark can have opacity `0.7`, while its merged color/stroke legend samples remain opaque. `LegendSymbolLayer` has no opacity property; public creation and whole/focused symbol edits reject it for line, point and swatch recipes. This is an explicit authoring gap, not a request to change automatic mark-alpha inference.

## Executable reproduction

The [review package](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/dc5ee512/agent_docs/impl/legend-symbol-layer-opacity/PROPOSAL.md) contains a two-row source-neutral [public reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/dc5ee512/agent_docs/impl/legend-symbol-layer-opacity/REPRODUCE.mjs) and [actual results](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/dc5ee512/agent_docs/impl/legend-symbol-layer-opacity/REPRODUCTION.json). It verifies two opaque samples and nine unsupported-option rejections across three recipe types and create/edit paths. No translation program or chart pixels are included.

## Proposed contract — pending approval

Add optional finite `[0,1]` `opacity` to the existing `LegendSymbolLayer` line/point/swatch members:

```js
program.createLegend({
  symbol: {layers: [{type: 'point', size: 5, opacity: 0.7}]}
});
```

Apply opacity once to the complete corresponding sampled glyph, including fill and stroke; keep labels/title and other recipe layers unchanged. Zero retains geometry/layout. Preserve default1 and every existing omitted-option output, including the current specialized area-gradient fallback. Do not introduce implicit global mark-opacity inheritance, alpha-color workarounds, new shorthand keys or new actions. Existing recipe replacement/reset semantics and target/channel selection remain unchanged.

The same existing recipe paths must support editing, persistence, Canvas/scale/data replay and supported facet promotion. Validate atomically; synchronize types/closed schema/docs/cards and verify concrete SVG/Canvas opacity, default parity and installed package consumers. The complete proposal specifies exact compatibility and required negative tests.

Related #191 covers gradient bodies (`gradient.opacity`), and #177 covers opacity-block selection; neither covers categorical symbol-layer paint.

**No implementation is included. Public API/schema approval is required before implementation.**

title: Support bounded scatter layers above the 10000 generated-point ceiling
body:
## Problem

Two valid, non-geographic Vega-Lite scatterplots cannot preserve all observations with the existing public scatter facade. The failure is the per-object generated graphics ceiling, rather than data import, numeric conversion, source validity, or the curve command ceiling.

At ggaction commit `690767d53415b93d22321c7915b0e2eddda24071`:

| Source | Original rows and point marks | Plot |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `vl_0802` (Europe, Olympic heights and weights) | 44,992 | 250 × 250 |
| `vl_0804` (America, Olympic heights and weights) | 20,707 | 250 × 250 |

Both immutable original sources render successfully in Vega-Lite. All raw rows and their string field types are preserved when imported into ggaction; existing computed numeric aliases are valid. The actual public `createScatterPlot({x, y, guides:false})` lifecycle fails when it materializes the points:

```text
createGraphics length must not exceed 10000.
code: resource-limit
operation: createGraphics
optionPath: createGraphics length
limit: 10000
actual: 44992  (or 20707)
```

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
const values = Array.from({length:10001}, (_, i) => ({x:i, y:i % 7}));
chart()
  .createData({values})
  .createScatterPlot({x:'x', y:'y', guides:false});
```

The array construction is only a standalone reproduction. It is not a proposed chart authoring idiom or a replacement for original source data.

## Required capability and constraints

Support an explicitly reviewed, bounded way to preserve the complete point dataset in these charts. Sampling, silently dropping observations, or dividing one source layer into artificial semantic layers to evade a resource guard would change the dataset meaning or authoring granularity and is unsuitable for this translation workflow.

This issue does **not** approve increasing the public limit, changing other resource limits, introducing a new API, or weakening resource checks. A design should retain predictable memory/work bounds and existing diagnostics, document scope, and test the exact boundary plus ordinary output compatibility. The separately approved per-path command limit in #192 does not address point-item materialization.

## Validation performed

- Current original source browser rendering: 44,992 and 20,707 settled symbol marks.
- Hash-verified frozen raw data, original row/field/type/order preservation, and numeric alias construction.
- Actual installed public native program execution reproduces both resource-limit diagnostics before rendering.
- No model requests, chart-pixel inspection, source modification, or delivered success claim.

The two candidates are held pending an appropriate public design; independent chart translation continues.

title: Support a shared in-plot facet legend wider than one narrow cell
Support one quantitative legend combining same-field color and point size
body:
## Missing capability

A point owner maps the same quantitative field to both color and area. The source has one numeric legend: each sample combines its mapped fill and mapped area, with one shared title and label list. The existing public API can render every point correctly, but selecting both legend channels creates two independent blocks. Selecting only color loses varying sample area; selecting only size loses the sample colors.

This is a confirmed missing public representation, not a request to change default spacing or hide a second block with dummy marks.

Verified on runtime `02661f6607e964cca7f158524e93ade5861a63a7` (unreleased). No model calls or chart-pixel inspection were needed.

## Reproduction with two observations

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 800, height: 600,
    margin: { left: 100, top: 100, right: 400, bottom: 100 } })
  .createData({ values: [
    { x: 'A', y: 'Z', amount: 0 },
    { x: 'B', y: 'Z', amount: 300 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: { field: 'x', fieldType: 'nominal' },
    y: { field: 'y', fieldType: 'nominal' }, guides: false
  })
  .encodeColor({ field: 'amount', fieldType: 'quantitative' })
  .editColorScale({ domain: [0, 300], palette: 'blues' })
  .encodeSize({ field: 'amount',
    scale: { domain: [0, 300], range: [Math.PI, 361 * Math.PI / 4] } });

const result = p.createLegend({
  channels: ['color', 'size'],
  representation: 'symbols',
  values: [0, 100, 200, 300]
});
```

Actual stored legend kinds: `gradient` and `size`. There are two title/label lists. Color samples all have radius `7`; size samples all have fill `#94a3b8`. The independently measured expected combined samples pair each color-scale result with the corresponding size-scale radius in one circle.

Additional public routes were checked:

- Color-only sampled symbols support one fixed radius, so they cannot carry the area scale.
- Size-only samples retain the area scale but their fill override is scalar.
- `editLegendBlock({target:'scatterPlot',channel:'size',symbol:{fill:[...]}})` rejects: `symbol.fill must be a non-empty string`.
- `editLegendSymbols({symbol:{radius:[...]}})` rejects: `Sampled color symbol radius must be a positive finite number`.
- No per-item legend channel editor is exposed. Raw graphics, proxy mark owners and fabricated data are not appropriate substitutes.

## Independently checked affected sources

Two valid current translation candidates are held before paid generation:

| Source | Complete raw rows | Aggregated plotted rows | Actual source legend |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `vl_1364` | 27,780 | 129 | One color+size block, values 0/100/200/300 |
| `vl_1376` | 27,780 | 88 | One color+size block, values 0/50/100/150/200 |

Both use the same `sum(purchase count)` for quantitative color and size, with matching domain endpoints. Actual source samples have both different colors and different radii. Original specs, all raw rows, resolved/compiled inputs, actual SVGs and their hashes were independently checked. The raw files are unchanged; neither candidate is labeled successful or source-invalid.

## Concrete proposal — review required

A proposal-only isolated checkpoint is available:

- [Public contract and lifecycle proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/6d8236ec143fe2704464c5cbd7df785634113e1e/agent_docs/impl/joint-quantitative-legend/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable public reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/6d8236ec143fe2704464c5cbd7df785634113e1e/agent_docs/impl/joint-quantitative-legend/REPRODUCE.mjs)
- [Actual/expected sample properties and immutable-parent result](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/6d8236ec143fe2704464c5cbd7df785634113e1e/agent_docs/impl/joint-quantitative-legend/EVIDENCE.json)
- [Frozen source evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/6d8236ec143fe2704464c5cbd7df785634113e1e/agent_docs/impl/joint-quantitative-legend/SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json)

It proposes explicit opt-in `combine: 'color-size'` on existing `createLegend`/`editLegend`, default separate behavior unchanged. It requires one owner, one same-field/grain numeric sample policy, both scale mappings per glyph, occupied bounds, ordinary focused/block editing, removal, refresh, persistence and immutable failures. This is **not approved or implemented**; the proposal includes a review gate and required compatibility tests. The running runtime pin, package and deployed docs are unchanged.

The checked proposal reproduction passes and package-boundary contracts pass 6/6. No release, publication or implementation approval is implied.

## Related issues / deduplication

- #171 is related categorical ordinal size+shape fusion, with different sampling/domain semantics; it does not cover this continuous quantitative pair.
- #179 concerns sampled continuous-color legends alone; these now materialize, but their scalar radius does not encode size.
- #164 concerns sampled size display labels; the labels themselves are already reproducible here.
- #193 concerns independent block placement, not one shared semantic sample glyph.

title: Support explicit alignment of top legend titles within their content block
body:
## Problem

The existing legend APIs cannot left-align a title above a horizontal item row. This blocks preserving a valid static Vega-Lite layout (source `vl_0901`): at the unchanged plot-local anchor `{-49,359}`, the source legend title occupies approximately x5–79.55, while the native centered title occupies x145.72–215.28 and overlaps the X-axis title at x148.60–400.40. Moving the complete legend or changing the source font/plot would change the requested design.

Existing `at` moves the complete group, whole-legend `align` aligns that group, and `titlePosition:'left'` produces an inline title rather than a left-aligned title above the row. `titleStyle.align` is currently rejected. A separately diagnosed corner-to-free rematerialization inconsistency does not supply the missing alignment choice and is outside this proposal.

## Concrete proposal

Add optional `titleStyle.align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right'` to the existing shared legend title style and focused `editLegendTitle`, with an edit-only `'auto'` reset. Align within the measured intrinsic content block, preserve all omitted-option defaults and normal collision/Canvas checks, and apply consistently to supported top-title legend families. Explicit alignment conflicts with the distinct inline title layout.

The full reviewed design, five public API reproductions, exact source/native bounds, hashes, compatibility rules and required verification are committed here:

- [Proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/72637f47/agent_docs/impl/legend-title-alignment/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable public reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/72637f47/agent_docs/impl/legend-title-alignment/reproduce.mjs)
- [Source evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/72637f47/agent_docs/impl/legend-title-alignment/source-evidence.json)

This is separate from #193's sharing/promotion scope and #200's gradient direction/bottom-title scope. No implementation or public API change has been made; explicit design approval is pending. Only the dependent source is held, and all original attempts and actual model usage remain preserved.

title: Support difference compositing through the existing bar appearance API
body:
## Problem

Existing bars support gradient fills, rounded corners, stroke and opacity, but cannot request difference compositing. The motivating design aggregates all 1,461 observations into twelve monthly bars with gradients, rounded 10px corners and a 4px yellow outline. Difference depends on the actual white/gray grid backdrop; a fixed inverted palette changes the design.

## Concrete proposal

[Pushed review package: difference compositing for bars](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7ae85b09d4b76fe969ceb2ca43635873f5db92bf/agent_docs/impl/bar-difference-blend/PROPOSAL.md)

Add the closed values `normal` / `difference` to existing `editBarMark({ blend })`. Omission preserves current output. Record bar meaning and explicitly materialize a backend-neutral graphical compositing choice. SVG and Canvas must agree for gradients, alpha and fill/outline intersections without changing ordinary painter order. Other marks and other blend modes are outside scope.

The package includes a generic public reproduction, numeric diagnosis, an independent SVG target and immutable source evidence. Required tests cover default parity, alpha/backdrop behavior, rounded and clipped bars, facets, rematerialization, persistence, immutability, atomic rejection and an installed consumer.

Status: proposal only; awaiting explicit public-contract approval. No runtime implementation, package publication or deployment has occurred. Only the affected source is held while independent translation continues.

title: Expose fitted regression statistics for data-bound annotations without duplicate moment pipelines
body:
## Problem

A regression line plus an R² annotation currently requires a separate statistics pipeline. In vl_0976 and vl_0977, the public regression transform produces predictions, while the annotation separately computes x², y², xy, aggregates six moments, and evaluates the full R² expression. The raw rows and result are correct, but this duplicates regression statistics and expands action and nested-expression counts.

Verified against unreleased runtime c53d1edda3625376b75f3157f798a3b099e1a750: RegressionDataOptions/RegressionParameterOptions expose fitting and prediction options, with no documented coefficient/statistics dataset output. Existing createComputedData + createSummaryData remains a working workaround; this does not block translation.

## Suggested direction

Consider a documented, data-lineage-preserving way to expose fitted linear-regression coefficients and diagnostics (initially intercept, slope, sample count, and R²) for ordinary text annotations. Prefer reuse of the existing regression resource and explicit public data ownership over host-side computations or hardcoded statistics.

Keep prediction rows, raw datasets, missing-value policy, grouping, numerical conventions, persistence, and existing rendering behavior compatible. Specify degenerate-input behavior and whether each group emits one statistics row. A future design should clarify method-specific diagnostic availability.

## Evidence and validation expectations

The two sources each retain 12 raw observations. Independent moment and fitted-line proofs validate their calculations to floating-point precision. A proposed implementation should compare coefficient/R² outputs with independent calculations, test grouped and missing/degenerate cases, and preserve existing prediction/export results.

Status: non-blocking improvement request only. No API design approval, implementation, package publication, or measured token-savings claim is implied.

title: Inferred rotated Y-axis titles can paint outside Canvas at small and enlarged fonts
Support independent gradient legend direction and optional bottom titles
body:
## Problem

A continuous color ramp cannot currently be horizontal while its legend group remains at the right. Creation and editing reject `direction: 'horizontal'` for gradient legends. The visible affected reference has a150×150 plot and a horizontal120×16 strip at the right; changing the legend edge or replacing the ramp with samples changes the design.

A related authored layout places a gradient title below the strip. `titlePosition: 'bottom'` is also rejected. In the two retained reference snapshots for that related choice, CSS-variable title paint resolves to `none`; these sources are **not** presented as visible bottom-title blockers.

## Concrete review package

[Proposal and verification plan](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/f188cc83/agent_docs/impl/gradient-layout-direction-bottom-title/PROPOSAL.md)

The same directory contains `REPRODUCE.mjs`, actual `EVIDENCE.json`, and hash-bound `SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json`. The two-row public repro confirms both creation/editing rejections, records accepted legacy geometry and SVG export, and proves the prior program remains unchanged. No API implementation or chart pixels are included.

## Proposed decisions, separately reviewable

1. Extend the existing `direction` option to gradient legends independently of `position`. Omitted legacy direction remains position-derived; explicit direction persists across partial edits. Existing length/thickness, samples, bounds, group packing and native spacing retain their meanings.
2. Optionally allow gradient-only `titlePosition: 'bottom'`, using existing native title clearance and occupied bounds. Other legend families retain their current vocabulary. This related choice is not required merely because invisible reference title text has a bottom DOM anchor.

No new action, primitive rendering workaround or new gap option is proposed. The package specifies creation/whole/focused editing, group routing, transformed/reversed scales, immutability, collision validation, refresh, facets, persistence, types, metadata, SVG/Canvas and legacy parity tests.

**Status:** proposal only; explicit user approval is pending. The visible horizontal-right source remains held. Independent translations continue. Nothing has been published to the package registry or deployed.

title: Support along-axis offsets for semantic Cartesian axis titles
body:
## Problem

Two heatmap sources use an X-axis title at an authored horizontal position independent of their three string categories. The 375-pixel plot starts at X=104; the source title anchor is X=376.5. Current `at: "center"` gives X=291.5, while `at: 272.5` is correctly interpreted as a scale-domain value and rejected. `offset` moves perpendicular to the axis. Changing categories or replacing the axis title with an annotation would change its semantics.

This extends the existing semantic axis-title anchoring from #174; complete-axis outward offset (#194) and label text alignment (#195) address different geometry.

## Reviewable proposal

[Along-axis title proposal, public repro, source bounds and immutable-parent evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/47b9f80783bba9fe2a3de05178fc9af6ac8ed589/agent_docs/impl/axis-title-along-offset/PROPOSAL.md). Add signed finite `title.alongOffset` to existing Cartesian title options; omitted value is zero. Resolve existing `at` first, then translate X titles screen-right and Y titles screen-down for positive values, consistently across side and reversed scales. Keep perpendicular offset and rotation semantics.

Support complete-axis creation, whole-axis and focused-title editing, existing persistence/refresh/facets, and actual occupied bounds/collision checks. Invalid values reject atomically and legacy output remains identical. The concrete repro must reach X=376.5 using centered `at` plus 85 pixels without moving any chart cell or other guide.

**Status: proposal only; awaiting explicit user approval.** Only `vl_0263` and `vl_0264` are held. No implementation, publication or deployment is included.

title: Support finite floor in typed computed expressions
body:
## Problem

A source bins each of its 5,000 observations into fixed-width X/Y intervals while retaining one independently painted rectangle per observation. Existing bin-data actions aggregate observations; the closed computed grammar can divide and multiply but cannot round down. A public repro confirms `op: "floor"` is currently rejected.

The frozen source proof reproduces all 20,000 source interval endpoints exactly with `floor(x/5)*5` and `floor(y/1000)*1000`. Raw rows remain unchanged. Final rendered geometry and paint still require ordinary verification.

## Reviewable proposal

[Computed floor proposal and executable evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/b6392220/agent_docs/impl/computed-floor/PROPOSAL.md). Add only `{ op: "floor", operand }` to existing computed expressions; no new action or callback. Require a finite numeric operand, retain explicit `toNumber`, existing lazy missing-value handling and expression/work bounds, and follow `Math.floor` for negative fractions and signed zero. Preserve immutable data, atomic failures, existing persistence semantics and all previous operations.

Synchronize types, owning contract, official docs, action/API metadata and MCP validation. Test numeric boundaries, nested operations, invalid inputs, limits, lifecycle/consumers and the complete source interval proof.

**Status: proposal only; awaiting explicit user design approval.** Only `vl_0084` is held; independent translation continues. No runtime implementation or package publication is included.

title: Support named independent Cartesian axes on the same plot
body:
# Support two independent Cartesian axes on the same plot

Independent position scales already work, but a plot cannot keep both a left and a right Y-axis. Calling `createYAxis` a second time throws `createYAxisLine requires a missing y-axis line.` Removing the first axis before creating the second leaves only the right guide. This blocks five reviewed references; their original data, separate domains, typography and positions must survive.

## Reproduction

Run `node agent_docs/impl/independent-axis-guides/reproduce.mjs` at the pinned review revision. The synthetic three-row example uses only existing public mark/encoding/axis actions. Both marks and independent scales remain, the second guide fails atomically, and the prior immutable program stays unchanged. The structural evidence is saved alongside the script. No chart pixels were inspected.

## Proposed existing-action extension

- Add optional `id` to `createXAxis` / `createYAxis`, preserving legacy canonical x/y resources and output when omitted.
- Add optional axis-resource `target` to complete and focused axis editors/removers. Preserve canonical omitted-target behavior; require an explicit target when several named-only candidates exist. Never choose the first candidate.
- Allow `createAxes({y: [{id, scale, position, ...completeAxis}, ...]})` and the corresponding x-array, also through `createGuides.axes`. This declares complete axes together before focused edits, without adding top-level actions or requiring many options per action.
- Limit the initial scope to one axis per physical side and Cartesian coordinate: left+right Y and top+bottom X. Duplicate same-side axes fail; automatic displacement and arbitrary axis offsets are outside scope.

Use one axis-ID-keyed semantic guide map, preserving canonical x/y entries. Named entries record their channel; materialization configs and concrete component IDs follow that identity. Data, scale, coordinate, Canvas, theme, grid and legend consumer plans must retain every bound axis. Renderers continue reading only fully materialized graphics.

A concrete proposal, state/compatibility rules, affected-reference hashes and test matrix are in this review package. Required tests cover legacy exact parity, both orientations, complete/focused edits/removals, explicit/ambiguous selectors, atomic failure, persistence, rematerialization, bounds, SVG/Canvas/PNG/PDF and installed-package consumers.

**Proposal only; implementation awaits explicit user approval.** No public API or runtime code has changed.

title: Support positive-response exponential regression through existing regression APIs
body:
Existing regression APIs reject method: exp, and the closed computed-expression grammar has no exponential operator. The required positive-response model uses y-weighted least squares on log(y). Ordinary unweighted log-linear substitution changes the retained nine-row reference curve by up to23.66494431030233.

Proposed scope: add exp to the existing regression method union, with stable response-weighted fitting, strictly positive finite responses, existing prediction values/domain/steps, and finite-result checks. Initial support has no confidence/prediction bands; incompatible options reject atomically. Extend existing method metadata and persistence without introducing a diagnostics dataset or new action.

[Concrete proposal, generic public reproduction and full source evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/a544b85d10b140d4adb3fe980d29af68a01159da/agent_docs/impl/exponential-regression/PROPOSAL.md)

The source-bound proof preserves all nine raw observations and all60 sampled curve positions. Independent weighted fitting matches every source response with maximum error1.42e-14.

Status: proposal only; awaiting explicit public-API approval. Only vl_0638 is held. Runtime implementation, publication and deployment have not occurred.

title: Support explicit Cartesian axis label text alignment
body:
The existing Cartesian axis-label API always infers text anchoring from the axis side. A left-axis source requires nine variable-width labels sharing one left anchor; increasing offset alone produces a shared right edge instead. Complete-axis, whole-axis, and focused-label actions currently reject an explicit alignment.

Proposed change: add optional align: left | center | right to the existing Cartesian label style, interpreted in the unrotated local text frame. Omission preserves existing inference; edit omission preserves an explicit value. Explicit alignment takes precedence over inferred side/flush alignment. Keep full occupied-bounds collision and Canvas checks, immutable edits, persistence, themes, facets, and refresh behavior. No new action or primitive.

[Review proposal and executable reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/5f434ef868047fb4034d39e9aaa3bc6e8eb8cedf/agent_docs/impl/cartesian-axis-label-alignment/PROPOSAL.md)

Source evidence: vl_1390, 600×180 inner plot, nine actual SVG label left edges all 20.5 px, font size 10 and explicit padding 75. The reproduction includes immutable-parent, current rejection, synthetic anchor/bounds, and frozen source/data/SVG hash evidence.

Status: proposal only, awaiting explicit public-API approval. Only the dependent chart is held; other translations continue. Runtime implementation, publishing and deployment have not occurred.

title: Support outward offset of a complete Cartesian axis frame
body:
## Problem

A valid Vega-Lite source explicitly displaces its complete bottom X and left Y axes 20 logical pixels outside a 600×500 plot. Actual frozen SVG translations are `(0.5,520.5)` and `(-19.5,0.5)`. GGaction rejects `offset` in complete axis creation and whole-axis editing. Increasing label offsets leaves domain lines and ticks at the plot edge.

## Reviewed proposal

Add an optional finite non-negative outward `offset` to existing Cartesian complete-axis creation and whole-axis editors. Default zero preserves legacy behavior; omitted edit preserves prior intent. Move the domain line, ticks, labels and title together; retain local component offsets. Keep plot, marks, scales and grids fixed. Preserve strict occupied-bound collision checks, atomic failure, refresh, persistence and renderer parity. No new action or graphic primitive is requested.

[Proposal and executable reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/2662f06c6927de4bc86bf85c936e8d6357fbf2ec/agent_docs/impl/cartesian-axis-frame-offset/PROPOSAL.md)

The reproduction verifies current creation and both whole-editor rejections, incorrect label-only surrogate geometry and immutable parent state. Source/raw/compiled/SVG hashes bind the reference. No paid model requests or chart-image inspection were used. Issues #174 (title-only anchoring) and #183 (legend clearance) do not provide this capability.

Status: proposal only, awaiting explicit public-API approval before implementation. Only the affected translation is held; independent families continue.

title: Support independent placement of selected legend blocks on one mark owner
body:
A scatter owner with category color and quantitative size cannot retain two independently requested legend anchors. Creating the second corner block opts the first block into a single target group and moves it; an explicitly created group instead rejects the conflicting anchor. This affects source families0461 and0459.

## Executable reproduction

- [Review proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fa693ceb6c8f1494d97c26c94100a0b9393dcb9f/agent_docs/impl/independent-legend-block-placement/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Public two-row reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fa693ceb6c8f1494d97c26c94100a0b9393dcb9f/agent_docs/impl/independent-legend-block-placement/REPRODUCE.mjs)
- [Recorded actual geometry and immutable-parent checks](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fa693ceb6c8f1494d97c26c94100a0b9393dcb9f/agent_docs/impl/independent-legend-block-placement/REPRODUCTION.json)

Requested: color top-left, size bottom-left. Actual: both blocks effectively bottom-left; the first color block's occupied top changes158→429.2026916606628. Raw data, scales, layers, coordinates and mark graphics remain unchanged. No chart pixels or additional model calls were used.

## Proposed existing-action extension

Add optional position to editLegendBlock({target,channel,position}) with the current four edges/four corners and an explicit inherit reset. An independently placed block is excluded from inherited group packing and retains its anchor across whole-group edits until reset. A merged categorical block moves as one block. Preserve native clearance, occupied-bounds checks, immutable failure, persistence, rematerialization, facets/repeat and exact existing behavior when omitted. No custom coordinate/offset, hidden items, smaller fonts, internal action, or duplicate mark workaround.

This is separate from #178, which places a complete target group at one anchor. Status: confirmed missing capability; concrete public/persisted contract awaits explicit user approval. Implementation remains held only for the dependent families; other translation work continues.

title: Raise the bounded path command ceiling to 20000
body:
## Problem

An ordinary continuous line with 12,070 finite ordered observations fails with `Curve path command count must not exceed 10000.` The raw dataset is accepted, and every observation contributes to one continuous path. Removing observations or splitting disconnected layers would change its meaning.

A source-neutral public reproduction confirms 10,000 commands succeed; 10,001 and 12,070 reject atomically. Caller rows and the previous immutable program remain unchanged.

## Concrete proposal — approval pending

Raise only the per-path command ceiling to **20,000**, inclusive, consistently across concrete path validation/persistence, linear/curve builders and complete area paths. Count generated commands (including interpolation expansion and area closure), not rows. Keep unrelated generated-item and total-work bounds unchanged; reject 20,001 commands atomically.

No runtime implementation has been made. The root repository policy requires explicit approval for this material bounded-resource contract change. Other translation work continues.

- [English proposal and verification scope](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d2c1aa8a/agent_docs/impl/curve-command-limit/PROPOSAL.md)

title: Add explicit opacity for continuous legend ramps
body:
## Problem

Continuous color and stroke legends expose ramp dimensions but no public body-opacity control. A translucent point layer can therefore need a matching translucent ramp that cannot currently be authored through domain actions. This is an absent capability, not a claim that existing automatic mark-opacity inference is broken.

A generic two-observation public probe creates points with opacity0.7 and a continuous color legend. Every one of the60 gradient strips has effective opacity1. Attempting the existing `editLegendBlock({target:'scatterPlot',channel:'color',symbol:{opacity:0.7}})` correctly rejects a gradient because it is not a glyph recipe. Current documented gradient options are only `length` and `thickness`.

## Proposed contract (approval pending)

Add nested `gradient.opacity` to existing creation, whole-legend editing, and focused legend-symbol editing. Use finite `[0,1]`, default1 at creation, preserve on omitted edits. Apply it only to ramp strips, including their matching strip strokes; preserve opaque title/ticks/labels/border and all geometry. Support both fill-color and stroke-color gradients. Keep mark opacity independent and retain rejection of gradient `symbol` patches. Legacy saved programs without the field remain opacity1; invalid new values fail atomically.

```js
program.createLegend({channels:['color'],gradient:{length:200,thickness:12,opacity:0.7}});
program.editLegend({gradient:{opacity:0.4}});
```

## Review package and verification

[Exact English proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7eb1e877d761f388c6200978f1b02e4e1f57acd9/agent_docs/impl/legend-gradient-opacity/PROPOSAL.md)

[Executable current-behavior probe](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7eb1e877d761f388c6200978f1b02e4e1f57acd9/agent_docs/impl/legend-gradient-opacity/REPRODUCE.mjs), with its generated reproduction record in the same directory.

Probe and `git diff --check` pass. The proposal specifies required immutable editing, persistence, all-edge/facet/replay, SVG/Canvas, TypeScript, compatibility, and documentation checks after approval.

**Runtime implementation has not started.** This introduces a public option and persisted-schema decision, so the repository approval Gate remains open. Affected translation cases are held; no unsupported internal-graphics workaround, package publication, or docs deployment is requested.

title: Support literal string replacement in typed computed expressions
body:
## Problem

A typed computed-data chain cannot currently remove a literal suffix from raw string values. For example, raw `Change: "1.15%"` needs literal `%` removal, explicit numeric conversion, and division by100. Existing `toNumber` correctly rejects the original percent string, while the closed expression grammar has no literal string replacement. Rewriting the raw dataset externally would lose the public transformation provenance.

The affected source has1,988 immutable raw rows. Its explicit percent/range operation retains1,987 rows; eight retained `Volume: "#VALUE!"` values do not paint, so the settled chart contains1,979 points. Handling those missing numeric values is possible with existing typed conditionals and is separate from this proposal.

## Proposed narrow addition

Add one computed expression node:

```js
{op:'replaceLiteral', operand:{field:'Change'}, search:'%', replacement:''}
```

The operand evaluates to a string. Search and replacement are literal strings, search must be nonempty, and only the first exact case-sensitive occurrence is replaced. No regex, flags, callbacks, dynamic replacement expression, implicit coercion or general string utility suite is proposed. Dollar characters are literal, with no replacement-template expansion. A missing match returns the input unchanged; invalid types/keys fail atomically.

The node composes with existing `toNumber` and arithmetic inside `createComputedData({id,as,expression})`, retaining three top-level action options and immutable raw rows. Existing expression depth/node/work limits remain unchanged.

## Reproduction and review package

- [Concrete proposal and complete compatibility/test matrix](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d7f33b89/agent_docs/impl/computed-literal-replace/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable current rejection reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d7f33b89/agent_docs/impl/computed-literal-replace/reproduce.mjs)
- [Observed errors and immutability checks](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d7f33b89/agent_docs/impl/computed-literal-replace/rejection-evidence.json)
- [Actual source/raw/compiled/SVG hash-bound evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d7f33b89/agent_docs/impl/computed-literal-replace/source-evidence.json)

The synthetic public-chain reproduction passes: existing numeric conversion and the proposed unsupported node both reject, while the prior program and caller rows remain unchanged. No model calls or chart pixels were used for this reproduction.

Status: **proposal only; awaiting explicit public-contract approval**. No runtime/type/schema implementation, publication or deployment has occurred. Only the affected translation family is held; independent work continues.

title: Add explicit own-property nested scalar access to computed data
body:
## Problem

Datasets preserve nested JSON objects, but computed field references address literal top-level names. `{field:'venue.name'}` correctly treats that entire string as a field name and throws when only a nested `venue` record exists. There is no explicit nested scalar accessor among the current closed computed operations. Host-flattening raw input would discard the authored transformation and original nested dataset structure.

This blocks two real designs:150nested rows require scalar properties under `_source` (including a two-level `ml.species_prediction` property), and382event rows require `venue.name`/`venue.capacity`. In the second source39rows lack `venue`; these must remain missing rather than acquire invented capacity/category values.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
const base=chart().createData({values:[
  {venue:{name:'North',capacity:100}},
  {venue:{name:'South',capacity:200}},
  {}
]});
base.createComputedData({
  id:'names',as:'venueName',expression:{field:'venue.name'}
}); // Dataset "data" does not contain field "venue.name".
```

Confirmed at8700172097655fb229745f26161b56403fe03822. Executable reproduction also confirms the proposed operation is currently unsupported and failed calls leave raw rows/earlier programs unchanged.

## Proposed contract; approval pending

Add one closed computed operation:

```js
{op:'getPath',operand:{field:'venue'},path:['name']}
```

Use a literal root-field operand and1–8literal own-property keys, returning an existing scalar unchanged. Missing/null/undefined intermediates return null; known optional root fields work per row. Unknown roots, malformed paths, reserved prototype keys, accessors, non-record intermediates, arrays and nonscalar leaves fail atomically. Keep ordinary dotted field names literal. Track the root dependency and preserve the explicit path in immutable persisted computed transforms. No dataset flattening, arbitrary evaluation, dynamic paths, coercion or renderer API is proposed.

This is a proposal-only checkpoint; no runtime/public schema change has been implemented. Explicit design approval is required before implementation.

- [Complete public contract, missing/error choices and tests](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8fb5dfc0/agent_docs/impl/computed-nested-scalar/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8fb5dfc0/agent_docs/impl/computed-nested-scalar/reproduce.mjs)
- [Exact existing errors and immutable-state evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8fb5dfc0/agent_docs/impl/computed-nested-scalar/rejection-evidence.json)
- [Source path, absence and frozen-input hash evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/8fb5dfc0/agent_docs/impl/computed-nested-scalar/source-evidence.json)

title: Support existing structured FillPaint for area fills
body:
## Problem

Area fills currently accept only nonempty strings. Existing `FillPaint` already defines structured linear gradients for other filled marks, but passing the same valid paint to `createAreaPlot` or `editAreaMark` throws `Area fill must be a non-empty string.` This blocks a real area design with a white-to-orange vertical gradient at opacity0.7 and an independent orange line overlay. Flattening that fill to a solid color loses the intended design.

## Minimal public reproduction

```js
const paint = {
  type:'linear-gradient',
  from:{x:0,y:1}, to:{x:0,y:0},
  stops:[{offset:0,color:'white'},{offset:1,color:'#fc6721'}]
};
const base = chart()
  .createCanvas({width:240,height:160,margin:20})
  .createData({values:[{x:0,y:1},{x:1,y:3},{x:2,y:2}]})
  .createAreaPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false});
base.editAreaMark({fill:paint}); // TypeError
```

Confirmed at runtime commit8700172097655fb229745f26161b56403fe03822. Both constructor and editor rejection are tested; earlier immutable program state remains unchanged. No chart pixels were viewed; exact source paint,54source vertices(27area+27line), SVG paths and input hashes are retained.

## Concrete proposal; approval pending

Reuse the existing `FillPaint` union and validator for area `fill`, preserving default string fill/opacity and existing color-encoding precedence. Persist and materialize the complete backend-neutral paint; reuse renderer gradient consumers. Keep the line overlay a separate semantic line layer through existing public actions. Verify immutable caller inputs, constructor/editor parity, scale/data/resize/persistence, missing/grouped/ribbon paths, selection, encoding overrides, legend swatches and SVG/PNG/PDF/package consumers. Reject incompatible stroke-from-fill atomically rather than selecting one gradient stop.

This is a proposal-only checkpoint. No public runtime behavior has been changed and implementation is waiting for explicit design approval.

- [Exact rejection evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d27b372f/agent_docs/impl/area-fill-paint/rejection-evidence.json)
