title: Hard-line Cartesian axis titles use single-line bounds and can reject fitting labels
body:
## Problem

Cartesian axis titles accept a string, but explicit hard breaks were measured as a single line and were not materialized as concrete text lines. A valid two-line title could therefore be rejected as exceeding the Canvas, even when the actual two-line block fits. In other cases the title could paint at an incorrect position or reserve the wrong collision bounds.

This blocks source 0247, whose original Y-axis title has two authored lines. Flattening that title, dropping a line, shrinking its font, or expanding the frozen plot would change the reference design.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 320, height: 300, margin: 45 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 10, y: 10 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false });
p.createYAxisTitle({
  text: "A moderately long description\nA moderately long description",
  fontSize: 11,
  offset: 30
});
```

Expected: two centered lines with correct rotated block bounds, fitting the existing Canvas. Previous behavior: a falsely concatenated single-line estimate could reject the title; concrete text lacked its per-line geometry.

## Implemented fix

Runtime checkpoint [76d08a16](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/76d08a167f91cbefe4e9cf1268562c90bdba85cb), with clean documentation provenance [87001720](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/8700172097655fb229745f26161b56403fe03822).

- Reuse the existing shared text-line resolver and backend-neutral text `lines`; no new public API, schema option, or renderer inference.
- Materialize ordered LF/CRLF/CR lines, including blank lines, as a centered block with `fontSize * 1.2` spacing.
- Use the same full rotated bounds for Canvas and axis-label collision checks.
- Remove stale derived lines when editing back to a single line, retaining the graphic identity, order, and unchanged single-line behavior.
- Keep immutable action failure behavior and axis-title replay through Canvas/scale changes, facets, and persistence.

## Verification and current status

13 dedicated regressions cover all four axis orientations, explicit rotation, blank/CRLF/CR lines, SVG and Canvas output, creation/edit parity, resize, scale replay, facets, persistence, single-line convergence, and atomic overflow/collision rejection. Full unit 2,990/2,990, action contracts 532/532, documentation 120/120, and the installed package consumer pass. Packed full/basic/SVG consumers retain their existing byte limits.

This is an implemented branch checkpoint, not an npm release. Source 0247 remains held until the translation runtime/documentation pin is synchronized and its unchanged reviewed model program is rerendered with normal source/DOM/family checks. No chart pixels were inspected.

Related but distinct: #184 concerns legend-title hard breaks; #141 concerns ordinary text marks.

title: Empty categorical legend labelMap values create invalid text primitives
Blank lines in multiline chart titles produce invalid empty text primitives
body:
## Problem

A valid multiline chart title or subtitle containing a blank line can fail concrete graphic validation: the title materializer creates a text item with an empty string, while graphic text requires nonempty content. Affected translation sources include 0723 and 0370. Removing blank lines changes the authored line spacing and is not a faithful repair.

## Expected behavior

Keep the exact semantic title/subtitle string, line indices, line height and reserved layout. Omit only the empty line's painted text primitive. Nonblank lines retain their original positions and typography. Apply the same behavior to chart titles and facet children, all supported title edges, persistence and rendering.

## Implementation and evidence

Implemented on the working branch `fix/sampled-color-legend` in [7819b2f0](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/7819b2f0), with documentation provenance in [15f04d6d](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/15f04d6d). This restores existing documented multiline text behavior; no public API or schema addition.

Verification: 34 focused regressions, 2,974 unit tests, 532 action contracts, 120 documentation checks, and the installed-package SVG/PNG/persistence consumer all pass. Tests cover blank first/middle/last lines, line spacing/index preservation, all four edges, facets, nonblank output parity and atomic rejection of genuinely invalid values.

This is an implemented working-branch fix, not an npm release. Affected source families remain held until the translation runtime and frozen documentation are synchronized and verified.

title: Hard-line legend titles use single-line metrics and overlap following content
body:
## Problem

Legend titles containing hard line breaks were measured as one text line. The concrete title bounds and item starting position therefore did not match the rendered text, causing title/item overlap or incorrect placement. Examples include `MCC cutoff\nthreshold`, `Optimisation\nexit code`, and `Average Shots\nPer Match`.

Issue71 concerns rematerializing an independently wrapped chart title; this defect is within the legend title itself.

## Implemented correction

Runtime source checkpoint `cb11792966210688a6978c464755adfab0fb78a0`, clean integrated revision `e0a9659a018f95658f177ec85f0b7074b6f9fd78`:

- Resolve ordered hard lines and the matching measured width/height through shared text metrics.
- Materialize existing backend-neutral text `lines` for categorical and continuous legend titles.
- Position samples and labels after the full occupied title bounds; keep single-line output unchanged.
- Preserve create/edit, block edits, Canvas replay, persistence, SVG and Canvas behavior, including blank lines and atomic overflow rejection.

Validation:11legend families ×4edges;2,966unit tests,532contracts,120documentation checks and installed Basic/Full JS/TS/browser/PNG/PDF consumer passed.44single-line cases are graphic-byte-identical to the prior committed implementation. No new public action, rendering primitive or npm release is claimed.

title: Default horizontal legend offsets omit the occupied axis lane
body:
## Problem

An external top or bottom legend with omitted `offset` used only its native family offset, without first reserving the actual occupied axis lane on that edge. Axis labels or titles could overlap the legend or make an otherwise valid default placement fail. Creation order and later axis edits also needed to converge.

This differs from issues98/102: those cover collision validation and occupied-bound alignment for a requested offset. The defect here is the omitted-offset default relative to an existing axis.

## Implemented correction

Checkpoint `8853fdcc`, integrated revision `e0a9659a018f95658f177ec85f0b7074b6f9fd78`:

- For inferred external top/bottom placement, reserve the actual same-edge axis lane and then add the original family default: categorical8px or continuous30px.
- Explicit offsets, including0, retain their requested meaning.
- Free coordinates and inside/corner placement retain their existing anchors.
- Preserve the offset intent across edits, grouped legends, representation transitions, Canvas/axis changes and persistence. Older snapshots conservatively retain fixed placement.

84focused checks cover defaults/explicit offsets, axis/legend creation order, rotated/larger labels and titles, axis removal, sampled/mixed/grouped legends and persistence. Combined revision passed2,966unit tests,532contracts,120documentation checks and installed package tests. Source-specific explicit placement still takes precedence. Existing chart programs are under zero-model-call revalidation; no npm release is claimed.

title: Fixed-pixel temporal bars incorrectly inset the position scale range
body:
## Problem and reproduction

A temporal bar with an explicit fixed pixel width still inherited the inferred half-slot range inset used by band-width bars. This moved its centers away from the ordinary temporal mapping and also shifted shared guides and line/rule/text consumers.

Minimal public sequence: create a bar plot with a temporal positional field and an explicit date domain, set `encodeBarWidth({pixels: 4})`, then create the positional axis. With a plot from29 to374, one reproduced domain resolved to33.29504670756316..369.70495329243687 instead of29..374. All39 source bar positions differed by up to4.17px; the corrected positions agree within2.84e-14px.

## Implemented correction

Checkpoint `7d4f8ee642cf308f52cc39e074255307c2b5d42e`, integrated revision `e0a9659a018f95658f177ec85f0b7074b6f9fd78`:

- Preserve the full inferred range when every temporal bar consumer explicitly uses pixels.
- Preserve existing inset behavior for mixed or inferred band-width consumers.
- Explicit scale ranges continue to win.
- Width-mode edits refresh compatible shared line, rule, text and axis consumers atomically.

Existing issue144 covers ordinal lookup failure and issue35 covers consumer rejection; this issue records the separate fixed-width range calculation defect.

Regression evidence includes horizontal/vertical mapping, mixed consumers, explicit overrides, shared graphics, Canvas/scale edits and persistence. Combined revision passed2,966unit tests,532contracts,120docs checks and the installed package consumer. Existing accepted translation programs are being rerendered from unchanged reviewed bytes; no package release is claimed.

title: Support square-root quantitative color and stroke scales
body:
## Confirmed gap

The quantitative color API supports sequential/log/symlog but rejects an otherwise valid square-root color mapping. Position scales already support sqrt, so the current error misleadingly routes this request to the discretized-color family.

Verified at `9c32a273db0bb79191a5e2bb718148d3e7ab963f`, Node22.23.1:

```js
chart().createCanvas({width:300,height:260,margin:40})
 .createData({values:[{x:0,y:0,v:0},{x:1,y:1,v:25},{x:2,y:2,v:100}]})
 .createScatterPlot({x:"x",y:"y",guides:false})
 .encodeColor({field:"v",fieldType:"quantitative",scale:{type:"sqrt",domain:[0,100]}});
// Scale type "sqrt" is not valid for discretized-color.
```

## Concrete proposed scope, awaiting explicit approval

[Review proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e12cb0db7db0d84aea74be7e8bff62bcd249c750/agent_docs/impl/square-root-color/PROPOSAL.md) and [reproduction evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e12cb0db7db0d84aea74be7e8bff62bcd249c750/agent_docs/impl/square-root-color/REPRO.json).

Allow existing quantitative color/stroke encodings and focused scale editors to retain `type:"sqrt"`, with signed-square-root normalization over the original numeric domain. Values0/25/100 on domain0..100 map to normalized0/.5/1. Raw data remains unchanged. Existing gradients and sampled symbol legends must use the exact same scale, including edits/rematerialization/replay and composition consumers. No pow exponent, new interpolation space, new mark or new action is proposed.

Validation must cover positive/negative/cross-zero/reversed/clamped/degenerate domains, color and stroke consumers, both legend representations, immutable/atomic failures, Full/Basic and synchronized types/current contracts/docs. Existing sequential/log/symlog outputs must remain unchanged.

This currently blocks source family1604 in the new translation batch; only that family is held while independent sources proceed. No implementation, merge or package release is claimed. No chart pixels were viewed.

title: Prevent large vertical legend labels from overlapping at compact default spacing
body:
## Bug
Vertical legend items can overlap after reducing the default item pitch to 18px. The layout reserves only the nominal label fontSize. A 16px Helvetica Neue label in reference 1286 has an actual settled SVG text box height 18.34375px, so the 18px center pitch overlaps three neighboring pairs by 0.34375px. The point samples are not the cause.

This concerns the vertical side/corner minimum pitch, not the default text size or horizontal arrangement. No chart pixels were inspected; the evidence is actual SVG DOM bounding boxes.

## Fix committed, runtime adoption pending
[Source checkpoint e9182b50](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/e9182b502aaa8a73c2ee48f8247cd994239b4435) reserves a conservative label line height of fontSize×1.2 when determining vertical item pitch. Painted symbol/stroke extent and explicit itemGap remain minimum constraints. Thus 16px text receives 19.2px pitch, while default 12px text still receives 18px. Horizontal row geometry remains unchanged. This is a deterministic reserve, not a claim to exactly measure every installed font.

The same rule applies to the custom vertical opacity sample layout. Source/docs are synchronized and pushed; final provenance checkpoint is d07c98e8866fa2f145847e8e2efca49369c9a4b3. Unit 2,899, contracts 531, docs 120 and packed consumer checks pass. Added regressions cover default/large labels, corners, explicit gap, thick samples, replay and unchanged horizontal geometry.

The translation runtime still uses the earlier pin while the approved sampled-color feature is completed. This issue remains open until integration and the actual reference 1286 render/DOM checks pass under the final runtime.

title: Support sampled symbol legends for continuous color scales
body:
## Problem
A continuous color scale can need discrete legend samples without changing the continuous scale used by marks. The current public API always selects a gradient for continuous color and rejects `values`, so this display cannot be authored through domain actions.

Reference 0392 has a settled continuous domain `[1,9]` and four circular entries labeled `2,4,6,8`. Actual SVG DOM confirms four circle symbols, no gradient strip, radius5, sampled fill and stroke. This is a display gap, not an ordinal scale or data conversion request.

## Reproduce
```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({width:600,height:400,margin:100})
  .createData({values:[{x:1,y:2,value:1},{x:2,y:1,value:9}]})
  .createPointMark({id:"points"})
  .encodeX({field:"x"}).encodeY({field:"y"})
  .encodeColor({field:"value",fieldType:"quantitative"});
p.createLegend({channels:["color"],values:[2,4,6,8]});
// Gradient legends do not support exact sample values.
```
The reproduction also checks that failure preserves the previous immutable program. Default creation still succeeds as a gradient. Verified against runtime `80bf03537d2f19eed02d3266f4dc4230c1c0fa12`.

## Proposed change — awaiting approval, not implemented
Add `representation: "symbols"` to existing createLegend/editLegend, preserving default gradient behavior. Reuse existing values/count sampling and continuous mark color mapping, single-point symbol recipe, item layout, target-owned legend groups, editors, persistence, and concrete renderers. Existing sequential/log/symlog color support remains the scope; no new scale type or stroke extension.

The complete API/state/default/transition/consumer/test review package is committed and pushed at:
[Proposal and exact public calls](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/cb61e5f24c3ebff52f632a9050af6a3128f92c80/agent_docs/impl/sampled-color-legend/PROPOSAL.md)
[Executable current-API reproduction](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/cb61e5f24c3ebff52f632a9050af6a3128f92c80/agent_docs/impl/sampled-color-legend/reproduce.mjs)
[DOM/source-hash evidence](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/cb61e5f24c3ebff52f632a9050af6a3128f92c80/agent_docs/impl/sampled-color-legend/evidence.json)

Independent review verified the current failure, unchanged previous program, SVG sample structure, and existing native mark mapper colors `#472d7b/#2c728e/#28ae80/#abdc32`. No chart pixels were inspected and no model request was needed for this diagnosis. Only this dependent translation is held; independent corrections continue.

## Acceptance
- Default gradient output remains unchanged; explicit symbols uses identical scale mapping as marks.
- Exact/automatic samples, editors, representation switching, group/corner/free placement, data/scale/Canvas changes, remove/recreate, composition and persistence work immutably.
- Types, contracts, public docs, generated references and package-consumer coverage stay synchronized.
- Reference 0392 is translated by the designated school model and every retained granularity stage passes render/DOM/equality checks before acceptance.

title: Support grouped legend placement and plot-relative anchors
body:
Categorical legends support plot corners, but the same existing position values are rejected for sampled size and opacity legends. A chart with independent color, size and opacity blocks consequently cannot place its complete legend group inside a corner. Top/bottom blocks also wrap or fail against the plot width even when the outer Canvas has enough room for the explicitly requested single row. There is no public plot-relative free anchor for an otherwise complete legend.

The current item `direction` and `columns` options arrange items inside one block; they do not express the arrangement of several blocks. These distinctions need to survive creation, focused edits, Canvas/data/scale changes, removal and recreation without altering samples or mark encodings.

## Reproduction and proposed contract

- [Self-contained review package](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/705aa19f1e310ca7d7e653957aac37bce8ed2c57/agent_docs/impl/legend-placement-restoration/PROPOSAL.md)
- [Executable existing-API probes](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/705aa19f1e310ca7d7e653957aac37bce8ed2c57/agent_docs/impl/legend-placement-restoration/reproduce.mjs)
- [Recorded geometry, immutable inputs and probe results](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/705aa19f1e310ca7d7e653957aac37bce8ed2c57/agent_docs/impl/legend-placement-restoration/evidence.json)

Proposed: extend the existing corner positions consistently and add optional `blockLayout: "row" | "column" | "wrap"` and `at: {x, y}` to the existing legend layout surface. The proposal defines complete occupied-group bounds, target selection, explicit group opt-in/inheritance, conflicts, fitting and compatibility. An external requested row may exceed plot width but must fit the Canvas; an in-plot group must fit the plot. No item hiding, font reduction, primitive graphics patch, silent wrapping or fallback placement is acceptable.

Status: confirmed capability gap; public API/persisted-state design is awaiting explicit user approval under the repository instructions. The review package is committed and pushed, but the proposed feature is not implemented. The independent vertical item-spacing correction is already implemented separately in 292adc07fe3c71b9c6be7ede344e300d46a5e318.

title: Focused legend text editors cannot select a coexisting opacity block on the same layer
Support clipping sampled legend symbols without changing encoded size
body:
## Problem

A sampled size legend cannot express a fixed-height window that clips each symbol while retaining its encoded circle size. This prevents faithful static translation of a valid Vega-Lite legend with `clipHeight: 30` and size range `[4, 5000]`.

The original SVG creates one `<clipPath><rect ... height="30"/></clipPath>` per legend item. Large circles are deliberately shown as sections. Drawing the complete circles, reducing their radius, or substituting a rectangle changes the design or size encoding.

## Minimal public API reproduction

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 300, margin: 50 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0, n: 0 }, { x: 1, y: 1, n: 100 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false })
  .encodeSize({ field: 'n', scale: { domain: [0, 100], range: [Math.PI, 1250 * Math.PI] } })
  .createLegend({ channels: ['size'], clipHeight: 30 });
```

Current runtime `0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd` rejects the final call with `Unknown createSizeLegend option "clipHeight".` The equivalent native area range preserves Vega circle diameters (the native area bridge is π/4). The largest circle is approximately 70.71 px high before stroke, so a 30 px clip is visibly significant.

## Current API boundary

`types/program.d.ts` and legend materialization expose sampled size values, point/line/rect symbol recipes, layout and borders. There is no public legend symbol clip/window setting. Internal rendering primitives should not be required to author this design. No library implementation or public API change is included in this report.

## Requested behavior / design considerations

Provide a documented way to clip each sampled legend symbol to a fixed vertical window, without changing its original scale-mapped radius, sample values, labels, paint, or mark geometry. A possible design is a focused symbol-window option on a legend/block, with clear semantics for:

- local clipping coordinates and vertical alignment;
- stroke clipping and item packing using visible bounds;
- categorical, size and opacity legend applicability;
- edits, removal, replay and SVG serialization.

Please keep default behavior unchanged. Tests should distinguish a clipped large circle from a smaller complete circle and verify that labels and neighboring symbols do not overlap.

title: Support the native arrow point symbol in the public point-shape vocabulary
body:
## Problem

Vega-Lite's built-in `arrow` point symbol has no corresponding public ggaction point shape. `editPointMark({shape: "arrow"})` throws `Unsupported point shape "arrow".` The public `PointShape` union omits it.

This is a native source symbol, rather than caller-defined SVG. The related wedge coverage gap is #170.

## Actual static source evidence

Source vl_1743 SHA-256 `08098bfea697086e27ae9950d1f996d13832c38c0ac3134105e67a07d95d5afc`, filtered to 1970 cars, contains 29 filled blue arrows at opacity0.6. Actual frozen SVG DOM gives this seven-vertex outline, translated per point:

```svg
M-0.391,2.739L0.391,2.739L0.391,-0.342L1.095,-0.342L0,-2.739L-1.095,-0.342L-0.391,-0.342Z
```

A triangle drops the shaft; a tick drops the filled head. Existing public polygon families have different vertex counts or topology, so area/rotation changes cannot preserve this shape. Arbitrary path drawing is outside the ordinary chart-authoring vocabulary.

## Neutral reproduction

After a two-field scatterplot:

```js
program.editPointMark({shape: "arrow"});
```

The installed public type/runtime reject it. No model calls or pixels are required for this probe.

## Suggested improvement

Consider adding a native arrow point shape with documented area normalization, anchor, orientation, SVG/Canvas rendering, categorical shape encodings, legends, and durable selection/replay behavior. Existing shape defaults should remain unchanged.

No API implementation or approval is assumed. The source remains valid; the current dataset retains its raw source, all attempts and model usage separately and uses an existing-API reserve.

title: Support semantic Cartesian axis titles inside or above the plot with explicit anchoring
body:
## Essential static first-render translation gap

Current public Cartesian axis-title actions cannot reproduce an axis title placed inside the plot, or a horizontal Y title above the plot with explicit source anchoring. This is a placement feature request, not permission to add a new API or to weaken layout validation.

### Small public API reproduction

```js
const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({width:500,height:400,margin:{left:60,top:40,right:40,bottom:60}})
  .createData({values:[{x:1,y:10},{x:2,y:20}]})
  .createBarPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false});
p.createXAxis({title:{text:'Source axis title',fontSize:11,offset:-30}});
```

Actual: `Axis title offset must be a non-negative finite number.` A Y title with offset -5 fails identically. `AxisTitleOptions` exposes at/rotation/nonnegative offset, but no independent signed titleX/titleY, alignment or baseline controls.

### Source-observed behavior

An ordinary 400×300 bar chart uses these explicit Vega-Lite options:

- X title `titleY:-30`, `titleAnchor:'end'`, `titleAlign:'right'`: title is inside the lower plot and right aligned.
- Y title `titleX:-5`, `titleY:-5`, `titleAngle:0`, `titleAlign:'left'`, `titleBaseline:'bottom'`: title runs horizontally above the plot.

Frozen source SVG measurements: plot starts (24,21), X title painted bounds x219.6875..424.5/y290.5..303.5; Y title x19.5..180.25/y4.5..17.5. Fonts are 11px bold sans-serif, color #676A86. These are visible first-render details with no interaction dependency.

### Requested design/review

Consider a documented semantic axis-title placement policy supporting signed inward/outward displacement and independent alignment/baseline, while retaining axis ownership, scale binding, layout diagnostics, persistence and focused title edits. A generic text annotation visually approximates the title but loses the axis ownership required by the high-to-low action dataset, so it is not accepted as a silent substitute.

### Verification expected

Source-neutral tests should cover inward X placement and horizontal above-plot Y placement, regular defaults unchanged, complete/focused action equivalence, render/export/persistence, and guide collision reporting. Until reviewed and implemented, affected source remains valid but excluded from the current translation batch; raw attempts and all token usage remain preserved.

Observed against runtime 0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd. No implementation or API approval is implied by this issue.

title: Support dashed legend borders in public legend creation and editing
body:
## Problem

The public legend border options cannot reproduce a visible dashed legend frame. `LegendBorderOptions` exposes only `color`, `lineWidth`, `padding`, and `background`; both `createLegend` and `editLegendBorder` reject dash properties.

This blocks a valid Vega-Lite chart whose initial static view contains three legend blocks with explicit lightgrey borders, width 5, and `strokeDash: [4, 2, 6, 1]`.

## Measured source evidence

Source vl_1720, SHA-256 `63385cf267afc060f27cfb3390987a56b1bfb9705f04054f55ea52a5510d5352`, frozen SVG SHA-256 `2a0ab80f345ff3a90ed7e71c84e9a0eae6137732de4c9545a20538132f9925f8`.

Actual SVG DOM contains three legend background paths with `stroke="lightgrey"`, `stroke-width="5"`, and `stroke-dasharray="4,2,6,1"`. Browser computed paint confirms `rgb(211, 211, 211)` and `4px, 2px, 6px, 1px`. This is a visible explicit border style, not a renderer artifact.

## Minimal existing API probe

After a simple categorical scatterplot with a color encoding:

```js
program.createLegend({
  border: { color: "lightgrey", lineWidth: 5, padding: 30,
    strokeDash: [4, 2, 6, 1] }
});
```

Result: `Unknown createLegend.border option "strokeDash".`

`editLegendBorder` rejects the same property; `dash` is also rejected. The installed public types confirm the property is unavailable. The point-symbol stroke style is separate from the legend frame and cannot reproduce the border.

## Proposed improvement

Consider adding a typed border dash option consistently to legend creation and editing. Specify odd-length dash normalization, validation, border occupied bounds, SVG/Canvas parity, and replay behavior. Existing default solid borders should remain unchanged.

No public API implementation or approval is assumed. The affected source remains valid; its translation and all model usage are preserved separately while an existing-API source is selected for the current dataset.

title: Support power transforms for continuous color scales and original-value legends
body:
## Problem

A source chart using a cubic power color scale cannot currently be expressed with the public continuous color scale options. Replacing `pow` with the default sequential mapping changes the point colors and the gradient legend's relationship to the original values.

The source is a scatter plot with quantitative color on `Acceleration`, domain `[8, 24.8]`, `type: "pow"`, `exponent: 3`, and yellow-to-red interpolation. The source chart is valid; this is a missing public color-scale capability.

## Reproduction

Tested on commit `0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd`:

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 300, height: 200, margin: 40 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { x: 1, y: 2, v: 8 },
    { x: 2, y: 3, v: 24.8 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false })
  .encodeColor({ field: "v", fieldType: "quantitative" })
  .editColorScale({ type: "pow", exponent: 3, domain: [8, 24.8] });
```

Actual: `Unknown editColorScale option "exponent".`

The public `NonPointContinuousColorScaleOptions` union currently lists `sequential`, `log`, and `symlog`, with no power exponent. This is not a documentation-only mismatch: the runtime rejects the option too.

## Expected capability

Please consider a documented public power transform for continuous color, including a positive exponent, with matching point paint and a legend expressed in the original data values. Keep the encoding and focused scale editor contracts consistent.

Useful validation would cover exponent 1 matching linear/sequential behavior; exponent 3 with a nonzero domain minimum; forward/reverse/clamp handling; original-value legend tick positions; and the existing interpolation behavior. Color interpolation differences are a separate concern from this missing transform.

## Why the translation is stopped

A manually cubed derived field can express the point transform, but it also changes the color domain and requires an inverse mapping for the legend's original-value labels and tick positions. We have not verified a complete public-API equivalent and will not accept an output that silently drops the power transform or misrepresents its legend.

No library API change is implemented or assumed approved by this report. The source, rejected attempts, and all token usage are preserved, and this chart will be replaced in the current successful-source batch while the capability remains pending.

title: Support a fused categorical legend for same-field ordinal size and shape encodings
body:
## Problem

A source chart encodes the **same categorical field** as ordinal size and shape. Vega-Lite renders one shared set of category labels whose symbols carry both the corresponding shape and size. ggaction can render the points correctly, but the current public legend planner splits this into separate shape and size blocks, duplicating the category labels and title.

The actual translation source has **two** legend blocks: `Origin` (color) and `Cylinders` (size + shape). The source explicitly describes the expected two sets of legend items. With the existing public actions the equivalent ggaction authoring produces three blocks.

This differs from closed #90, which addressed missing size content / wrong line symbol inference. Both channels are currently present; the missing capability is a *single shared categorical legend block* for two encodings of the same field.

## Source-neutral reproduction

Verified at `0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd`. No external data is needed:

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 1000, height: 1000, margin: 300 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { x: 1, y: 1, c: 'A', n: 4 },
    { x: 2, y: 2, c: 'B', n: 6 },
    { x: 3, y: 3, c: 'A', n: 8 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false })
  .encodeColor({ field: 'c' })
  .encodeSize({
    field: 'n', fieldType: 'ordinal',
    scale: { type: 'ordinal', domain: [4, 6, 8], range: [Math.PI, 182.5, 361] }
  })
  .encodeShape({
    field: 'n',
    scale: { type: 'ordinal', domain: [4, 6, 8],
      range: ['circle', 'square', 'triangle-up'] }
  });

const result = p
  .createLegend({ channels: ['color'], labels: { fontSize: 10 }, titleStyle: { fontSize: 11 } })
  .createLegend({ channels: ['size', 'shape'], labels: { fontSize: 10 }, titleStyle: { fontSize: 11 } });
```

Actual semantic legend owners / displayed titles:

- `color`: title `c`
- `series`: channels `['shape']`, title `n`
- `size`: title `n`

Expected: one `c` block and one `n` block, with three `n` samples combining the mapped circle/square/triangle and mapped areas.

Additional attempted public routes:

- `p.createLegend({ channels: ['color', 'size', 'shape'] })` rejects with `Combined legend channels must encode the same field.` That is reasonable for the independent color field, so this is not the requested solution.
- `p.createCategoricalLegend({ channels: ['size', 'shape'] })` rejects with `Legend channels must be a non-empty unique color/strokeDash/shape array.`

## Current implementation boundary

`src/actions/guides/legends/categorical/actions.js` deliberately strips `size` from the categorical step and appends `createSizeLegend`, including when the size scale is ordinal and shares the shape field. The categorical channel vocabulary excludes size. A constant symbol recipe cannot express each category's different mapped size, so replacing it with a single constant symbol loses source meaning.

The point geometry itself needs no new API: ordinal size accepts an explicit numeric area range while retaining the raw category values. The example areas include the existing documented equal-area conversion for a source circle; no source data or x/y geometry needs to change.

## Suggested design / acceptance criteria

Consider a supported way for ordinal size + shape (and potentially other same-field categorical encodings) to share one categorical legend owner. Prefer existing high-level `createLegend({ channels: ['size','shape'], ... })` semantics or an explicit, documented composition policy after design review.

- One title and one category-label list for a shared field and identical ordered domains.
- Each glyph carries its mapped shape and mapped size, with correct occupied sample bounds / label clearance.
- Independent color remains a separate block.
- Raw category values and ordering remain unchanged.
- A continuous size encoding of a different field retains its separate sampled legend.
- Full/Basic actions, legend editing/removal, Canvas/data/scale replay and serialization preserve the ownership.
- Existing default outputs and independent-channel selection retain their behavior unless explicitly covered by the new contract.

The affected valid source is held and is being replaced in the batch; all paid attempt history is preserved. No new public API has been implemented.

title: Support the built-in wedge point shape through the public mark and shape vocabulary
body:
## Problem

A valid static Vega-Lite chart uses the built-in `wedge` point shape. The current public ggaction shape vocabulary rejects it, so its first-render design cannot be reproduced through the supported mark/encoding actions.

This is a request for a named built-in shape, separate from the arbitrary, data-bound custom SVG path capability in closed #136. It does not request a custom renderer or SVG primitive escape hatch.

## Minimal public API reproduction

Verified against commit `0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd`:

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 200, height: 200, margin: 30 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 2, y: 3 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false })
  .editPointMark({ shape: 'wedge' });
```

Actual error: `Unsupported point shape "wedge".`

The exported `PointShape` union in `types/program.d.ts:1097` and the validated list in `src/grammar/pointShapes.js` include the four triangle directions and other symbols, but no wedge. Arbitrary SVG path strings also fail the named-shape validator, so there is no existing public equivalent.

## Actual source evidence

The translation corpus chart `vl_1744` is valid and produces 29 unfilled wedge symbols in its first render. The source filters the cars dataset to 1970; its visual encoding is simply Horsepower / Miles_per_Gallon, opacity .6, the default point size 30, and a blue 2px outline. The first actual Vega SVG symbol is:

```xml
<path transform="translate(108.33333333333333,71.42857142857142)"
  d="M0,-3.162L-0.685,1.581L0.685,1.581Z"
  stroke="#4c78a8" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.6"/>
```

This is a distinctly narrow triangle. Substituting `triangle-up` changes its aspect ratio and silhouette; changing x/y scales to disguise that would damage the data geometry. The displayed path is source evidence only, not a proposed chart implementation.

Source SHA-256: `ffbf786eeab7570fb21579cac6e99fbcc275ffab906d0c5b888e3cb24e9f83c8`.

## Suggested public design

Consider adding `wedge` to the named `PointShape` vocabulary and shape-scale range validation, available through existing `editPointMark` / `encodeShape` actions. No new action or option is needed. Its documented size convention should be explicit: ggaction uses equal-area size whereas Vega's nominal symbol size is not always the geometric area. The translation should therefore use the documented geometric area conversion, while the built-in shape preserves the wedge's aspect ratio.

Useful acceptance checks:

- Filled and unfilled constant wedge marks preserve the expected narrow silhouette and orientation.
- Wedge is valid in a data-bound shape range and categorical legend symbol.
- Radius / equal-area size changes preserve the documented sizing convention, with finite bounds.
- Existing scale/data edits, rematerialization, serialization and replay retain the shape.
- All existing named shapes and default output remain unchanged; unsupported arbitrary paths remain rejected.

No library implementation has been made. The affected family is held and will be replaced in this translation batch while the API design is reviewed. Its original data, attempts and token usage remain preserved.

title: Support an explicit gamma control for continuous cubehelix color interpolation
body:
## Problem

Valid Vega-Lite quantitative color scales can specify `interpolate: {type:"cubehelix-long", gamma:...}`. ggaction's closed public `ContinuousColorInterpolation` currently accepts only interpolation-name strings, with no gamma setting. Using the same two endpoints and interpolation name therefore cannot preserve the source's interior mark colors and connected gradient legend.

This is separate from the D65/D50 Lab/HCL convention question in #168.

## Actual frozen sources / DOM evidence

All four sources use the 406-row cars data, Acceleration color domain `[8,24.8]`, and explicit `["yellow","red"]` endpoints. The settled source SVG contains 392 valid visible point records; raw input is retained.

- vl_1591: `cubehelix-long`, gamma2.
- vl_1592: gamma10, 95 distinct settled source colors.
- vl_1588: gamma-0.1, 93 distinct settled source colors.
- vl_1589: gamma0, 83 distinct settled source colors.

Gamma0 and negative gamma do **not** reduce these sources to a constant mark color. Native gamma1 in vl_1596/vl_1597/vl_1590 remains supported and in scope.

The present public declaration is:

```ts
type ContinuousColorInterpolation =
  | "rgb" | "hsl" | "hsl-long" | "lab"
  | "hcl" | "hcl-long" | "cubehelix" | "cubehelix-long";
```

Passing the source interpolation object is not a valid existing API. Dense hand-authored color lookup tables would obscure the original continuous design and exceed this dataset's compact-authoring intent.

## Requested design decision

Please consider an explicit, typed gamma control for supported interpolation families, with documented valid range and interaction with clamp/reverse/midpoint. Specify whether zero/negative finite values are supported or intentionally rejected; Vega accepts them, but ggaction should make its own policy explicit.

Independent tests should compare interior values with the selected interpolation convention, preserve endpoint behavior, and verify identical point/stroke/gradient-legend colors. Invalid/nonfinite gamma and unsupported interpolation combinations need explicit atomic errors.

No new API or default change is implemented here. These valid sources are excluded from the current batch and replaced; original specs, model responses, failures and token usage remain preserved. This issue records the confirmed capability gap for later approved design work.

title: Define explicit Lab/HCL white-point interoperability with Vega/d3 D50
body:
## Problem

The current `interpolate: "lab" | "hcl" | "hcl-long"` public API does not specify its reference white point. ggaction uses D65 Lab, while Vega/d3-color uses chromatically adapted D50 Lab. Both conventions are mathematically meaningful; their identical-looking API names currently cannot express an explicit interoperability choice.

This prevents an exact native translation of a valid Vega-Lite chart using quantitative `Acceleration` color with domain `[8, 24.8]`, explicit range `["yellow", "red"]`, and interpolation `"hcl"`. Its point coordinates/data are correct, but the interior colors differ systematically. Expanding geometry or changing legend styling cannot fix this.

## Measured reproduction (no image pixels)

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 300, height: 200 })
  .createData({ values: [{x: 1, y: 1, v: 17.5}, {x: 2, y: 2, v: 20.5}] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false })
  .encodeColor({
    field: "v",
    fieldType: "quantitative",
    scale: {domain: [8, 24.8], range: ["yellow", "red"], interpolate: "hcl"}
  });
```

| Input | ggaction D65 | Vega/d3 D50 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | `#ffff00` | `rgb(255,255,0)` |
| 12 | `#ffd300` | `rgb(255,211,0)` |
| 17.5 | `#ff9100` | `rgb(255,147,0)` |
| 20.5 | `#ff6900` | `rgb(255,107,0)` |
| 24.8 | `#ff0000` | `rgb(255,0,0)` |

Neutral local calls to `mapSequentialColors` versus installed `d3-interpolate.interpolateHcl` reproduce these values. The valid 406-row cars source has a maximum two-unit RGB-channel difference; this is an interoperability limitation, not a claim that the charts look substantially different.

### Primary implementation evidence

- `src/grammar/scales/color.js`, `rgbToLab`/`labToRgb`: D65 white point `(0.95047, 1, 1.08883)` and associated sRGB matrices.
- `d3-color/src/lab.js`: D50 `(0.96422, 1, 0.82521)` with adapted matrices.
- `docs/api/scales/continuous-color.md`: enumerates interpolation names, without declaring white point or compatibility policy.
- Existing continuous-color tests check valid concrete colors/endpoints, without independent interior Lab/HCL color witnesses.

## Requested design decision (no implementation authorized here)

Please define the public convention explicitly. Options include an explicit opt-in D50/d3 interoperability mode while preserving the existing D65 default, or a versioned and documented D50 default migration with compatibility impact disclosed. The choice needs review; silently changing the existing default would alter accepted chart colors.

Focused tests should cover independent interior D50 and D65 witnesses, both HCL hue paths, achromatic endpoints, reversal/clamping/midpoint, point/stroke colors and gradient legend consistency. Existing RGB/HSL/cubehelix behavior should remain covered.

A dense color lookup/resampled range is not an appropriate minimal native solution: current sequential domain has two bounds and interpolates uniformly spaced stops, whereas source scalar values are irregular. Widening the global color oracle tolerance would hide the convention mismatch.

For now the affected source remains valid but is excluded from this translation batch and replaced; all source/model usage histories are retained. No ggaction API/default was changed.

title: Support exact calendar-year or substring extraction in computed data expressions
Support native dash styling for Cartesian ticks and per-value guide lines
body:
## Problem

Cartesian ticks cannot declare a dash pattern through the public API, and a directional grid has only one shared dash pattern. A valid source chart therefore cannot retain different solid/dashed ticks and grid lines at individual values without rebuilding guides using unrelated marks or rendering primitives.

Runtime inspected: `0951a880733b912cf7c190a5d6f134cc4ff7d4bd`.

## Concrete source behavior

A Vega-Lite temporal stock chart has eight quarterly X-axis ticks in 2006–2007. January ticks/grid lines are solid; the other quarters use `[2, 2]`. Its compiled Vega rules and frozen SVG confirm both patterns within the same axis and grid. This is static first-render styling; no interaction is involved.

The original source is valid and renders. Translation source identifier: `vl_1702`; SHA-256 `208d1ba5375dc31105c816b6cc656d91bb0c2299b3628fe1b35a34ebe6bb30f3`.

## Minimal public-API reproduction

Start with a normal line plot with `guides: false`, create a complete X axis with tick values `[0, 1, 2]`, and create its vertical grid. The desired appearance is a solid first tick/grid line and two dashed ones.

Current operations reject:

```js
program.editXAxisTicks({ strokeDash: [2, 2] });
// Unknown editXAxisTicks option "strokeDash".

program.editVerticalGrid({
  strokeDash: [
    { value: 0, dash: [] },
    { value: 1, dash: [2, 2] },
    { value: 2, dash: [2, 2] }
  ]
});
// Grid strokeDash must be an even-length array of non-negative finite numbers.

program.createVerticalGrid({ values: [0], strokeDash: [] });
// createVerticalGrid requires a missing grid.
```

All three operations leave the original program unchanged. A uniform `[2, 2]` grid works, but it removes the solid major lines. Recreating the same directional grid cannot supply a second style group.

## Possible API direction (proposal only)

1. Add ordinary uniform `strokeDash` support to Cartesian tick editors/complete-axis tick options, consistent with the existing grid vocabulary.
2. Consider a typed, finite value-to-paint map for ticks and directional grids, or another native way to group guide values by style. For example, a map could distinguish a numeric timestamp from the same timestamp written as a string and use `[]` for a solid line.
3. Keep guide ownership, public-action replay, rematerialization, scale edits and semantic round trips intact. Do not require internal graphics primitives or fake data marks to represent an axis.

The exact public schema needs design review; no API has been added for this report.

## Validation needed

- Uniform and per-value dash styles, including empty/odd-pattern semantics.
- Duplicate typed values, invalid/negative/non-finite dash entries and atomic rejection.
- Data/scale/Canvas edits and serialization/replay retain styles.
- Tick and grid lines remain native guides, with normal ordering and collision checks.
- Existing charts without this option remain unchanged.

## Translation handling

Only this affected source is paused and replaced in the current successful-chart target. Its raw source, model responses, failed attempts and token usage are retained. General guide-paint checks are not weakened. Negative Vega-Lite label padding is a separate issue: its net outward position can be expressed with the existing positive label offset and is not the blocker reported here.

Updates `playwright` from 1.62.1 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API
