title: Support bounded overflow summaries for categorical size legends
body:
## Problem

Categorical point-size legends cannot bound a large nominal domain with the public \`overflow\` option. The equivalent categorical color legend supports \`overflow: { maxItems, summary: "ellipsis-count" }\`, but a size-only legend currently rejects or ignores that option and materializes every ordinal-size sample.

This blocks static translation of Vega-Lite charts such as a scatter plot with \`size: { field: "GDP", type: "nominal" }\`. With 50 distinct values, Vega-Lite renders a bounded list ending in an ellipsis-count summary, while ggaction attempts to place all 50 size samples and fails with a Canvas overflow error.

## Reproduction

\`\`\`js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 630, height: 410 } })
  .createData({ values: rowsWithManyNominalSizes })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: "x",
    y: "y",
    size: { field: "category", fieldType: "nominal" },
    guides: false
  })
  .createLegend({
    channels: ["size"],
    overflow: { maxItems: 10, summary: "ellipsis-count" }
  });
\`\`\`

## Expected behavior

Ordinal size legends should apply the same deterministic domain truncation and \`…N entries\` summary used by categorical legends, while preserving the original size scale domain and encoded mark sizes. The feature should work at all supported legend positions and through legend edits/rematerialization.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`createLegend({ channels: ["size"], overflow: ... })\` accepts ordinal size scales.
- Only the configured number of domain entries is materialized, followed by an ellipsis-count summary item.
- The size scale domain and point encodings remain unchanged.
- Editing/rematerializing the legend preserves the overflow policy.
- Invalid overflow options fail atomically.
- Public types and legend documentation describe support and limitations.

title: Support independent corner radii for rect marks
body:
## Problem

Vega-Lite rect marks can apply different radii to individual corners. ggaction 0.0.17 exposes only one `cornerRadius`, so a static chart with two rounded diagonal corners and two square diagonal corners cannot be translated through the public rect APIs.

This blocked `vl_1750` in a Vega-Lite-to-ggaction translation batch. Replacing the authored shape with four rounded corners materially changes the repeated cell glyph, and manually drawing paths would bypass the mark API.

## Minimal source behavior

```json
{
  "width": 200,
  "height": 200,
  "data": {"url": "https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/data/cars.json"},
  "mark": {
    "type": "rect",
    "size": 30,
    "opacity": 0.6,
    "cornerRadius": 16,
    "cornerRadiusBottomLeft": 0,
    "cornerRadiusTopRight": 0
  },
  "encoding": {
    "x": {"field": "Origin", "type": "nominal"},
    "y": {"field": "Cylinders", "type": "ordinal"}
  }
}
```

The expected cell has rounded top-left and bottom-right corners, with square top-right and bottom-left corners.

## Current ggaction surface

The installed 0.0.17 documentation for `RectMarkOptions` and `RectStyleDetails` exposes one `cornerRadius` value applied to all corners. `createRectMark`, `createRectPlot`, and rect styling do not document per-corner alternatives.

A four-corner replacement can preserve neither the authored geometry nor the first-render appearance.

## Requested API

Support per-corner rect radii in the public rect mark/style options, for example:

```js
.createRectPlot({
  x: { field: "Origin", fieldType: "nominal" },
  y: { field: "Cylinders", fieldType: "ordinal" },
  rect: {
    cornerRadius: 16,
    cornerRadiusTopRight: 0,
    cornerRadiusBottomLeft: 0
  }
})
```

Equivalent names or a four-value corner object would also work. A global `cornerRadius` should remain the fallback, with per-corner values overriding only the specified corners.

## Acceptance criteria

- Public rect creation and rect style APIs accept independent top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left radii.
- Mixed radii render correctly for categorical rect cells and quantitative ranged rects.
- A global radius plus selected per-corner overrides resolves predictably.
- Negative values are rejected and oversized values are clamped or validated consistently with the existing global radius behavior.
- Faceted and composed rect charts preserve the same corner geometry.
- The minimal example above renders two rounded diagonal corners and two square diagonal corners without custom SVG paths or manual drawing.

title: Support in-plot categorical legends with bounded overflow summaries
body:
## Problem

A static Vega-Lite chart can intentionally place a large categorical legend inside the plot and let the renderer truncate overflowing entries with a summary sentinel. ggaction 0.0.17 only documents edge positions (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`) with `edge` or `legacy-bottom` layout, and requires the complete legend to fit the Canvas. There is no public option for an in-plot legend anchor or bounded categorical overflow.

This blocks a faithful static translation when the legend is the main visible content rather than an incidental guide.

## Source case

The blocked initial-state chart (`vl_1207`) has about 107 distinct quantitative values treated as nominal color categories. Its legend is a white block anchored at the plot's top-left. Vega-Lite shows the entries that fit and ends with an `…78 entries` sentinel. The encoded line groups generally contain one point each, so almost no paths are visible; moving or dropping the legend changes the chart's main first-render appearance.

Relevant Vega-Lite intent:

```json
{
  "mark": "line",
  "encoding": {
    "x": {"field": "date", "type": "temporal"},
    "y": {"field": "value", "type": "quantitative"},
    "color": {
      "field": "value",
      "type": "nominal",
      "legend": {
        "orient": "top-left",
        "fillColor": "white"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Current ggaction behavior

A categorical legend can be created on an edge:

```js
program.createLegend({
  channels: ["color"],
  position: "top",
  direction: "vertical",
  columns: 1,
  border: { fill: "white" }
});
```

This consumes top margin and must fully fit. For a large single-column legend, materialization fails with a Canvas-space error rather than providing a bounded overflow strategy. None of the installed public types or v0.0.17 legend docs expose an inside-plot anchor or truncation/sentinel option.

## Requested capability

Please add public, deterministic support for both:

1. Anchoring a categorical legend inside the plot, at least at `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, and `bottom-right`, with a documented offset/padding model.
2. Bounding categorical legend content by item count or available height/width, with a renderer-independent overflow policy that can show a summary item such as `…78 entries`.

One possible shape is illustrative only:

```js
program.createLegend({
  channels: ["color"],
  position: { space: "plot", anchor: "top-left" },
  overflow: { maxItems: 29, summary: "ellipsis-count" },
  border: { fill: "white" }
});
```

The resulting legend should remain a semantic legend resource, participate in edit/remove operations, preserve category order, and expose the hidden-item count in semantic/render traces.

## Why existing workarounds are insufficient

- Moving the legend to an outer edge changes the dominant layout and first-render appearance.
- Omitting or arbitrarily filtering categories changes the encoded category explanation and loses the overflow count.
- Rebuilding the legend from independent text/point marks loses legend semantics and uses many low-level actions.
- Enlarging the Canvas until all 107 entries fit does not match the authored bounded overlay behavior.

## Environment

- ggaction: 0.0.17
- Documentation snapshot commit: `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`
- Static initial-render translation; interaction is intentionally out of scope

title: Support independent dual y-axis guides on one Cartesian coordinate
body:
## Problem

Layered charts often need two independent quantitative y scales and two guides on one Cartesian coordinate: a left axis for daily values and a right axis for cumulative values. The translation case is `vl_1953`, which layers temporal range bars with a cumulative line.

The required guide topology is:

- shared temporal x axis
- left y axis bound to the daily/bar scale
- right y axis bound to the cumulative/line scale

## Current ggaction behavior

Marks can retain distinct y scale IDs, but the public axis API exposes one y-axis resource slot and no scale selector for a second guide. After creating the first y axis, attempting another `createYAxis` for the right side fails during execution with:

```text
createYAxisLine requires a missing y-axis line.
```

`editYAxis` cannot select a different scale or create a distinct guide resource. Omitting either axis loses essential quantitative context; manually drawing ticks and labels bypasses public guide semantics.

## Requested behavior

Allow multiple y-axis guide resources on one Cartesian coordinate, each bound to an explicit compatible y scale and position. One possible API direction is an axis `id` plus `scale` selector, while preserving the existing single-axis defaults.

```js
program
  .createYAxis({ id: "daily-axis", scale: "dailyY", position: "left" })
  .createYAxis({ id: "cumulative-axis", scale: "cumulativeY", position: "right" });
```

## Acceptance criteria

- Two y axes can coexist on the same Cartesian coordinate.
- Each axis selects a distinct y scale and can be placed left or right.
- Lines, ticks, labels, titles, and grids resolve without resource collisions.
- Focused edits/removal can target either axis by stable public identity.
- Existing single-y-axis code keeps its current defaults and behavior.
- Documentation includes an executable layered bar-plus-line example.

title: Support left and right headers for one-field column facets
body:
## Problem

A Vega-Lite column facet can explicitly place its field-dependent headers on the right side of each facet cell:

```json
{
  "facet": {
    "column": {
      "field": "category",
      "header": { "orient": "right" }
    }
  }
}
```

The translation case is `vl_1782`. It is a faceted bar chart with one column-facet field, shared quantitative scale, and an explicitly authored right-oriented facet header.

## Current ggaction behavior

A one-field facet creates a column header role. `editFacetHeaders({ role: "all", side: "right" })` fails because a side edit requires an explicit role. Using `role: "column", side: "right"` is also unsupported: column headers currently accept top or bottom, while right is reserved for row headers.

Moving the header to the top/bottom or omitting it changes an explicitly authored layout property. Drawing labels manually would bypass the facet-header API and lose field-dependent header behavior.

## Requested behavior

Support right/left placement for headers of a one-field column facet, with one field-derived header attached to each facet cell. A focused call could remain compatible with the existing editor shape, for example:

```js
program.editFacetHeaders({ role: "column", side: "right" });
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A one-field column facet can place headers on `right` and `left`.
- Header text remains derived from each facet value and stays attached to its cell.
- Layout reserves non-overlapping space and works with shared axes and zero/small facet padding.
- Existing top/bottom column headers and left/right row headers remain unchanged.
- Documentation includes an executable example and the role/side compatibility table.

title: Support scalable facets with more than 100 observed children
body:
## Problem

The public `facet` API in ggaction 0.0.17 has a fixed 100-child limit. A valid settled Vega-Lite first render in an 800-chart translation batch contains 106 observed facet values, so it cannot be represented as one semantic facet.

The source is a faceted area chart of 106 UK shopping-basket item categories. Each child has independent temporal x and quantitative y scales. The pinned Vega-Lite renderer accepts the source and produces all 106 panels in a 27,294px-wide first frame.

## Verified environment

- npm `ggaction@0.0.17`
- Node 22.23.1
- official documentation snapshot commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`

## Reproduction and investigated workaround

A direct `facet({ field, values })` with all 106 values exceeds the documented 100-child limit. We tried preserving all values by splitting them into a 100-child facet and a 6-child facet and combining those public programs with `hconcat`. Even after giving the large facet enough legend margin, the independently executed renderer fails with `Invalid string length` while materializing/serializing the resulting composed chart. The first attempt also failed with the same error; a reduced retry reached the categorical-legend layout check, then the complete split reproduction failed again.

Omitting six categories changes the data. Manually creating 106 copied child programs or arbitrary SVG paths would bypass the semantic facet API and produce even larger retained state, so we did not use those approaches.

## Requested capability

Support large observed facets beyond 100 children with bounded retained state and export cost, or expose a documented scalable paging/chunking composition that retains facet semantics.

Suggested acceptance test:

- 106 observed categories with roughly 300 rows per category;
- independent x/y scales and one shared categorical color legend;
- headers, gap, title, replay, edits, serialization, SVG/PNG export;
- a deterministic resource limit/error based on actual work or output size rather than a fixed 100-child semantic ceiling;
- a chunked public composition, if preferred, that renders the same 106 panels without duplicating the full source dataset into every retained child.

title: Support nominal point-size encodings and categorical size legends
body:
## Problem

Vega-Lite permits a nominal field on the point `size` channel. Each distinct category receives an ordinally assigned point area and the size legend labels the original category values. ggaction 0.0.17 exposes point size only as a quantitative channel, so this authored encoding cannot be preserved through the documented public API.

This blocks one chart in an 800-chart static translation batch. The source uses quantitative x/y, quantitative color, and `GDP` as a **nominal** point-size field. The same numeric-looking GDP values are deliberately categories for size and appear as category labels in the legend.

## Verified environment

- npm `ggaction@0.0.17`
- Node 22.23.1
- official documentation snapshot commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`

## Current public API boundary

`BasicSizeChannel` and `encodeSize` accept quantitative size fields and continuous/discretized quantitative scales. A categorical size field is rejected or must be converted to numeric ranks. Converting categories to ranks changes the authored field semantics, and the sampled quantitative size legend does not provide the categorical value-label mapping needed to restore the original GDP labels.

We did not silently omit the legend, coerce the nominal field to quantitative, or draw a manual legend.

## Requested capability

Support nominal/ordinal point-size encodings with an explicit categorical domain and graphical size/area range. The corresponding legend should retain each raw category label and symbol size.

Suggested tests:

- string categories mapped to three point areas and a categorical size legend;
- numeric-looking values treated as nominal keys, with their original labels retained;
- explicit domain/range ordering, missing values, edits, replay, serialization, facets, and export;
- coexistence with an independent continuous color legend.

title: Support proportional theta with field-driven radius on arc sectors
body:
## Problem

A Vega-Lite arc can map the same quantitative aggregate to both proportional angular sweep (`theta`) and an independent quantitative outer radius (`radius`). ggaction 0.0.17 cannot express that joint geometry through its documented public API.

This blocks two charts in a 600-chart static translation batch. Both aggregate values by category, use the value for proportional sector angles, and independently map the value through a square-root radial scale. Replacing this with `createPiePlot` preserves weighted angles but forces a common outer radius. Using categorical theta with `encodeR` preserves variable radius but forces equal angular bands. Either substitution changes essential geometry.

## Verified environment

- npm `ggaction@0.0.17`
- Node 22.23.1
- official documentation snapshot commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`

The two source cases require:

1. `theta = sum(value)`, `radius = sqrt(sum(value))` with radial range `[0, 80]`, inner radius 30, two categorical colors, and value labels.
2. `theta = sum(value)`, `radius = sqrt(sum(value))` with radial range `[20, 100]`, inner radius 40, two categorical colors, and value labels.

## Current public API boundary

The documented proportional arc/pie path accepts a quantitative value for angular sweep but uses one shared outer radius. The documented radius-bearing arc path uses categorical theta bands. Direct quantitative arc theta does not combine with `encodeR`; no documented public action accepts explicit per-sector start/end angles together with a field-driven outer radius.

We did not approximate with equal angles, a fixed radius, or arbitrary SVG paths.

## Requested capability

Support proportional quantitative theta and a quantitative radial encoding on the same arc sectors. The API should preserve:

- aggregate or pre-aggregated value input for theta;
- an independent radius field/scale, including square-root scales and explicit radial ranges;
- inner radius, stroke, pad angle, categorical color, and labels;
- stable replay, serialization, legends, and resizing.

Suggested tests: two unequal values should yield unequal angular sweeps and unequal outer radii; cover `[0, 80]` and nonzero `[20, 100]` radial ranges; verify inner radius, labels, color legend, edits, and export.

title: Support log and symlog transforms for continuous color scales
body:
## Problem

Quantitative position scales support transformed mappings, but quantitative color scales cannot express logarithmic or symmetric-logarithmic transforms. This blocks faithful translation of charts where the color transform and matching gradient legend are explicitly authored.

Two Vega-Lite cases from a static-chart translation batch require:

1. `type: "log"` for a positive quantitative color field.
2. `type: "symlog"` with `constant: 0.01` for a signed quantitative color field.

In ggaction 0.0.17, `NonPointContinuousColorScaleOptions` exposes only `type?: "sequential"`. `editColorScale` supports ordinal, sequential, quantize, quantile, and threshold, with no log/symlog transform or constant/base option. Substituting linear interpolation changes the visual encoding and legend positions materially.

## Desired public API

Allow transformed continuous color scales through the high-level color channel, for example:

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas()
  .createData({ values: rows })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: { field: "x" },
    y: { field: "y" },
    color: {
      field: "magnitude",
      scale: {
        type: "log",
        base: 10,
        range: ["#ffff00", "#ff0000"]
      }
    }
  });
```

and:

```js
color: {
  field: "signedChange",
  scale: {
    type: "symlog",
    constant: 0.01,
    range: ["#ffff00", "#ff0000"]
  }
}
```

The continuous gradient legend should use the same transform, including tick placement and value-to-color interpolation.

## Suggested acceptance tests

1. A positive domain maps through a base-10 log color scale and renders a matching gradient legend.
2. A signed domain maps through symlog with an explicit constant and renders zero plus symmetric small magnitudes correctly.
3. Editing the transform or constant rematerializes marks and the legend together.
4. Invalid log domains and nonpositive base/constant values produce clear validation errors.

This should remain available through the high-level scatter/point color option so the translation does not need manual color precomputation and a separately fabricated legend.

title: Support data-bound text annotation layers in faceted Cartesian charts
Support multiple columns in left and right categorical legends
Support independently identified left and right Cartesian axes
body:
## Problem

ggaction 0.0.17 cannot display two independently scaled y axes on the same Cartesian plot. Creating the right-side axis after the left-side axis fails even when the axes bind different scales.

This blocks static translations that need one shared x axis plus interpretable left and right measures. Two encountered examples are:

- Spending `[1, 2]` on the left and Caseload `[1.5, 3]` on the right.
- First-time buyers `[0, 500000]` on the left and FTB share `[0, 100]` on the right.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

export function buildChart() {
  return chart()
    .createCanvas({ width: 600, height: 400, margin: 80 })
    .createData({ values: [
      { x: 0, left: 1, right: 1.5 },
      { x: 1, left: 2, right: 3 }
    ] })
    .createLinePlot({
      x: { field: "x", scale: { id: "x" } },
      y: { field: "left", scale: { id: "left", domain: [1, 2] } },
      guides: { axes: { x: {}, y: { title: false } } }
    })
    .createLinePlot({
      id: "rightLine",
      x: { field: "x", scale: { id: "x" } },
      y: { field: "right", scale: { id: "right", domain: [1.5, 3] } },
      guides: false
    })
    .createYAxis({ scale: "right", position: "right", title: false });
}
```

Result:

```text
createYAxisLine requires a missing y-axis line.
```

## Cause observed in 0.0.17

- Cartesian axis graphic IDs are derived from the channel, so every y-axis line targets the same `yAxisLine` resource.
- Guide state has one `guide.axis.y` entry. `scale`, `position`, and `coordinate` select properties of that entry rather than identifying another axis.
- Moving or removing the first axis only replaces it. A second coordinate still writes the same global y-guide keys.
- `hconcat` and `vconcat` create adjacent charts and cannot overlay two independently guided series on one plot.

## Requested behavior

Support independently identified Cartesian axis instances bound to channel, scale, coordinate, and side. Existing default axis IDs can remain for compatibility.

Acceptance cases:

1. The reproduction renders shared x, left y `[1,2]`, and right y `[1.5,3]` simultaneously.
2. Each axis retains its own title, ticks, labels, color, position, and scale after guide edits or rematerialization.

Hand-drawing ticks and labels as marks can imitate the pixels, but it bypasses native guide semantics and makes guide editing and layout unreliable.

Tested with npm `ggaction@0.0.17` and source snapshot commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`.

title: Expose cardinal tension through public line options
body:
## Missing capability

Expose cardinal tension through public line options. `CurveInterpolation` currently accepts only a string, so an authored cardinal curve with tension0.9 cannot be represented. The current fixed curve is a valid default; this is an enhancement request, not a claim that it should silently match another library's defaults.

## Reproduction

Executed with ggaction0.0.17, Node22.23.1. Source snapshot: `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`.

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
import {renderToSVG} from 'ggaction/svg';
const values=[2,4,3,5,4,3,4].map((y,i)=>({x:i+1,y}));
const p=chart()
 .createCanvas({width:440,height:224,margin:0})
 .createData({values})
 .createLinePlot({
   x:{field:'x',scale:{domain:[.5,7.5],nice:false}},
   y:{field:'y',scale:{domain:[0,5],nice:false}},
   line:{curve:'cardinal',strokeWidth:2.7},guides:false
 });
console.log(renderToSVG(p));
```

Two public option probes both reject:

- `line:{curve:'cardinal',tension:.9}` → `Unknown createLinePlot line option "tension".`
- `line:{curve:{type:'cardinal',tension:.9}}` → `Unsupported curve interpolation "[object Object]".`

## Concrete effect

Compared the same seven points and440×224 plot with Vega-Lite5.23/Vega5.33 using `mark:{type:'line',interpolate:'cardinal',tension:.9,strokeWidth:2.7}` and identical scales. Both SVGs were rendered and their original pair, side-by-side, overlay and difference images inspected.

At the interior peak `(220,0)`, the outgoing control point is:

- requested tension0.9: approximately `(222.095,-0.747)`
- current ggaction cardinal: `(240.95238095,-7.46666667)`

The tangents differ by a factor of10. The current curve has visibly broader rounded peaks/valleys and greater overshoot. This is larger than text alignment or antialiasing variation. Image outer extents differ slightly from renderer stroke/autosizing, so the control-point comparison isolates the curve itself.

## API/implementation evidence

- [`CurveInterpolation`](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/types/program.d.ts#L89) is a string union.
- [`buildCardinalCommands`](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/grammar/curveCommands.js#L137) fixes control offsets to neighbor differences divided by6, without a configurable tension multiplier.

Consider a compact public tension option or structured curve specification, forwarded consistently through high-level line creation, lower-level line marks, edits and serialization. Preserve today's default behavior. Document supported tension range and endpoint tangent convention separately; the interior coefficient alone does not define cross-renderer endpoint parity.

Suggested validation: ordinary default regression, tensions0/.5/.9/1, two/three-point inputs, repeated points and groups, invalid parameters, edit/replay. At tension1, cardinal tangents should follow the documented limiting convention.

This blocks one static translation with explicitly authored tension0.9. We stopped that chart instead of replacing its curve, adding sampled synthetic observations, or embedding a custom path. Other charts continue. A separate bottom-legend fit error in its first full draft is not evidence for this capability gap; the successful minimal curve probe above isolates it.

title: Support opt-in robust residual reweighting for LOESS
Support sub-day UTC directives in public label formats
body:
## Request

Extend public UTC label formats to sub-day time components, especially `%H` (hour), `%M` (minute), `%S` (second), and `%L` (millisecond). Current time positions support millisecond timestamps, but axis labels cannot express these components through the public formatter.

Verified on npm ggaction0.0.17, Node22.23.1, official commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`.

## Executed reproduction

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
chart().createCanvas({width:600,height:400,margin:100})
 .createData({values:[{t:1960,p:1},{t:2021,p:2}]})
 .createLinePlot({
  x:{field:'t',fieldType:'temporal',temporalUnit:'timestamp'},
  y:{field:'p',aggregate:'mean'},
  guides:{axes:{
   x:{ticksAndLabels:{values:[1990,2020],
      labels:{format:'.%L',overlap:'allow'}}},
   y:false
  }}
 });
```

Actual: `Label format must be auto, { decimals }, or a supported format string (numeric or UTC).`

Independent control matrix:

- `%Y` succeeds.
- `.%L`, `%H:%M`, and `%d %b %H:%M` each reject with the same error.

The tiny epoch values are deliberate synthetic inputs to isolate millisecond formatting, not calendar years.

## Evidence and impact

[Runtime directive validation](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/grammar/valueFormat.js#L2) accepts Y/m/d/b and a literal percent. [Public types](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/types/program.d.ts#L1266) also enumerate only these date components.

In a static translation, two source ticks differ by milliseconds. A working public workaround suppresses automatic tick labels and creates explicit plot-space annotation labels. That adds repeated text/position/rotation options and requires recalculation if the domain changes. Another source uses hourly timestamps with `%d %b %H:%M`; date-only labels lose useful distinctions.

This is an additional format capability, separate from closed #37, which addressed combining already-supported date directives. Existing composite date formats need not change.

## Expected validation

Add explicit UTC semantics for these components in types, validation and rendering. Verify zero padding, literal percent, mixed date/time directives, midnight/year boundaries, millisecond values0/1/999, axes and other consumers of the shared formatter, and consistent browser/Node output. Reject unknown directives clearly. Keep existing date and numeric formatting behavior unchanged.

This is non-blocking where explicit static labels provide a valid public-API workaround; it would reduce both action count and configuration duplication.

title: Support explicit polar mark overflow beyond plot bounds
Support fontStyle in title and subtitle styles
body:
## Request

Support `fontStyle` in `createTitle` / `editTitle` title and subtitle styles, including public types, validation, SVG materialization and measured layout. This is a non-blocking fidelity improvement from static Vega-Lite translation: source subtitles use italic credits, and currently their text, font size, color and alignment can be preserved but italics cannot be expressed through the title API.

## Verified environment

npm `ggaction@0.0.17`, Node 22.23.1; official source commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76` (also GitHub main when checked on 2026-09-16).

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
chart()
  .createCanvas({ margin: 100 })
  .createTitle({
    text: 'Chart',
    subtitle: 'Data source',
    subtitleStyle: { fontSize: 10, fontStyle: 'italic' }
  });
```

Actual: `Unknown createTitle.subtitleStyle option "fontStyle".`

Control: removing only `fontStyle` succeeds. Both cases were executed on the pinned package. This is a request for additional supported styling, not a claim that the documented API already promises italics.

## Source evidence

- [TitleTextStyleOptions](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/types/program.d.ts#L4538) exposes color, fontSize, fontFamily and fontWeight.
- [Title style validation](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/actions/titles/resolve.js#L26) rejects fontStyle.
- [Title materialization](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/actions/titles/actions.js#L72) should carry the style through to the rendered text and layout measurements.

## Expected behavior and validation

- Permit at least `normal` and `italic` with clear validation and a normal default.
- Apply independently to the title and subtitle through creation and editing.
- Include font style in measurement/cache keys so wrapped italic text, alignment and margins remain correct.
- Retain semantic serialization and replay behavior.
- Test title-only, subtitle-only and mixed styles, plus edits and wrapping.

Related #143 concerns scoped typography and other authoring improvements; this issue isolates the concrete title-style restriction. We permit an upright subtitle as a recorded minor difference under our current approximate visual policy, so this does not block the translation batch.

title: Temporal ranged bars fail during ordinal position lookup
body:
## Problem

A ranged bar with temporal x and quantitative y/y2 fails at materialization with an ordinal-domain lookup error. This surfaced when translating candlestick bodies with real date spacing and a fixed five-pixel width. The same two rows work with ordinal x, but that changes the meaning of date gaps.

Verified on npm **ggaction 0.0.17**, Node 22.23.1 and Chromium. GitHub main on 2026-09-16 resolves to **e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76**, matching the pinned source.

## Minimal executable reproduction

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
chart().createCanvas().createData({values:[
  {date:'2009-06-01',open:28.7,close:30.04},
  {date:'2009-06-02',open:30.04,close:29.63}
]}).createBarMark()
 .encodeBarWidth({pixels:5})
 .encodeChannels({target:'bar',channels:{
   x:{field:'date',fieldType:'temporal'},
   y:{field:'open',scale:{zero:false}},
   y2:{field:'close'}
 }});
// Error: Value "2009-06-01" is outside the ordinal domain.
```

Executed a four-case control: temporal x fails whether width is assigned before or after positions; ordinal x succeeds in both orders. The failure also reproduces in browser rendering, before SVG output.

## Contract and root cause

- [Position contract](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/docs/reference/actions/encodings.md#L98) describes quantitative y plus ordinal/temporal x as vertical bars.
- [y2 contract](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/docs/reference/actions/encodings.md#L808) includes ranged bars.
- [Bar width contract](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/docs/reference/actions/encodings.md#L1477) permits fixed pixel width before or after ranged positions.
- [deriveRangedRectangles](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/materialization/bars/ranged.js#L26) maps the independent values through `mapOrdinalPositionValues` unconditionally. There is no branch for a temporal scale or its normalization.

The combined public contracts suggest this should be supported, but do not explicitly spell out every ranged-bar combination. If intentionally unsupported, document and validate the narrower restriction before an opaque ordinal lookup. The preferred behavior is temporal centers with fixed pixel widths.

## Expected behavior and regression checks

Preserve real date spacing, including weekends; render each bar from open to close and retain five-pixel width. Cover both orientations, ISO strings and normalized timestamps, width-before/after authoring, source rebinding, scale edits and resize. Leave categorical range bars unchanged.

A temporal Rule with y/y2, butt caps and strokeWidth 5 is a valid static workaround for these simple candlestick bodies; a separate one-pixel Rule renders the wick. Translation continues through that public API workaround. This is not an essential blocker for the sampled chart.

Related #139 requests a high-level raw interval bar facade, and #143 tracks quantitative centers. This issue concerns failure of the existing low-level temporal range path. Closed #35 concerned temporal-scale rule/text consumers, not this materializer.

title: Track remaining facade and scoped styling improvements from static-chart translation
body:
## Environment and scope

Verified with npm `ggaction@0.0.17`, Node 22.23.1. GitHub `main` resolved to `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76` on 2026-09-16, the same commit as our pinned official source snapshot. These are authoring improvements found while translating 50 static Vega-Lite charts (47 accepted); they are not new blockers for those accepted charts. We prioritize preserved meaning, visual fidelity, then fewer public actions and explicit options. Synthetic data below is independent of the dataset.

## Purpose

Track the smaller API design gaps found in accepted charts after removing avoidable calls with existing APIs. This is a scoped authoring backlog, not a request to bypass validation or wrap arbitrary low-level drawing. Proposed API spellings below are not implemented calls.

## Facade coverage

- [ ] **Quantitative bar centers with pixel width.** A histogram-like source can specify numeric centers plus constant 70px widths without asking ggaction to bin. `createBarPlot({x:'x',y:'y',width:{pixels:20},guides:false})` on numeric x/y currently throws `Bar y encoding requires a quantitative field opposite a categorical position.` Our accepted workaround creates a categorical key with calibrated padding and a transparent numeric point to own the numeric x-axis. Support raw numeric centers directly, preserving numeric distance and fixed pixel width.
- [ ] **Standalone scale/axis binding.** If a guide is intentionally tied to an explicit coordinate and scale, consider permitting it without an invisible mark. A scale definition alone is currently insufficient for a numeric axis (`Axis line requires scale amountX on x channel.`). This is related to the bar workaround above; document ownership/rematerialization explicitly.
- [ ] **Precomputed box summaries and pixel dimensions.** [BoxPlotOptions](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/types/program.d.ts#L2560) accepts raw-data statistical input and band width. Support explicit min/q1/median/q3/max summaries, pixel box/median widths, and whisker cap/style controls without re-estimating statistics. One translated summary is min3.07,q1=13.3475,median17.795,q3=24.1275,max50.81 with a capless black whisker, blue box and18px median tick. Existing `createErrorBar(caps:false)` already reduces its whisker chain; this request addresses the remaining composite, not a missing error-bar capability.
- [ ] **Scatter stroke channel.** [Scatter options](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76/src/actions/charts/scatter.js#L17) include color/size/shape but not field-driven stroke. Executed `createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',stroke:{field:'g'},guides:false})` → `Unknown createScatterPlot option "stroke".` Separate `encodeStroke` works. Add a matching facade channel with guide ownership and constant-vs-field conflict rules.

## Text and styling authoring

- [ ] **Data text facade.** One public action owning x/y/text plus style/guide intent would remove repeated position/content setup for text-only plots. `encodeChannels` already bundles encoding actions and `createMarkLabels` already handles attached labels; document and prefer those existing alternatives first.
- [ ] **Semantic plot-center annotation anchor.** A centered donut value currently needs `text`, `space:'plot'`, `x:.5`, `y:.5`, `align:'center'`, `baseline:'middle'`, plus authored fontSize/fill: eight explicit fields. A true center anchor should define position and alignment together, remain centered on resize, and distinguish plot from outer-canvas or source-mark center. Merely nesting the same fields does not reduce authoring complexity.
- [ ] **Scoped typography defaults and initial facet-header style.** `applyTheme` already supports fontFamily and color tokens; we verified it changes axes successfully. The remaining gaps are axis-only font size/family/color scope, separate label/title roles, and facet-header style during initial composition. Global tokens also change legend/title, requiring compensating overrides. Provide scoped defaults with clear precedence, and avoid claiming an entirely new theme system is needed. `facetGrid({scales:...})` already works and is not a missing feature.

## Validation direction

For each checked-off item, compare semantic spec and rendered geometry with a low-level reference, verify resize/facet/scale edits, and report actual authored action count plus top-level and nested option counts. High-level calls may reasonably exceed three options when total actions/settings decrease. Keep defaults explicit in metadata and avoid introducing hidden data transforms.

The numeric-bar and scatter rejection examples were executed on 0.0.17. The box/annotation/theme items are API/type and accepted-chart design evidence, not claims of a failing implementation for an already documented feature.

## Dedicated issues from the same review

- #137: Align action-card call patterns and facade metadata with executable API contracts
- #138: Preserve explicit inner plot dimensions while automatically allocating guide margins
- #139: Add raw lower/upper interval support to the high-level bar facade
- #140: Support field-driven text color and explicit source appearance inheritance for attached labels
- #141: Support multiline text marks with explicit line height and measured block alignment
- #142: Support ordered categorical positions directly in line charts

title: Support ordered categorical positions directly in line charts
body:
## Environment and scope

Verified with npm `ggaction@0.0.17`, Node 22.23.1. GitHub `main` resolved to `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76` on 2026-09-16, the same commit as our pinned official source snapshot. These are authoring improvements found while translating 50 static Vega-Lite charts (47 accepted); they are not new blockers for those accepted charts. We prioritize preserved meaning, visual fidelity, then fewer public actions and explicit options. Synthetic data below is independent of the dataset.

## Problem

Categorical point positions are supported, but a line cannot use the same categorical independent axis. Accepted translations currently encode ordered categories as numeric ranks with a second categorical point/axis layer, or expand a polyline into individual rule segments (99 segments in one chart). This adds derived data and scale coordination unrelated to the user's chart meaning.

## Executed reproduction

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
chart().createCanvas().createData({values:[
 {k:'first',y:2}, {k:'second',y:4}, {k:'third',y:3}
]}).createLinePlot({
 x:{field:'k',fieldType:'ordinal',scale:{domain:['first','second','third']}},
 y:'y',guides:false
});
// line x position does not support field type "ordinal".
```

An equivalent two-row ordinal probe was executed with the same error. The full three-row example retains the same unsupported channel contract.

## Proposal

Support line vertices at explicitly ordered band/point category positions. Define category ordering (explicit domain and inferred order), duplicate-category handling, series grouping and missing-category gaps. Reuse the categorical scale contract used by companion points so both layers align without numeric rank adapters.

## Acceptance checks

- Explicit nonalphabetical domain order is preserved.
- Multiple colored series share category centers; category gaps and missing values obey a documented connection policy.
- Facets, scale editing and Canvas/SVG rematerialization retain alignment.
- Existing quantitative/temporal line behavior stays unchanged.

Related: #134 requests ordered categorical **area** positions. This issue records the separate line capability and its action/data complexity; implementation may share the same path-position infrastructure. Geographic charts remain outside our scope.

body:
## Problem and impact

A static chart made from inline GeoJSON polygons cannot be represented with the public `ggaction@0.0.17` API. The translation target contains six postal-code polygons colored by category and a text layer positioned by longitude/latitude. Polygon topology, geographic projection, and label placement are essential to the chart, so replacing it with Cartesian rectangles or replaying the reference SVG would change the chart rather than translate it.

The installed documentation explicitly lists geographic projection among unsupported static capabilities. The installed `ChartProgram` types and action descriptors have no geoshape mark, geographic coordinate/projection action, or longitude/latitude encoding. A query through the installed ggaction MCP also returned `unsupported.geo` for this recipe.

## Environment and checked evidence

- `ggaction@0.0.17`
- Node.js `v22.23.1`, macOS
- Official documentation snapshot: tag `v0.0.17`, commit `e539c0b71be569dfc5d82f4180e8a08a8f580c76`
- Checked installed public declarations in `types/program.d.ts`, built-in action descriptors, action cards, and the official errors/recovery documentation
- Searched all existing issues for `geo`, `geoshape`, `GeoJSON`, `projection`, and `map`; no matching feature request was found

## Minimal target

The following synthetic data describes the minimum useful case. This is desired input data, not a currently executable API example:

```js
const rows = [
  {
    type: "Feature",
    properties: { region: "A", longitude: 0.5, latitude: 0.5 },
    geometry: {
      type: "Polygon",
      coordinates: [[[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1], [0, 0]]]
    }
  },
  {
    type: "Feature",
    properties: { region: "B", longitude: 1.5, latitude: 0.5 },
    geometry: {
      type: "Polygon",
      coordinates: [[[1, 0], [2, 0], [2, 1], [1, 1], [1, 0]]]
    }
  }
];
```

A public recipe should be able to:

1. render the two GeoJSON polygons with a documented projection,
2. encode polygon fill from `properties.region` and create a categorical legend, and
3. overlay `A` and `B` labels at the corresponding longitude/latitude fields.

There is currently no public action sequence to reduce to an executable failure because the required mark, coordinate, projection, and position encodings are absent from the API surface.

## Expected behavior

Provide a concise public path for GeoJSON `Feature`/`FeatureCollection` data, geoshape marks, a geographic projection, and longitude/latitude position encodings. The exact action names can follow ggaction's resource model; the requirement is that the complete static chart can be authored without arbitrary Canvas/SVG drawing.

## Suggested acceptance coverage

1. Polygon and MultiPolygon geometry, including holes and disconnected pieces.
2. A documented default projection plus explicit projection selection/configuration.
3. Deterministic fit/extent behavior and explicit Canvas sizing.
4. Categorical and quantitative fill scales with legends.
5. Point/text overlays positioned by longitude and latitude in the same projected coordinate system.
6. Missing/invalid geometry policy and antimeridian behavior.
7. SVG, Canvas, PNG, and PDF parity, with public types, action cards, inspection descriptors, examples, and documentation updated together.

This request concerns static first-render output only; interaction and map navigation are outside the requirement.

Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.7

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

hono/jsx renders plain strings unescaped in boundary components, leading to XSS

Affects: Suspense, ErrorBoundary, and Context.Provider in hono/jsx, and renderToString() / renderToReadableStream() in hono/jsx/dom/server. Fixes missing HTML escaping for a plain string placed directly as a child or fallback of these components, or as the root value of the server rendering functions, so untrusted strings could be emitted as markup. GHSA-hxh3-vqpv-xpqv

Users who render untrusted strings inside Suspense, ErrorBoundary, or Context.Provider, or pass them directly to hono/jsx/dom/server, are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

v4.13.6

What's Changed

  • fix(client): keep a param value of "index" in $url() and $path() in honojs/hono#5297
  • fix(client): normalize root WebSocket URLs in honojs/hono#5291
  • fix(types): allow symbol keys in Context get and set fallbacks in honojs/hono#5300
  • chore: bump editorconfig-checker in honojs/hono#5336

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.5...v4.13.6

v4.13.5

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Query parser reads parameters after the URL fragment, causing cache-key and proxy interpretation differentials

Affects: Cache Middleware and applications behind a proxy, WAF, or logging layer that inspects query strings. Fixes query parsing that did not stop at the URL fragment, so a ? after a # was treated as the start of a query string and the application could read parameters that the other component never saw. GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx

Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-39408: toSSG() still writes files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path normalization gap where consecutive parent-directory segments in ssgParams values were not fully collapsed, bypassing the containment check added in 4.12.12. GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv

Unbounded dot-notation nesting in parseBody() can cause memory exhaustion

Affects: parseBody() when dot-notation parsing is enabled. Fixes unbounded expansion of dot-separated field names, where a small request body could allocate a disproportionately large object graph and concurrent requests could exhaust the heap. GHSA-g6gw-c38x-mqfc

Users who use Cache Middleware, deploy behind a proxy or WAF that inspects query strings, use Static Site Generation, or use parseBody({ dot: true }) are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.
