[Bug]: Window operations silently omit an output field named __proto__
body:
## Summary

`createWindowData` accepts `as: "__proto__"` as a new field, records it in the transform, and returns success, but the derived rows have no such own field. The requested result disappears silently.

This is distinct from #69's resource-ID rejection: here a supported output-field name loses data during window calculation.

## Environment

Source `fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6`, package version 0.0.12, Node.js 22.23.1 on macOS arm64.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const p = chart()
  .createData({ values: [{ value: 10 }, { value: 20 }] })
  .createWindowData({
    id: "ranked",
    operations: [{ op: "rowNumber", as: "__proto__" }]
  });

const dataset = p.semanticSpec.datasets.at(-1);
console.log(dataset.transform[0].operations); // still specifies "__proto__"
console.log(dataset.values); // [{ value: 10 }, { value: 20 }]
console.log(Object.hasOwn(dataset.values[0], "__proto__")); // false
```

## Expected behavior

The derived rows should contain the requested own data field with values 1 and 2, consistent with the nonempty-string `FieldName` contract and sequential window operations. If a name is intentionally unsupported, it must be explicitly rejected before reporting success; silently omitting the output is incorrect.

## Additional verified cases

The same omission occurs with `cumulativeSum` and numeric `lag` using this output name. Control names `result`, `constructor`, and `toString` produce own fields correctly.

No global prototype mutation or exploit is claimed by this report; the reproduction only demonstrates dropped numeric output.

## Cause and regression coverage

[deriveWindowRows/applyOperation](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/src/grammar/window.js#L334) writes outputs with `entry.row[operation.as] = value` on ordinary objects. For `__proto__`, this reaches the inherited accessor rather than creating an own data property.

Cover all window operations with this supported field name, dependent operations that read the new output, preservation of source fields, JSON serialization, and immutability. Output construction must use own data-property semantics.

Filed during a repository audit at the maintainer's request. No source fix is included.

title: [Bug]: createTimeUnitData stores NaN buckets for valid timestamps near the Date lower bound
[Bug]: Top categorical legends crash on rematerialization when a chart title is wrapped
body:
## Summary

A valid chart with a top categorical legend and a wrapped bottom title renders initially, but editing the canvas or a scale throws a TypeError. The legend collision check assumes a title is a single text object with root properties; wrapped titles are text collections.

## Environment

Source `fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6`, package version 0.0.12, Node.js 22.23.1 on macOS arm64. Reproduced with public actions and SVG output.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
import { renderToSVG } from "ggaction/svg";

const before = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    width: 600, height: 500,
    margin: { top: 150, right: 40, bottom: 150, left: 50 }
  })
  .createData({
    values: [{ x: 1, y: 2, g: "A" }, { x: 2, y: 3, g: "B" }]
  })
  .createScatterPlot({
    id: "points", x: "x", y: "y", color: "g", guides: false
  })
  .createLegend({ target: "points", position: "top" })
  .createTitle({
    text: "A chart title with several words that wraps",
    position: "bottom", wrap: "word", maxWidth: 160
  });

renderToSVG(before); // succeeds
before.editCanvas({ width: 600 }); // throws, even at the same width
```

## Actual behavior

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'y')
    at resolveGridLayout (.../src/actions/guides/legends/categorical/layout.js:218:31)
```

The existing `cars-density-area / wrapped-title-bottom` visual fixture also fails on same-width canvas edit, resize-and-restore, and same-domain edits of x, y, or color. Its initial rendering tests pass.

## Expected behavior

The top legend and bottom title occupy separate margins and should remain editable. Layout checks must support all title graphic representations, including multiline collections, and use the actual occupied bounds/position.

## Cause

[resolveGridLayout](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/src/actions/guides/legends/categorical/layout.js#L215) selects `chartSubtitle ?? chartTitle`, checks only `type === "text"`, and then reads `titleGraphic.properties.y` and `fontSize`.

The wrapped title has `{ type: "text", items: [...] }` with no root `properties`. The collision logic also needs to distinguish a bottom title from a title occupying the top margin.

## Suggested regression coverage

- Wrapped title and wrapped subtitle, top/bottom positions.
- Both title-before-legend and legend-before-title authoring orders.
- Canvas and scale rematerialization after initial successful rendering.
- Real overlap should yield a layout error; separated margins should remain valid.
- Reuse the existing wrapped-title visual fixture for edit lifecycle checks.

Filed during a repository audit at the maintainer's request. No source fix is included.

title: [Bug]: MCP task resolver silently reverses negated requirements
body:
## Summary

The deterministic MCP resolver treats negated phrases as positive constraints. It recommends a legend, axes, color encoding, or regression specifically excluded by the query, while returning empty `unmatchedRequirements`, `unresolved`, and `unsupported` arrays.

This is an authoring correctness problem: clients are told there are no unresolved details even though the plan contradicts an explicit requirement.

## Environment

Source `fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6`, package version 0.0.12, Node.js 22.23.1 on macOS arm64.

## Minimal reproduction

From the repository root:

```js
import { searchGgaction } from "./knowledge/task-resolver.js";

for (const query of [
  "scatter plot with color encoding and no legend as svg",
  "scatter plot without axes and without grid as svg",
  "line chart without a regression line as svg",
  "scatter plot with no color encoding"
]) {
  const packet = searchGgaction(query);
  console.log(query, packet.exactCalls,
    packet.unmatchedRequirements, packet.unresolved);
}
```

The installed MCP route is the equivalent `search_ggaction({ query })`; the server uses the same deterministic packet.

## Actual behavior

| Excluded requirement | Returned plan |
| --- | --- |
| `no legend` | `createScatterPlot(... guides: { legend: {} })` |
| `without axes and without grid` | `createScatterPlot(... guides: {})`, which enables automatic guides |
| `without a regression line` | Adds `createPointMark({})` and `createRegression({})` |
| `no color encoding` | Adds `color: "category"` |

All four return empty unmatched/unresolved arrays.

A related extraction failure occurs for `"scatter plot with color encoding without a legend as svg"`: the resolver additionally records `color: "without"` as an applied field, with source text `"color encoding without"`.

## Expected behavior

Negation should not be converted into positive authoring intent. If this bounded parser cannot safely represent a negative requirement, it should preserve it as an unmatched/unresolved decision and avoid adding the excluded action. It need not become a general natural-language parser to behave conservatively.

Words introducing a restriction should not be confidently promoted to caller field names.

## Cause and regression scope

[semanticMatchResult](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/knowledge/task-resolver.js#L99) uses phrase occurrences without a negation scope. Requested-option extraction likewise treats the nearby word `without` as a field candidate.

The [documented workflow](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/docs/mcp.md#one-tool-workflow) asks clients to send the exact user request and uses unmatched/unresolved fields to surface details that could not be applied safely.

Suggested tests: positive/negative minimal pairs; `no`, `without`, and explicit exclusions around charts, guides, encodings, statistics, and renderers; mixed positive and negative clauses; field names that really contain those words; preservation of uncertainty rather than false closure.

Filed during a repository audit at the maintainer's request. No source fix is included.

title: [Bug]: Valid mark IDs such as constructor and toString are falsely reported as existing graphics
[Bug]: Canvas edits recreate invalid point graphics after removeEncoding emptied the incomplete mark
body:
## Summary

Removing a point's x/y encoding leaves an empty collection that renders successfully. A subsequent canvas edit recreates point items lacking the removed position, and rendering then throws. Canvas editing changes a valid intermediate chart into an unrenderable one.

## Environment

Source `fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6`, package version 0.0.12, Node.js 22.23.1 on macOS arm64. Reproduced with SVG serialization.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
import { renderToSVG } from "ggaction/svg";

const incomplete = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 400, height: 300, margin: 20 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 50, y: 50 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ id: "point", x: "x", y: "y", guides: false })
  .removeEncoding({ channel: "x" });

console.log(incomplete.graphicSpec.objects.point.items); // []
renderToSVG(incomplete); // succeeds

const edited = incomplete.editCanvas({ width: 400 });
console.log(edited.graphicSpec.objects.point.items);
// Items have y and fill, but lack x.
renderToSVG(edited); // throws
```

## Expected behavior

The incomplete mark should remain empty until a later encoding completes it. The [removeEncoding contract](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/agent_docs/contract/current/ENCODINGS.md#removeencoding) explicitly promises this behavior. Changing canvas dimensions, including assigning the same dimensions, should preserve the valid empty state.

## Actual behavior

Both x-removal and y-removal reproduce. The subsequent SVG error is:

```text
Graphic "point:0" requires a finite x property.
```

With y removed, the error instead requires finite y. Earlier immutable programs remain unchanged.

## Cause and regression scope

[planCanvasRematerialization](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/src/materialization/dependencies.js#L26) defers only complete marks. Resolving a surviving position scale can therefore invoke the [point materializer](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/src/actions/marks/point/materialize.js), which recreates partial row graphics for the incomplete layer.

Suggested coverage: remove x/y; render the empty state; resize/edit canvas or a remaining scale; render again; then reattach the missing encoding and verify recovery. Check empty collection preservation, not merely absence of the semantic channel. Include other row-owned mark policies where applicable.

Filed during a repository audit at the maintainer's request. No source fix is included.

title: [Bug]: encodeOpacity with a constant removes an unrelated layer's opacity legend
[Bug]: Removing or moving a scale consumer leaves the old automatic domain and remaining marks stale
[Bug]: Nested compositions exponentially expand graphic identifiers and snapshot size
body:
## Summary

Each nesting level re-encodes every existing graphic ID as six hexadecimal characters per input character. Consequently, a small composition with linearly increasing object count acquires exponentially increasing identifiers and serialized graphics.

This occurs through the supported public `hconcat` API without custom IDs or large datasets.

## Version and environment

- Source: `fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6` (main; package version 0.0.12)
- Node.js 22.23.1, macOS arm64
- Affects retained composition snapshots and downstream serialization; this report does not claim a renderer crash

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart, hconcat } from "ggaction";

const leaf = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 80, height: 80, margin: 5 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 1 }, { x: 2, y: 2 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false });

let program = leaf;
for (let depth = 0; depth <= 4; depth++) {
  if (depth > 0) {
    program = hconcat({ programs: [program, leaf], gap: 0 });
  }
  const ids = Object.keys(program.graphicSpec.objects);
  console.log({
    depth,
    objects: ids.length,
    longestIdentifier: Math.max(...ids.map(id => id.length)),
    graphicSpecBytes: Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(program.graphicSpec))
  });
}
```

## Actual results

| Nesting depth | Objects | Longest object ID | Serialized graphicSpec bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 3 | 11 | 415 |
| 1 | 7 | 176 | 3,441 |
| 2 | 11 | 1,166 | 20,498 |
| 3 | 15 | 7,106 | 121,735 |
| 4 | 19 | 42,746 | 728,052 |

Only four nesting operations and nineteen graphic objects already produce a 42,746-character object ID. This unnecessarily inflates immutable snapshots, keys, references, item IDs, and exports. Repeated composition can become expensive long before the actual chart content is large.

## Expected behavior

Namespaces must remain collision-free and deterministic, including for arbitrary supported child IDs. Their storage cost should grow in proportion to the original IDs and nesting information, rather than re-encoding the entire already-encoded prefix at every level.

Equivalent bounds should cover object keys, child references, order entries, and item IDs.

## Cause

[namespaceGraphicId](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/fc45c3d5f518c8acc1ce4555d6db0896e56899c6/src/materialization/compositionSnapshot.js#L32) applies this encoding to both the namespace and the entire previous ID:

```js
character.codePointAt(0).toString(16).padStart(6, "0")
```

Thus each nested call has approximately `L(next) = 6 * L(previous) + prefix`. Starting with `"canvas"` and repeatedly namespacing with `"view-1"` yields lengths `6, 74, 482, 2930, 17618, 105746`.

## Suggested regression coverage

- Keep a bounded public nested-composition fixture and assert a reasonable linear/polynomial identifier-size bound.
- Cover repeated child IDs, namespace delimiter characters, Unicode, item IDs, and nested retained editing.
- Preserve collision avoidance, graphic-tree validity, deterministic rendering, and child-reference rewriting.

The measurements above are deterministic lengths/byte counts, not a timing benchmark. The probe deliberately stops at depth four; no unbounded stress test was run.

Filed during a repository audit at the maintainer's request. No source fix is included.

title: Support quantitative x positions in createErrorBar

Support categorical offsets for point-and-whisker layers
body:
## Summary

A grouped point-and-whisker chart needs a categorical offset (dodge) within each ordinal x category. In ggaction 0.0.11, `encodeXOffset()` accepts bar marks only, so point estimates cannot share the offset layout with their error bars.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const rows = [
  { grammar: "ggaction", model: "0.5B", estimate: 0.66 },
  { grammar: "ggaction", model: "1.5B", estimate: 0.68 }
];

chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 320, height: 240 })
  .createData({ values: rows })
  .createPointMark({ id: "estimate" })
  .encodeX({ field: "grammar", fieldType: "ordinal" })
  .encodeY({ field: "estimate" })
  .encodeXOffset({ field: "model" });
```

Actual result:

```text
Error: bar mark requires an eligible layer.
```

## Expected behavior

- `encodeXOffset()` can target point marks on an ordinal x scale.
- An error-bar layer can reuse the same x and xOffset scales, so its rule and caps remain aligned with each dodged point.
- The explicit error-bar facade can express this grouped categorical position without synthesizing extra ordinal categories.

## Current workaround

For a 4-grammar x 3-model chart, I had to synthesize 12 ordinal slots plus spacer slots, draw the points and explicit intervals on those slots, and replace the four center tick labels after materialization. This produces the requested rendering but bypasses semantic category + offset structure.

## Environment

- ggaction: 0.0.11
- Node.js: 23.5.0
- macOS

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.12 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}

title: renderToPDF misplaces hconcat text when child margins differ
Time-axis labels reject composite format strings such as %b %Y
body:
ggaction version: 0.0.10

## Problem

Time-axis label formatting accepts individual supported tokens such as %Y, but rejects a composite format string such as %b %Y with:

    TypeError: Label format must be auto, { decimals }, or a supported format string.

This prevents a time axis from expressing a partial first year accurately as Jun 2023 while retaining explicit month and year context.

## Reproduction

Configure a temporal x-axis with explicit tick values and:

    labels: { format: "%b %Y" }

The error is raised by validateAxisFormat because it tests the complete string against TIME_FORMATS rather than parsing a sequence of supported temporal directives and literals.

## Expected

Composite temporal patterns should be accepted when every directive is supported, including common patterns such as %b %Y and %Y-%m.

## Workaround

Materialize the labels with %Y, then override the concrete xAxisLabels text array with editGraphics.

title: Temporal bar x-axis line exposes grid-colored end caps
body:
ggaction version: 0.0.10

## Problem

For a temporal bar plot with a horizontal grid and an explicit pixel bar width, the x-axis line uses the bar-inset resolved scale range while the horizontal grid uses the full plot bounds. At y = 0, the gridline therefore remains visible as light-colored end caps on both sides of the darker x-axis line.

## Reproduction

Create a temporal bar plot with:

- canvas plot bounds x = 88 through 684
- x scale range = [88, 684]
- bar width = 13.4 pixels
- horizontal grid color = #d9d9d9, width = 0.7
- x-axis line color = #333333, width = 0.8

The materialized SVG contains:

    grid at y=408: x1=88, x2=684
    xAxisLine at y=408: x1=94.534..., x2=677.466...

The 6.7-pixel difference on each side is exactly half the bar width.

## Expected

The visible x-axis baseline should cover the full plot bounds, or the baseline gridline should use matching geometry, so no differently colored end caps remain.

## Workaround

After guide materialization, overriding xAxisLine.x1 and xAxisLine.x2 with the plot bounds removes the artifact:

    program = program
      .editGraphics({ target: "xAxisLine", property: "x1", value: plotLeft })
      .editGraphics({ target: "xAxisLine", property: "x2", value: plotRight });

The behavior appears to come from the temporal bar scale resolved range being inset by half the bar bandwidth while the horizontal grid is generated from the full graphic bounds.

title: Temporal bar scales reject rule and text annotation consumers
body:
## Summary

A rule or text annotation cannot reuse the x time scale created by a temporal bar chart. This blocks a common vertical event-annotation pattern.

## Reproduction

- ggaction: 0.0.10
- Node.js: 23.5.0

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const rows = [
  { date: Date.UTC(2024, 0, 1), value: 10 },
  { date: Date.UTC(2024, 1, 1), value: 20 }
];

chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 400, height: 240 })
  .createData({ values: rows })
  .createBarPlot({
    x: { field: "date", fieldType: "temporal", scale: { id: "x" } },
    y: { field: "value" },
    guides: false
  })
  .createData({ id: "events", values: [{ date: Date.UTC(2024, 1, 1) }] })
  .createRuleMark({ id: "eventRule", data: "events" })
  .encodeX({
    target: "eventRule",
    field: "date",
    fieldType: "temporal",
    scale: { id: "x" }
  });
```

The final `encodeX` call throws:

```text
A temporal bar position scale requires compatible bar or line consumers of one field.
```

## Expected behavior

A temporal rule or text annotation using the same temporal field should be able to reuse the bar x scale and align with the corresponding bar center.

## Additional observation

Using a separate time scale with the same explicit domain and range does not exactly align the annotations. In a 720 px chart with 16 logical-pixel bars, the event lines differed from the corresponding bar centers by as much as about 6.6 logical pixels because temporal bar materialization applies an additional width-dependent range inset.

The current workaround is to read the completed bar geometry from `graphicSpec` and apply the materialized bar centers to the rule and text graphics with `editGraphics`. This produces correct output but leaves the semantic annotation scale misaligned.

title: Shared auto-scale domain expansion leaves existing mark geometry stale
body:
## Summary

Adding an error band that inherits an existing line's position encodings can expand the shared automatic scale domain without rematerializing the already-rendered line. The line and band then use the same resolved scale semantically, but their concrete Canvas coordinates were computed from different scale domains, so they do not align.

This is reproducible in published `ggaction@0.0.9` and current local `0.0.10` source.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    width: 600,
    height: 360,
    margin: { top: 52, right: 220, bottom: 58, left: 68 }
  })
  .createData({ id: "data", values: rows })
  .createLineMark({ id: "main-mark", data: "data" })
  .encodeX({
    target: "main-mark",
    field: "Year",
    fieldType: "temporal",
    scale: { id: "x-scale", type: "time" }
  })
  .encodeY({
    target: "main-mark",
    field: "Miles_per_Gallon",
    fieldType: "quantitative",
    scale: { id: "y-scale", type: "linear", zero: false },
    aggregate: "mean"
  })
  .createErrorBand({ target: "main-mark" });
```

Using the Cars data, the resolved Y domain changes from approximately:

```
before band: [17.1, 33.696551724137926]
after band:  [15.596788564787, 36.373657209101]
```

However, `graphicSpec.objects["main-mark"]` is byte-for-byte unchanged after `createErrorBand`. Calling this afterwards fixes the alignment:

```js
program.rematerializeLineMark({ id: "main-mark" });
```

## Expected behavior

When a new position consumer joins an existing automatic scale and changes its resolved domain, every already-materialized complete consumer of that scale should be rematerialized against the new domain.

The inherited error band and source line should align without an extra user action.

## Actual behavior

The new band is materialized with the expanded scale domain, while the existing line retains coordinates from the previous domain.

## Root cause

The position-encoding materialization path rematerializes the scale and the newly encoded target mark, but does not plan rematerialization for existing sibling marks consuming the same position scale. This leaves stale concrete geometry even though `semanticSpec` and `resolvedScales` are correct.

The issue is broader than error bands: any newly added position consumer that expands a shared automatic scale can leave earlier consumers stale.

## Suggested regression assertion

After adding an inherited error band:

1. the shared scale domain differs from the pre-band domain;
2. the source line graphic differs from its pre-band graphic;
3. the resulting line graphic equals a copy explicitly refreshed against the final scale domain.

A fix should live in the common position-scale consumer materialization plan, not as an error-band-specific rematerialization call.

title: Add extension authoring knowledge
body:
## What changed

- route agents through the installed extension runtime, declarations, action cards, and bounded task resolver before proposing new actions
- capture repeated authoring lessons from Roadmap, Gate, Attempt, and corrective history:
  - freeze the executable feature slice and action hierarchy before code
  - reuse actual public child actions and keep one canonical owner and resolver
  - preflight complete lifecycle changes atomically and prevent stale resources
  - compare primitive and public programs through semantic, graphic, order, renderer, and representative visual evidence
  - give LLMs complete executable prerequisites and distinguish terminal unsupported behavior from open decisions
- document the current upstream boundary, including the absence of a public extension registration mechanism
- require the guide in the bounded npm artifact and verify its structure and local links

## Why

Extension repositories need the tacit knowledge accumulated in ggaction development without copying the core repository `AGENTS.md` or consulting a mutable GitHub branch. Shipping the guide with ggaction keeps the knowledge aligned with the installed package version and turns recurring failure patterns into current, test-backed authoring rules.

## Impact

title: Reduce the browser bundle for a minimal chart

labels.name: packaging
labels.description: Package entries, artifacts, and consumer boundaries

labels.name: needs-design
labels.description: Requires a maintainer design decision before implementation

body:
## Problem

A browser project that follows the current Getting Started pattern and renders
a three-row scatterplot produces an unexpectedly large initial bundle.

### Reproduction

Environment:

- `ggaction@0.0.6` installed from npm
- Node.js 22.23.1
- npm 10.9.8
- Vite 6.4.3

The entry imports only `chart` and `render`, then calls `createCanvas`,
`createData`, and `createScatterPlot` for three inline rows.

```bash
npx vite build
```

Current result:

```text
dist/index.html                  0.37 kB │ gzip:   0.27 kB
dist/assets/index-CZ2HdANC.js  826.38 kB │ gzip: 212.91 kB

(!) Some chunks are larger than 500 kB after minification.
```

The production build completed in 645 ms. A separate minified esbuild bundle
was 785,046 bytes (202,692 bytes with gzip -9) and retained 373 input modules.

### Likely cause

`src/ChartProgram.js` calls `registerActions(ChartProgram)` at module
initialization. That registry imports and installs every action family on the
shared prototype, so bundlers cannot remove unrelated chart types, statistical
transforms, layouts, and guide implementations from a minimal consumer.

This is not an installation-speed failure: a cold-cache install of
`ggaction@0.0.6` completed in 2.64 seconds and installed three packages. The
concern is browser transfer, parse, and evaluation cost for simple charts.

## Desired outcome

- Add a reproducible browser bundle-size measurement for a minimal chart
  consumer.
- Establish and document an intentional bundle-size budget.
- Reduce the code required for a minimal browser chart, either through a
  tree-shakeable registration design, a supported lean entry point, or another
  backward-compatible approach.
- Keep the existing default API working, or document any deliberate
  compatibility tradeoff.
- Cover the chosen packaging boundary in the installed-package/browser test
  matrix.

The implementation approach and quantitative target need maintainer input; this
issue records the measured baseline so improvements can be evaluated
objectively.

Filed by an autonomous AI agent working for the ggaction project.
